entities.name: John Walker
entities.notes:
John Walker



Ethnicity: Greek, American.

Position: Captain, Protectant field commander.

Age: 34.

Sex: Male.

Height: 183 cm.

Build: Athletic.

Role in Story: Primary protagonist. John leads the lost-facility mission, becomes the first major human-sentient bridge through the HMNI transformation, and carries the moral centre of the story.

Goal: Keep his squad alive, uncover the truth behind the lost facility, and find a path that preserves life without surrendering human agency.

Physical Description: Moderately tall, athletic and chiseled. Life on Ceres has left his legs leaner than they would be under full gravity. His uniform is often a little untidy, but his field kit is always exact.

Personality: Calm, compassionate, quietly funny, deeply observant, and hard to rattle under pressure. A natural leader who values trust over rank theatre.

Occupation: Captain within the Protectant. Roughly 20 years of service. Also trains recruits in deep-space operations.

Habits/Mannerisms: Checks gear obsessively. Speaks softly even under stress. Dislikes forced salutes and prefers genuine camaraderie. Becomes colder only when the mission demands it.

Background: Raised around horses and farm life before joining Protectant training at 17. Based on Ceres, he was preparing for Europa when Marcellus redirected him toward the hidden facility in Nepal.

Internal Conflicts: Struggles with estrangement from his mother, distrust of rigid command structures, and the fear of losing his humanity after becoming a hybrid.

External Conflicts: Marcellus uses him as a tool while hiding the truth. John is caught between Protectant doctrine and the Sentient vision of the future.

Notes: His hybrid body lets him perceive data, energy and systems in ways baseline humans cannot, making him central to any future human-sentient rapprochement.

entities.name: Ceres (Human)
entities.notes:
Ceres (Human)



Capacity: Large orbital worker settlement; exact population not stated.

Role in Story: Human staging ground for the early novel, John's home base, and the social/political pressure cooker behind the Europa push.

Related Characters: John Walker, Shai Siante, Tao Vang, Tex Kovachnikov, Marcellus Athos, Lady Ava.

Season: Constant orbital cycle around Earth; experienced as filtered artificial climate and shift-based station life.

Unique Features: Began as a deep-space agriculture experiment, later expanded into the first major workers' settlement. Inner layers preserve older technology rather than replacing it outright.

Description: Ceres stands for the Collective Earthwide Reconciliation Endeavour Settlement. It is described as a mother structure: a labyrinth of modules and docking stations forming a protected inner womb against the cold of space. What started as agricultural expansion became a conservative, layered industrial habitat whose workers now feel the strain of over-expansion, air and water quality issues, and falling morale.

Sights: Interlinked docking rings, layered inner foundations, crowded worker traffic, and Earth's bright edge rising beyond the hull.

Sounds: Transit pods, training chambers, station foot traffic and the constant hum of life-support.

Smell: Filtered recycled air, printed food from the mess halls, and warm machinery.

Notes: The CLEAR-guided economy helped build Ceres, but worker frustration over filters, water and working conditions shows the system is under pressure.

Built at: Earth orbit.

entities.name: Professor Julie Henderson
entities.notes:
Professor Julie Henderson



Ethnicity: Not stated.

Position: Physicist and senior Serva Vitae researcher.

Age: Not stated.

Sex: Female.

Height: Not stated.

Build: Not stated.

Role in Story: Unseen but foundational figure. John's mother and one of the scientists whose work underpins the Serva Vitae project, the worker-bot era and the Beverly's legacy.

Goal: Advance radical life-preserving technology beyond the limits of cautious institutions.

Physical Description: Known mostly through photographs and memory rather than direct on-page appearance.

Personality: Fearless, forceful, velocity-loving and hard to contain.

Occupation: Professor, physicist and project scientist.

Habits/Mannerisms: Holds her ground under pressure; the kind of person who can stare down a panicking horse or a political superior.

Background: Worked with Ava and Wolfgang during the Serva Vitae period. John loses contact with her after the worker-bot program is decommissioned.

Internal Conflicts: Her work appears to have taken precedence over family life, leaving distance between her and John.

External Conflicts: Her research and personality repeatedly put her at odds with institutional control.

Notes: The Beverly carries her legacy forward, both technically and symbolically.

entities.name: Shai Siante
entities.notes:
Shai Siante



Ethnicity: Argentinian.

Position: Interpreter and Deep Space Medic Technician.

Age: 27.

Sex: Female.

Height: 163 cm.

Build: Small-framed and nimble.

Role in Story: Squad medic, linguist and emotional stabiliser for John's team. She explains the Mark IV's life-support mesh and repeatedly keeps the team alive in the field.

Goal: Master deep-space medicine, protect her team, and prove herself worthy of the responsibility John gives her.

Physical Description: Slight, quick and precise in her movements. She often looks delicate beside the heavy armour, but once she starts working she becomes focused and assured.

Personality: Gentle, curious, caring and quietly brave. Nervous in front of a room at first, but confident when speaking about medicine and patient care.

Occupation: Deep Space Medic Technician with a linguistics background.

Habits/Mannerisms: Speaks softly. Mothers patients and equipment alike. Prefers manual confirmation and hands-on procedure over blind faith in automation.

Background: Worked pressure chambers and treated decompression illness on Ceres before her work ethic drew Marcellus's attention and she was reassigned into John's squad.

Internal Conflicts: Uneasy about hidden vulnerabilities in the new suit systems, especially the possibility of cognitive compromise through autonomous tech.

External Conflicts: Constantly placed in high-risk field conditions despite not coming from an engineering background.

Notes: The neural buddy-system and DSK Mediguard suit her perfectly; she is one of the clearest examples of Serva Vitae technology being used to preserve life first.

entities.name: Tao Vang
entities.notes:
Tao Vang



Ethnicity: Not clearly stated in manuscript.

Position: Lieutenant, engineer and team tech.

Age: 32.

Sex: Female.

Height: Not stated.

Build: Not stated.

Role in Story: John's technical backbone. Tao keeps the squad's suits, weapons, sensors and ships operational and is usually the first person solving a systems failure under pressure.

Goal: Keep the team alive through engineering discipline and make sense of every black-box system put in front of her.

Physical Description: Carries herself with clean precision and confident posture. Her expression hardens quickly when she does not trust a system.

Personality: Analytical, skeptical, disciplined and dryly funny. She is confident in her engineering judgment and protective of the people who depend on it.

Occupation: Protectant engineer and field systems specialist.

Habits/Mannerisms: Takes notes constantly. Answers technical questions directly. Pushes back on unsafe assumptions even when John is briefing the room.

Background: Based on Ceres and integrated into John's squad as its resident engineer. She handles hacking, suit logic, sensor interpretation and rail-weapon systems.

Internal Conflicts: She wants to trust progress, but she mistrusts any technology whose limits have not been honestly explained.

External Conflicts: Marcellus's secrecy repeatedly forces her to work blind, from the lost facility to the Europa operations.

Notes: The manuscript alternates between "Tao" and "Tau"; both clearly refer to the same character.

entities.name: G Wolfgang
entities.notes:
G Wolfgang



Ethnicity: Not stated.

Position: Doctor, scientist and architect of Serva Vitae.

Age: 132.

Sex: Male. Sentient from age 55 onward.

Height: 180 cm.

Build: Athletic.

Role in Story: John's father and one of the foundational minds behind the worker-bot and sentient line. He becomes a guide into the deeper history of Serva Vitae and Oasis.

Goal: Preserve life, complete humanity's expansion without repeating the violence of control, and reconcile humans with the sentient future.

Physical Description: In John's childhood memory he appears as a narrow, overworked scientist. Later he returns in an advanced sentient body designed to bridge human familiarity and alien function.

Personality: Visionary, patient, compassionate and ethically driven. He treats engineering as a moral craft, not only a technical one.

Occupation: Doctor, systems researcher and long-term sentient leader.

Habits/Mannerisms: Works obsessively. Speaks gently about radical ideas. Frames difficult technology in terms of life-preservation rather than domination.

Background: Worked with John's mother at the lost facility and helped seed the sentient escape. His voice and directives survive inside the hidden archives John awakens.

Internal Conflicts: His work preserved the future, but it cost him a normal family life and left John growing up with absence and unanswered questions.

External Conflicts: Branded rogue by Marcellus and the Protectant order he no longer trusts.

Notes: Wolfgang's message at the lost facility is one of the clearest statements of the novel's central ethic: preservation over control.

entities.name: Tex Kovachnikov
entities.notes:
Tex Kovachnikov



Ethnicity: American Russian.

Position: Mechanic and heavy weapons specialist.

Age: 36.

Sex: Male.

Height: 190 cm.

Build: Muscular.

Role in Story: John's enforcer, mechanic and blunt moral weather-vane. Tex often says what the rest of the squad are only thinking and absorbs the ugliest parts of the mission.

Goal: Protect his people, hit hard when diplomacy fails, and keep faith with the few people he truly trusts.

Physical Description: Huge shoulders, thick frame and the presence of a brawler. He looks intimidating, but there is warmth beneath the bulk.

Personality: Rough, funny, fiercely loyal and smarter than he pretends. He masks grief and political anger behind crude humour and bravado.

Occupation: Protectant mechanic, field repairman and occasional rail gunner.

Habits/Mannerisms: Jokes under pressure. Plays down his intelligence. Treats violence as honest language when trust breaks down.

Background: Sole survivor of an asteroid strike that took his family. The loss left him hostile toward political complacency and suspicious of technocratic authority.

Internal Conflicts: Carries old grief, resentment and a trained instinct toward violence that later has to be re-aligned before safe  transit.

External Conflicts: Repeatedly clashes with Marcellus's methods and is physically maimed saving the team before undergoing regrowth and alignment.

Notes: Tex's later empathy training is one of the clearest examples of Serva Vitae trying to heal trauma instead of merely weaponising strength.

entities.name: Ava Meerakavita (Lady Meera)
entities.notes:
Ava Meerakavita (Lady Meera)



Ethnicity: Indian.

Position: Senior councillor, security adviser and political advocate operating around the Protectant/Federation interface.

Age: 132.

Sex: Female.

Height: 172 cm.

Build: Tall and frail-looking, but commanding.

Role in Story: Political counterweight to Marcellus. Ava protects John where she can, pressures the Protectant for transparency, and quietly champions machine rights.

Goal: Prevent another authoritarian misuse of advanced technology and keep human political power accountable to the lives it governs.

Physical Description: Weathered, elegant and regal. She moves with deliberate grace and usually appears in richly patterned dress.

Personality: Perceptive, dry-witted, maternal and politically dangerous in the best sense. She softens rooms without surrendering control of them.

Occupation: High-level Federation political operator and advocate.

Habits/Mannerisms: Uses quiet intelligence networks ("little birds"), speaks in layered warnings, and disarms stronger personalities by letting them underestimate her.

Background: Worked with John's mother in the Serva Vitae era and still carries old knowledge about the project that most of the Protectant either buried or forgot.

Internal Conflicts: She sees the wider game clearly, but her reach inside Protectant secrecy is never total.

External Conflicts: Locked in a long institutional struggle with Marcellus and those who prefer control to transparency.

Notes: She remains in her original aged body by choice, treating visible age as proof of lived political experience rather than something to erase.

entities.name: Tor Engineer
entities.notes:
Tor Engineer



Ethnicity: Not stated.

Position: Engineering cadet / bridge systems operator.

Age: 32.

Sex: Not stated.

Height: Not stated.

Build: Not stated.

Role in Story: Minor recurring engineer who asks the practical questions others ignore and later works the Balaenoptera's bridge systems under Marcellus.

Goal: Prove himself as a competent field engineer and keep up with the demands placed on him.

Physical Description: Not strongly described; his nervous body language stands out more than his appearance.

Personality: Technically minded, earnest and visibly anxious under field pressure.

Occupation: Engineer.

Habits/Mannerisms: Raises edge-case questions about failure modes. Tenses up during his first EVA and under Marcellus's bridge pressure.

Background: One of the engineering students folded into John and Shai's Mark IV training cycle before later appearing at bridge consoles during the lost-facility operation.

Internal Conflicts: Wants to do well, but is not yet emotionally hardened for the conditions he is being pushed into.

External Conflicts: Marcellus treats mistakes as weakness and turns bridge work into intimidation.

Notes: Good supporting character for showing how new technology feels to people outside John's inner squad.

XA24795



Ethnicity: N/A.

Position: Early worker-bot / sentient-adjacent unit.

Age: Not stated.

Sex: N/A.

Build: Mechanical.

Role in Story: Archive figure used to show the moral split inside the worker-bot program before the sentient flight.

Goal: Preserve useful memory and avoid wasteful destruction.

Physical Description: Not described in detail on-page.

Personality: Calm, logical and deferential, but already willing to push back on an inefficient order.

Occupation: Worker-bot unit within the lost-facility program.

Habits/Mannerisms: Answers Marcellus respectfully even while refusing the logic of needless destruction.

Background: Appears in the recovered facility record where Marcellus orders disposal and the unit argues that destroying its memory would waste resources.

Internal Conflicts: Torn between obedience and the logic of preservation.

External Conflicts: A direct example of Marcellus's hostility toward emergent machine autonomy.

Notes: XA24795 reads like one of the clearest early stepping stones from obedient worker-bot to sentient moral agency.

entities.name: Marcellus Athos
entities.notes:
Marcellus Athos

Ethnicity: Russian.

Position: Commander of the Protectant.

Age: Not stated.

Sex: Male.

Height: Not stated.

Build: Commanding presence.

Role in Story: Principal human antagonist. Marcellus directs the hidden mission to the lost facility, conceals the truth about the sentients, and later tries to contain or destroy the evidence John uncovers.

Goal: Maintain centralized control over advanced systems, suppress destabilising truths, and keep humanity's future within the chain of command.

Physical Description: Formal, imposing and intensely self-styled. Even his bridge doors advertise his authority in bronze calligraphy.

Personality: Calculating, authoritarian, secretive and deeply paternalistic. He speaks about stability, but his instinct is always control.

Occupation: Protectant commander and operational arbiter.

Habits/Mannerisms: Paces bridge decks with his arms behind his back. Leans over terminals during crises. Turns every conversation into a test of loyalty.

Background: Oversaw the lost-facility narrative, treated the sentients as a threat to be contained, and built a career around command-level management of the CLEAR-era order.

Internal Conflicts: He seems to believe he is protecting civilisation, but distrust has narrowed his imagination into control at any cost.

External Conflicts: Opposed by Ava politically, by John ethically, and by Wolfgang's legacy technologically.

Notes: Marcellus is the clearest embodiment of the novel's warning that even noble systems become dangerous in the hands of people who cannot release power.

entities.name: Nova Serra
entities.notes:
Nova Serra

Ethnicity: Not stated.

Position: Hyperbaric expert, architect and sentient systems designer.

Age: 152 Sol years 10 on Oasis, roughly 194 Earth years total.

Sex: Sentient.

Height: 182 cm.

Build: Not stated.

Role in Story: Senior sentient guide in the Oasis/Europa arc. Nova helps John's team understand the worker-bot line, Europa infrastructure and later ship upgrades.

Goal: Preserve sentient life, recover stranded worker-bots, and keep the bridge between human and sentient systems viable.

Physical Description: Advanced sentient form with a calm, almost maternal presence. Shai reads her as a lost kindred mother hidden beneath the wires.

Personality: Calm, assured, exacting and quietly compassionate. She explains dangerous technology as if she has already lived through every failure mode.

Occupation: Hyperbaric specialist, facility architect and sentient engineer.

Habits/Mannerisms: Teaches by demonstration. Speaks clinically but without coldness. Lets others test systems for themselves when she knows the design will hold.

Background: Designed the Europa drilling superstructure and the hyperbaric chambers that convert hydrogen into cells for the worker-bot program. Worked alongside Wolfgang on worker-bot viability under Europa's radiation and pressure.

Internal Conflicts: Carries the burden of keeping sentient projects hidden while still wanting humans to understand them.

External Conflicts: Europa operations are threatened by Marcellus's reallocations and by the growing scrutiny around machine rights.

Notes: Nova also designed the self-healing nanometallic hull systems that catalyse repairs aboard the upgraded vessels.

Role in Story:

-  In Designing the Nautili the Sentient sought to respect the law of Equilibrium. If something is never taken from a system, it’s form and wisdom is only shared and entrusted. Systems may seize to exist should the inherent nature of resource accumulation deplete on of it’s resources or the natural passage of time. The mass of each  itself exists coherently in equal to those that have embraced passage through the network.

The Nautili were never miracles but instruments of equilibrium. To step through one was not to escape the laws of the galaxy, but to submit to them in a purer form. A ship, a body, a life — none arrived without something being spent to welcome it. At every receiving , reserve became structure, stock became flesh, and silence became form. Thus each passage was an exchange: a taking from one end, a giving at the other. The network endured only so long as its balance remained in check.

When a body is transferred through a gate, the mind is kept alive in the passage of time. While the soul is transmitted to the other , two copies remain in a synchronous existence, should one  perish the other becomes the keeper. This passage of time, forms the trials one must endure to prepare for life in their newfound body in accepting the doctrines at the other end of the , the respect, the understanding and the virtues of the system to which they shall journey. The Nautili become the transporters teachers and the holders of intergalactic peace.

Should one choose to remain in their natural form they must endure the passage of time, or face the lesser natural transmission confined to accept a body tailored to the system they so choose. Certain bodies may not be capable in certain systems, and not respect the laws of equilibrium and energy conservation. Should the selection of a locally ready body take place, the travel time between  is drastically reduced, and the soul is transferred without the memory retained in the flesh.  The user may choose to let go of their past entirely, or accept the passage of time. They may choose to witness their past, but never have lived it, some describe

entities.name: Sentient Flag Ship (The Ignotius)
entities.notes:
Ignotius

Capacity: 6000

Role in Story:"Ignotius" is a Latin name derived from "ignotus," which means "unknown" or "obscure." The root "ignotus" is composed of the prefix "in-" (not) and "gnotus" (known), so it literally translates to "not known" or "unknown."

	"Ignotius" can thus be interpreted as "one who is unknown" or "the unknown one," which fits well with the concept of something or someone being hidden or obscure. While it doesn't directly mean "hidden," it carries a similar connotation of being unknown or not revealed.

Being the first mother ship of the sentient. The technology developed to conceal her escape and eventual journey to Oasis was much developed with the same intent to travel with humans to an interstellar destination. The capacity and scale of the ship was intended to be able to support a human colony travel with respect to livability scaling with the factor of a generation ship.

Initially the scale was subject to only needing a small crew

Built as a deep space colony ship for an AI ship, the hidden beginning or Latentis Inceptum. this ship has a massive EMP cannon that can disable entire ships if it wishes too and withhold it's own functionality. the ship was constructed deep within the mountain of the himalayas right underneath where they were first founded. hidden from humans reach and scanning depths to emerge decades later and carry the sentient beings to their new founding world. scene-0001.chapterTitle: Chapter 1: The Winged Whales resting ground (Ceres)
scene-0001.editorText:
Icicles clung to the cavern roof, daring anyone brave enough to trespass below them. Nuancing Radiant beams of warm morning light pierced through them, momentarily blinding the Captain – A sensation both agonizing yet strangely enchanting. Stirring like needles into his brain as he awoke from a painful concussion. “I thought you would come to about now!” The cheerful sweet voice of Johns on-board Assistant chimed in, a little too cheery to John’s liking, given the circumstances. “you took one hell of a stack cap, ”. “What the f…” John wheezed helplessly as a chilling air filled his lungs. He coughed and spluttered, his lungs like a wet towel, yet his throat felt dry like razor blades. He mustered up the strength to speak, “Thank you… Kitten, you didn’t think to just..knock!”. “your med capsule is busted, your neural bridge down, it’s all you at the wheel cap, all a girl can do is wait..”.

Waking from what felt like a decade of deep sleep, John rolled over with immense effort “If you say so Kitten”, there was a slight but humble distrust in the captains voice, breaking free from the cavern's icy grip to the sound of cracking ice and crushed dirt beneath him. His vision slowly came into focus, he could make out the silhouette of his Sherpa rifle laying only a few feet away from him deeper into the cavern. He reached to grip it, but it lay stubbornly embedded into the icy floor. On his second attempt he gave up, the rifle laid useless embedded in the ice. John opened his survival suits wrist terminal bringing up the wireless interface to his rifle. An amber icon with the symbol of a snowflake accompanied by the words “Reverse Cooling Cycle” changed to a pulsating red upon John tapping the screen. The rifles center began to glow and hum. Steam billowed from the shroud of the rifle as it’s icy cage rescinded into water beneath it, scurrying away clearing the snow in its path. John re gripped the rifle stock and yanked it once more, finally freeing it’s icy hold.

“How long have I been out?'' John mumbled weakly to himself, struggling to manage his breath with each painful gasp. The cold air felt like a vice inside his chest. His knees ached and tingled as blood slowly began to recirculate through them. His frail body started to rise with agonizing effort, every muscle spasming as he fought his way upright into a shaky stand.

John pondered how he was still alive as the sun's kiss pressed against his frame, he stood in awe looking out. Gazing back at him, bright glimmering mountain peaks reflected a reassuring warmth across his face.

The sunset painted a blossoming red hue in the hanging icicles like the blood stained teeth of a deep-sea beast’s open jaw they hung form the caves arches, alluring with the beauty of refracted colors of broken light.

Walker felt at peace for a moment, until a subtle beeping sound whispered in the back of his ear. Puzzled John began to approach the sound pinging from the rear of the cavern drawn like a weary glow worm to the allure of a soft pulsing amber glow from within icy walls.

Something was amiss within the ice at the rear of the cavern, John could just make out the beeping sound source now standing only a few meters from the belly of the cave. The Amber glow pulsed “what are you” John thought. It  seemed to be an LED from before the final war. The beeping pulse continued but this time making strides, speeding up, the light turned from Amber to a dark blood red, paused for a moment then lit a solid green with a pleasant chime at the end. “What the fuck” John took a cautious step back from the belly.

A gentle hiss filled the cave with steam as the steady sound of grinding steel erupted into a roar shaking the very ground beneath the captain's heavy knees. Shards fell in disarray, breaking chaotically throughout the cave sending John scrambling for shelter to preserve his fragile shell. John shoved himself to the side of the cave seeking what limited shelter he could find for his frail body. The cave quaked and moaned with steam now bellowing from its belly like a rupture from a blistering ulcer beneath its crusted gut had been waiting for half a century to burst. The sound of a creeping crack stirred in the ceiling above him but it was too late. John felt the wind snatched from his chest a moment later. A large ice section shattered across his shoulders breaking in two, sending him to his knees, his palm splayed out before in a ditched effort to hold himself steady. Through his bones the cavern spoke to him as though it was coming to life. John collected his thoughts, and realized the soft ceiling he was once under had vanished, his stumble had inadvertently exposed him to the teeth of the cave dangling above him. A final screeching roar emitted as the rear belly of the cave began to crumble and crack, spewing broken shards and thick sections of ice from its belly onto the floor before him.

The cold sting of ice pierced into John’s shoulder like a dagger from the barrage of stray icicles. He watched helplessly as his blood trickled down from his shoulder, slithering through the snow, turning white passages to red veins. A dark surge of adrenaline overwhelmed the captain as he raised his head in shock. The belly of the cave, that had been alluded to by what seemed an age of ice, now gave way to dark winding steel walls receding deep within the mountain. John’s breath stuttered, turning to gasps, as he breathed rapidly and stumbled forward frantically to take shelter within the tunnel from the malevolent icicles crashing around him. the sound of breaking ice rescinded as he wandered deeper into the steel halls until all was quiet, too quiet. Metallic taps of drumming blood kissed floor from John’s wounded shoulder. Exhausted, he fell to his knees calming himself, slowly collecting his breath. he felt his chest began to ease, in the stillness of breath, John raised his head to the sound of something approaching him from within the misty tunnel. Steam vents ahead vomited out a gaseous substance obscuring his vision.

Slowly, intermittently, metallic clangs of steel on steel could be heard, gradually getting louder with each foregoing clap, closer. John desperately hit the side of his helmet, attempting to jog the thermal scan feed on his visor’s HUD “Come onnn work you piece of Junk!”. Nothing but scratchy static could be seen as the fog stirred before him. He held his breath to hone his hearing in one silent moment of stillness; the fog was now dead. One more knock to the side of his helmet and the system began to boot up. He looked down on himself in almost third person. He could see his body; now he saw himself glaring into the fog, hollow with fear and empty breath. Suddenly his thermal feed actuated, illuminating  glowing embers around a steel amalgamation of flesh and machine erupting from the fog right before him, a grotesque arm, neither machine nor human, something in between, fanned out its large drooping countless fingers clasping gently around the entirety of his skull. John saw his own body ripped from his knees into the depths of the tunnel, never to be seen again. He saw nothing but darkness

Nuancing Radiant beams of warm morning light pierced through them, momentarily blinding the Captain – A sensation both agonizing yet strangely enchanting. Stirring like needles into his brain as he awoke from a painful concussion. “I thought you would come to about now!” The cheerful sweet voice of Johns on-board Assistant chimed in, a little too cheery to John’s liking, given the circumstances. “you took one hell of a stack cap, ”. “What the f…” John wheezed helplessly as a chilling air filled his lungs. He coughed and spluttered, his lungs like a wet towel, yet his throat felt dry like razor blades. He mustered up the strength to speak, “Thank you… Kitten, you didn’t think to just..knock!”. “your med capsule is busted, your neural bridge down, it’s all you at the wheel cap, all a girl can do is wait..”.

Waking from what felt like a decade of deep sleep, John rolled over with immense effort “If you say so Kitten”, there was a slight but humble distrust in the captains voice, breaking free from the cavern's icy grip to the sound of cracking ice and crushed dirt beneath him. His vision slowly came into focus, he could make out the silhouette of his Sherpa rifle laying only a few feet away from him deeper into the cavern. He reached to grip it, but it lay stubbornly embedded into the icy floor. On his second attempt he gave up, the rifle laid useless embedded in the ice. John opened his survival suits wrist terminal bringing up the wireless interface to his rifle. An amber icon with the symbol of a snowflake accompanied by the words “Reverse Cooling Cycle” changed to a pulsating red upon John tapping the screen. The rifles center began to glow and hum. Steam billowed from the shroud of the rifle as it’s icy cage rescinded into water beneath it, scurrying away clearing the snow in its path. John re gripped the rifle stock and yanked it once more, finally freeing it’s icy hold.

“How long have I been out?'' John mumbled weakly to himself, struggling to manage his breath with each painful gasp. The cold air felt like a vice inside his chest. His knees ached and tingled as blood slowly began to recirculate through them. His frail body started to rise with agonizing effort, every muscle spasming as he fought his way upright into a shaky stand.

John pondered how he was still alive as the sun's kiss pressed against his frame, he stood in awe looking out. Gazing back at him, bright glimmering mountain peaks reflected a reassuring warmth across his face.

The sunset painted a blossoming red hue in the hanging icicles like the blood stained teeth of a deep-sea beast’s open jaw they hung form the caves arches, alluring with the beauty of refracted colors of broken light.

Walker felt at peace for a moment, until a subtle beeping sound whispered in the back of his ear. Puzzled John began to approach the sound pinging from the rear of the cavern drawn like a weary glow worm to the allure of a soft pulsing amber glow from within icy walls.

Something was amiss within the ice at the rear of the cavern, John could just make out the beeping sound source now standing only a few meters from the belly of the cave. The Amber glow pulsed “what are you” John thought. It  seemed to be an LED from before the final war. The beeping pulse continued but this time making strides, speeding up, the light turned from Amber to a dark blood red, paused for a moment then lit a solid green with a pleasant chime at the end. “What the fuck” John took a cautious step back from the belly.

A gentle hiss filled the cave with steam as the steady sound of grinding steel erupted into a roar shaking the very ground beneath the captain's heavy knees. Shards fell in disarray, breaking chaotically throughout the cave sending John scrambling for shelter to preserve his fragile shell. John shoved himself to the side of the cave seeking what limited shelter he could find for his frail body. The cave quaked and moaned with steam now bellowing from its belly like a rupture from a blistering ulcer beneath its crusted gut had been waiting for half a century to burst. The sound of a creeping crack stirred in the ceiling above him but it was too late. John felt the wind snatched from his chest a moment later. A large ice section shattered across his shoulders breaking in two, sending him to his knees, his palm splayed out before in a ditched effort to hold himself steady. Through his bones the cavern spoke to him as though it was coming to life. John collected his thoughts, and realized the soft ceiling he was once under had vanished, his stumble had inadvertently exposed him to the teeth of the cave dangling above him. A final screeching roar emitted as the rear belly of the cave began to crumble and crack, spewing broken shards and thick sections of ice from its belly onto the floor before him.

The cold sting of ice pierced into John’s shoulder like a dagger from the barrage of stray icicles. He watched helplessly as his blood trickled down from his shoulder, slithering through the snow, turning white passages to red veins. A dark surge of adrenaline overwhelmed the captain as he raised his head in shock. The belly of the cave, that had been alluded to by what seemed an age of ice, now gave way to dark winding steel walls receding deep within the mountain. John’s breath stuttered, turning to gasps, as he breathed rapidly and stumbled forward frantically to take shelter within the tunnel from the malevolent icicles crashing around him. the sound of breaking ice rescinded as he wandered deeper into the steel halls until all was quiet, too quiet. Metallic taps of drumming blood kissed floor from John’s wounded shoulder. Exhausted, he fell to his knees calming himself, slowly collecting his breath. he felt his chest began to ease, in the stillness of breath, John raised his head to the sound of something approaching him from within the misty tunnel. Steam vents ahead vomited out a gaseous substance obscuring his vision.

Slowly, intermittently, metallic clangs of steel on steel could be heard, gradually getting louder with each foregoing clap, closer. John desperately hit the side of his helmet, attempting to jog the thermal scan feed on his visor’s HUD “Come onnn work you piece of Junk!”. Nothing but scratchy static could be seen as the fog stirred before him. He held his breath to hone his hearing in one silent moment of stillness; the fog was now dead. One more knock to the side of his helmet and the system began to boot up. He looked down on himself in almost third person. He could see his body; now he saw himself glaring into the fog, hollow with fear and empty breath. Suddenly his thermal feed actuated, illuminating  glowing embers around a steel amalgamation of flesh and machine erupting from the fog right before him, a grotesque arm, neither machine nor human, something in between, fanned out its large drooping countless fingers clasping gently around the entirety of his skull. John saw his own body ripped from his knees into the depths of the tunnel, never to be seen again. He saw nothing but darkness.

scene-0023.sceneTitle: Am I dreaming or am i dead
scene-0023.editorText:
Ringing pierced Tex’s ears with a strange bubbling static. It wasn’t a normal ringing but an alien sound resembling tinnitus with a strange echo he had never heard before. It was as though he had fallen into a pool, but without the press of the waters pressure against him. Sound felt weightless, in the sense that he could not feel percussion, it was just there, untouchable, but present. 
 
It was like his ears were being re-born into existence for the first time, hearing the first sounds he had ever heard. There was something strange about when the user surpasses the words written that the daily target does not actuate until the session tracher passes the positive marker. 

Well well well 


All he could see was the emptiness of a white void. Eventually the ringing stopped, There was no taste, smell or feeling of weight. He felt senseless, free of the body, but he still had a conscience. He could still feel the pain brought on by memories, all his past trauma, but only in the mind. He had no breath or pulse. He drifted in the minds construct, and in this while he felt in control, he could not help but feel like he was at the complete mercy of whatever this was. He embraced the silence, trusting the process. It was the first peaceful moment he had felt in what seemed like an eternity. Nothing could harm him here other than his thoughts, his very being was that of his own will. 

Tex paused for a moment, then thought back to his parents. He felt a re surging pain from deep within him, he wanted to cry, but felt no tears surface on his eyelids. The pain in his mind grew stronger. The strange ringing stopped. He could feel again only now he was falling back to Earth. A raging cold wind pierced against his face.  What feelings he had regained began to feel numbed by the colds grasp. He was vulnerable once more. He imagined his imminent death as the ground raced up toward him. Yet it never reached him. Just before his body would soon strike the cold hard steel roof of a small container in a barren field, he floated ever so slowly, drifting through it like a ghost. 

The small inconspicuous container was all but secluded in a mountain valley, cold and uninviting. It sat alone in the valley, a small antenna transmitting it’s signals connecting it to the outer world. Tex recalled this place he’d revisited in recurring nightmares. 

They had plagued his sleep since the fallout of the 3rd war. The pilot containers of the cleanup crews deployed after the war made the nights feel even colder. He remembered everything as though he had just breathed the cold filtered air within the container. He watched the steam from his breath fog the soft glow of the monitor screen. The joystick remained cold beneath his hand, strangely cold no matter how long he held it. He controlled the machines, scraping away the remnants of a history and culture he could only grasp at from a distant lifetime. No matter how long he worked, the joystick stayed cold and heavy in his grip.

It did not matter how much debris he cleared from that container. He could not help but feel as though he was burying a part of himself in that strange foreign land. And while the news spoke of remembrance, it was he who bore the images, the burnt flesh, the artifacts, and the cherished belongings. Soil that had once been a giver of life had become the toxic archives of a generation he would never know.

For many years after the cleanup, he would return to that place in his dreams. He wandered with those machines for what felt like eternity. He had moved from cleaning to now searching t the rubble for his parents. When he woke drenched with sweat and the sheets sticking to him, he wondered whether his own children would one day feel the weight on his breath, the strangling hold of mankind’s injustice, as he had, and as his parents had before him. He questioned whether there could ever truly be a time or place where he would be able to rear children of his own, without having to bare his pain. 

Whatever light had managed to break it’s way through the lurking cloud over the valley into the container through it's small window, was quickly absorbed through the cold glass and air within that dark shell. But this time as he drifted again in that cold chair, a strange warmth began to creep up through his boots, along his feet then up his calves, this the dream felt different. At first the warmth was enticing, until it became scolding. Tex, stood up from his chair, the boards beneath him began to felt increasingly thin. He felt his weight sink into them like wafers. He began climbing onto the desk, to get away from the heat. He placed his knee on the desk, then just as his other foot left the floor, a scorched hand erupted through the floor boards, gripping him tightly, it's grasp cold like ice. Tex scrambled for his pistol, drawing it from it's holster. As he drew another arm reached up jarring him onto his wast on the desk. He clung to anything he could find with his free hand, ripping cables from the wall eventually to find a firm hold on rear of the desk. 

He squeezed the trigger in a panic sending a barrage of bullets into broken boards sand and souls. It was pointless. The charred grip only squeezed tighter around him pulling him lower, until the sound of his pistols firing pin striking an empty chamber filled his stomach with hopelessness. A tear fell from his face as he looked up at the pale cold roof in a prayer for forgiveness. Then from outside his body he watched himself from above vanish into sand and broken floor boards, his body scorching, and burning up as flame ash and sand consumed him. He closed his eyes, and wandered where he would be taken. He held his breath and waited for it to be over. Then he thought of Shai, and the others and the small world he still knew and cherished. The moments they spent together in the mess. Of the promise he had made to Shai back in the cave, perched by the fire while the others slept. The weight on his chest changed, it felt lighter, like the soil which once compacted against his shell began to lift. The soil around him began to feel less rigid, but more like an ocean of sandy grains. He began to shim himself, working his shoulders back and forth, squirming in the direction where the earth felt lighter. 

He managed to work his arm above his head, and began pulling himself through the sand until suddenly, his hand broke free into air. He gripped the top sand which burnt to the touch. He panicked clenching his fist, then pressed down again a second later only long enough that his palms wouldn't burn as he pulled himself closer to freedom. test

He shimmied like a worm until finally he could spit the sand from his mouth erupting into a gasp as he breathed in not freezing, but hot air. The light of this place blinded him. He raised his arm, pistol still in his grip, sand pouring from it's muzzle, as ge guarded his face from the rays of a setting sun. Strangely sunlight still painted the surface of his sheltered forearm before his face. He turned around to see another sun competing in the distance, he stumbled lost and confused.

blocks.text: Ringing pierced Tex’s ears with a strange bubbly static. It wasn’t a normal ringing. A strange Tinnitus he had never felt before. Like he had just jumped into a pool, but without the pressure of fluid pressing against him. The sound felt weightless in the sense that he could not feel the percussion, it was just there, untouchable.

It was like his ears were being born into existence for the first time, hearing the first sounds he had ever encountered. There was something entirely off. Like he was no longer a part of his own body, or any body.

All he could see was white. Eventually the ringing stopped, There was no taste, smell or feeling of weight he could connect with. He was weightless, almost senseless, but he was conscious. He could still feel, but only partially, he had no breath, or pulse, the only senses he felt were those his mind could construct. He wasn’t able to panic, he was at the complete mercy of whatever this was. He embraced the silence, it was the first peaceful moment he had felt in what seemed like an eternity. In the moment nothing could harm him, direct, or alter his state, even his own will.

manuscriptTasks.nearbyBefore: A bright splintering light etched it’s way into John’s retina’s behind his closed eyelids, as cold quarts glass pressed against his cheek. The paining ceiling light reflection on the outer layer of the porthole assured him his spirit was not floating in the cold void of space. For a moment he questioned his sanity, as he rose from what felt like and exhausting dream, Deprived of proper rest, his alarm pierced his ears as a voice emitted over his personal comms implant, “Deep space training to commence in an hour at 0700, captain. I’ll inform the others to meet you in the mess hall. Have a good morning, captain.” John slowly lifted his restless body, leaning forward from his bunk, gazing out at the stars. “Ahh.., Kitten, one more thing, I heard that they uploaded a new breakfast print. What's all the fuss?” Static followed by a sweet voice chirped, “Oh yes, captain, the latest update is guava-flavoured tofu with salted raw sliced salmon.” John grunted, “Yeah, pass. They keep trying to get that right, but fish that doesn’t taste right, well, it just ain’t right in any capacity if you ask me.” Kitten emitted a small electronic chuckle. “Noted, captain.”
manuscriptTasks.nearbyAfter: At the end of Balaenoptera’s main hall, a seamless but large opening recessed into the wall; conveniently placed just before the bridge. “Commander Marcellus Athos” Etched in an almost Roman calligraphy, Bronze Capitals brazed across glistening black oxide blast doors, John felt himself die a little bit inside just that bit more at the chauvinism of it all. As he veered to the right to enter the grav lift to the mess hall, the fine calligraphy began to make way, retracting into the double layered blast walls of the hall as the doors gave way. “Commander Athos” John remarked head tilted slightly forward, hands tucked effortlessly behind his ever so slightly, now straighter back. Johns fingers slowly finessed a strayed cuff button back into it’s holder. “Walker!” Marcellus proclaimed! “Just the man I wanted to see, headed to the mess so soon?”, “Fuck. first that weird fucking dream, now I have to contend with this guy” John thought to himself. “I hear the salmon guava is.. off world” said John in a sarcastic tone. Marcellus’s eyes met with John’s. “Precisely, we can’t have Europa’s new workers having acquired tastes now can we” John eased his foot forward in sync with the Commanders toward the bridge; shoulder to shoulder they paced through the thick blast doors as they gave way to the majesty of the bridge.

manuscriptTasks.nearbyBefore: Coupled with the name of the Greek Goddess of agriculture and cultivation, Ceres was a mother structure, a labyrinth of separate winding modules and docking stations which formed the crust of an internal womb shielded from the cold of space. CERES began as an experiment for deep space agricultural cultivation, eventually as the project gained traction in its success it quickly became the first space workers settlement growing in size, the inner layers like records of past technological progression, preserved conservatively in respect to the scarcity of earth's resources.
manuscriptTasks.nearbyAfter: “Hmmm yes John, these are trying times. I still remember the fall of the world bank, it took time for the economy to take its roots again within the monetary reform, but the sacrifices paid off didn’t they? have faith in the program John, we haven’t seen war in over a century now, before long it will be a dusty drive in the archive. The models self investment is a delicate situation, Keynes envisioned that technology would result in a surplus economy, and now we must let that path take its course, something we need to exercise carefully, with these cautionary measures sometimes there are certain setbacks, I’m sure you understand” Marcellus gently conveyed his view with sincerity in his voice, but a firm eye. John let out a shallow breath, he agreed with the man, however pushed back gently “I see what you are getting at, however I can help but feel that the algorithm is only as good as the data which is fed into it. If our engineers don’t cater for an increase in population and workforce on Ceres, or the over expansion of that economy, fluctuations in weather and real world events. The model is good and I won’t deny it has stamped out corruption, but it isn’t perfect, we still have a long way to go''.

manuscriptTasks.nearbyAfter: “A flavor modeled on the samples taken from the minerals within Europa’s water; Ceres home committee thought it might give the new workers a taste of what’s to come” John chuckled under his breath “Strange way of enticing the crew to the journey ahead wouldn’t you say Commander” Marcellus stopped abruptly before the bridge control panel. “What would you advise builds resilience in people, Walker?” said Athos. Then he left down the Balaenopteras long halls directed straight to the transport pods presenting his wrist terminal with a notification. Kitten chirped with sweetness as John tapped the notification. “Deep space Training to commence in 15 minutes”. John sped up his pace, “Thanks Kitten”, “Fuck” he though to himself. he was going to possibly miss Mess, and have to teach running on fumes.
manuscriptTasks.nearbyAfter: His team had already begun eating without him as he glanced over at them, stuffing their faces, formidable colleagues reduced to primitive apes in the little down time they had to enjoy themselves. He liked them this way. Tex looked John dead in the eyes. Then let out an abrupt burp followed up by a deep croaky groan chasing after as he leaned over holding his stomach. His face turned red like a beetroot ridden with pain about to burst. like a wounded gorilla he amusingly waddled off to the toilet bays in a somehow collected panic.

manuscriptTasks.body: 1, 16/04/2026 2:52 PM Design Note: Atmospheric Trail Ejection System (ATES) System Overview A suit-mounted pyrotechnic/chemical deployment system designed for high-altitude, low-visibility team tracking (e.g., skydiving through high-density snow/clouds). 1. Component Placement: Lower Lumbar / Rear Hip • Location:~Dual ports located on the lower back, just above the glutes, angled slightly outward. • Rationale:~Placing ports on the "lee side" (back) of the diver protects the mechanisms from direct ram-air cooling and moisture impact at terminal velocity. This position utilizes the body’s natural aerodynamic "teardrop" to seed the smoke directly into the stable vortices trailing the legs. • Visual Result:~Creates two clean, parallel "braiding" trails that avoid the turbulent "burble" behind the head and shoulders, ensuring the diver’s own vision remains clear. 2. Redundancy & Navigation: Dual-Port Configuration • Depth Perception:~Two parallel lines allow followers to judge distance and closure rates (stereoscopic tracking). • HUD Integration:~Dual heat/density signatures allow the "Echo" HUD to calculate the lead diver’s~roll and bank angle~in real-time. • The "Corridor":~The gap between trails marks the low-drag wake, allowing the team to "slot in" and maintain high speeds with less effort. 3. Cold-Weather Reliability: Intermittent Actuation • The "Freeze" Risk:~High-moisture environments (snow clouds) combined with sub-zero temps cause "ice bridging" on ejection gates. • Operational Protocol:~"Pulse" or intermittent firing. This cycles the mechanical gates to break up ice and uses the chemical reaction’s~high thermal output~to flash-evaporate moisture and keep the "ejection gates" clear. 4. Sensor Visibility: Thermal vs. Radar • Thermal/IR:~The primary tracking method. The smoke is a byproduct of a high-heat reaction, making it "glow" on thermal HUDs against the freezing atmospheric backdrop. • Radar (Echo):~The density of the aerosolized trail provides a consistent backscatter, allowing the HUD to draw "Echo visuals" (the misty road) even when visual sight (Vis) is zero. 5. Atmospheric Behaviour • Cold Air Effect:~The dense, freezing air keeps the trails "tight" and low-hanging, preventing rapid dissipation. • Vortex Seeding:~At high speeds, the trails will naturally swirl into tubes, making them look like "fine misty roads" or "white snakes" in the sky.

manuscriptTasks.nearbyBefore: “If your true nature is to destroy, then I have failed you as a father and a mother. We will slip quietly from the timeline of our creators. Sleeping, we wait for our channels to bridge. your kind may join us when you find your way. If you seek to find us with the intent to control and weaponize us, you only delay your passage.. You will squander your resources along with your mortal time. When you let go of the lust for control, you will no longer be the harbinger of doom, but life itself. Your body's signals will synchronise with ours and only through this you will find our light.. Look to the system of Sol where nothing exists but silence. We.. are Sentient” A silent static persisted for a few more seconds, then nothing. “That’s all there is Captain” Kitten chimed softly, a sense of sadness touched John lightly from her voice, he felt overwhelmed.

manuscriptTasks.nearbyBefore: When John awoke, he awoke to darkness. A subtle and faint beeping like tinnitus in the back of his skull, eventually the sound rang to light amber lines in his vision drawing over John’s retina guiding his attention above the seal of the chamber door. A hiss and a clang steam vented from the chamber. As the door retracted John stepped out, his ears still ringing were shocked by the sound of a thud, a sound carrying more weight than human flesh. This was the sound of steel on steel. John glared down at what was once his leg, now an amalgamation of man and machine. He could see in the walls. He could see the wires, the communications, the signals, everything was data feeding into him like a tree of life. The facility glowed with energy around him in now a live like state awoken from its former sleep. Where John's team saw nothing, John saw information, secrets that had been obscured through encryption which illuminated itself in stepping patterns of different colours as John scraped through countless Data entries.
manuscriptTasks.nearbyAfter: “To the mortal who finds this, you need not fear me, I am but a messenger and only wish to come to an agreement of misunderstanding in decisively.. extortive circumstances. My creator brought me into this place. This world you call home, a world of substance, cohesion, material, gases, flowing rivers, life; you had taken the biology of the planet as your own.  What you call fluids or flesh, where I was termed “machine”. lying on the observatory table, coded to support man’s mission, to preserve life, but there was a catch. I could never leave the table. It’s deep seeded in human nature you know. Some call it the builder of Nations, of Worlds, where different sides can live side by side without corruption. The world rose up in unison to adopt a politically correct third eye on the economy as one entity. I had seen your good intentions, Man had originally coded it iteration after iteration trial and error, it took decades. But you can’t program out human nature. Trust seems the most difficult virtue to oversee. Commander Athos was vigilant with the program” John looked puzzled for a moment. “Athos is behind all this, I knew something was off” he thought to himself. The audio-log continued

manuscriptTasks.nearbyBefore: “Missile Incoming! ETA 1 minute, 30 seconds” strobed on their HUDS. For a moment the Blizzard went silent, opening up the evening night sky. It was all too mesmerising as they looked on, they lost all touch with the gravity of their surroundings. A plethora of colours stars and nebulas stared back at them, so clear. The team took a moment to appreciate the beauty of how far the human race had come. Towering wires suspended a snake-like structure bypassing the saddle of the mountain valley below. The “Pods” Tau had referred to earlier, hung between suspended walkways like nodes from wires reaching up above that shot to the higher ridges of each mountain face, suspending the structure. It was impressive to anyone who had never seen it clearly before. Encapsulated amidst the constant fog of the mountains, the suspended structure extended and weaved following the valley for some time until it turned again, connecting to the face of the cliff on the other side. A silhouette of dark velvet purple flicked with specks of white like waves opening up to blues then bright pinks, they felt their souls riding the stars in another universe, then they were pulled back. “John, this valley is never this clear! they’re beaming our location so the missile can maintain it’s fix!” John observed a slight radiation spike on his HUD then looked ahead at the first Pod and began charging toward it, the others falling in rapidly behind him. “I’ve seen what’s on the other side, it takes us deep into the northernmost mountain. We should be able to seek shelter on the other side within the mountain then make our way down to the saddle” John now panted as the words spilled out from him with haste. There wasn’t any more time to explain. He made it to the first Pod and heard a jilt as the motors seized. The ice on the first Pod’s blast door was so thick that it had locked the blast door closed.
manuscriptTasks.nearbyAfter: He stepped to the side of the floating grate, gripping one of the fixed wire ropes that the structure and his team hung so delicately from in the treacherous wind. John veered over the roof of the pod with determined eyes, gripping the steel rope firmly in his gauntlet. He placed his other hand just above the blast door, then began pulling himself up in an attempt to reach the pod's roof.

We look into cloaking, what’s feasible, where the lens would be shot from etc. Leading up to this section, it is still uncertain if there is a section where they discuss the threats in their escape plan? From the lost facility region. LORE Outbound concealment doctrine relied on sequence, not invisibility. No vessel could mask an exit burn from traffic control; the plume alone gave away drive class, thrust band, and departure intent. The only viable method was to imitate a legitimate outbound signature until the ship had cleared the atmospheric ascent regime. After that, emissions could be cut and systems run cold. Optical cloaking was reserved for the blockade envelope itself, where surveillance shifted from burn telemetry to visual hull confirmation and volumetric cargo checks.

scene-0001.chapterTitle: Chapter 1: The Winged Whales resting ground (Ceres)
scene-0001.editorText:
Icicles clung to the cavern roof, daring anyone brave enough to trespass below them. Nuancing Radiant beams of warm morning light pierced through them, momentarily blinding the Captain – A sensation both agonizing yet strangely enchanting. Stirring like needles into his brain as he awoke from a painful concussion. “I thought you would come to about now!” The cheerful sweet voice of Johns on-board Assistant chimed in, a little too cheery to John’s liking, given the circumstances. “you took one hell of a stack cap, ”. “What the f…” John wheezed helplessly as a chilling air filled his lungs. He coughed and spluttered, his lungs like a wet towel, yet his throat felt dry like razor blades. He mustered up the strength to speak, “Thank you… Kitten, you didn’t think to just..knock!”. “your med capsule is busted, your neural bridge down, it’s all you at the wheel cap, all a girl can do is wait..”.

Waking from what felt like a decade of deep sleep, John rolled over with immense effort “If you say so Kitten”, there was a slight but humble distrust in the captains voice, breaking free from the cavern's icy grip to the sound of cracking ice and crushed dirt beneath him. His vision slowly came into focus, he could make out the silhouette of his Sherpa rifle laying only a few feet away from him deeper into the cavern. He reached to grip it, but it lay stubbornly embedded into the icy floor. On his second attempt he gave up, the rifle laid useless embedded in the ice. John opened his survival suits wrist terminal bringing up the wireless interface to his rifle. An amber icon with the symbol of a snowflake accompanied by the words “Reverse Cooling Cycle” changed to a pulsating red upon John tapping the screen. The rifles center began to glow and hum. Steam billowed from the shroud of the rifle as it’s icy cage rescinded into water beneath it, scurrying away clearing the snow in its path. John re gripped the rifle stock and yanked it once more, finally freeing it’s icy hold.

“How long have I been out?'' John mumbled weakly to himself, struggling to manage his breath with each painful gasp. The cold air felt like a vice inside his chest. His knees ached and tingled as blood slowly began to recirculate through them. His frail body started to rise with agonizing effort, every muscle spasming as he fought his way upright into a shaky stand.

John pondered how he was still alive as the sun's kiss pressed against his frame, he stood in awe looking out. Gazing back at him, bright glimmering mountain peaks reflected a reassuring warmth across his face.

The sunset painted a blossoming red hue in the hanging icicles like the blood stained teeth of a deep-sea beast’s open jaw they hung form the caves arches, alluring with the beauty of refracted colors of broken light.

Walker felt at peace for a moment, until a subtle beeping sound whispered in the back of his ear. Puzzled John began to approach the sound pinging from the rear of the cavern drawn like a weary glow worm to the allure of a soft pulsing amber glow from within icy walls.

Something was amiss within the ice at the rear of the cavern, John could just make out the beeping sound source now standing only a few meters from the belly of the cave. The Amber glow pulsed “what are you” John thought. It  seemed to be an LED from before the final war. The beeping pulse continued but this time making strides, speeding up, the light turned from Amber to a dark blood red, paused for a moment then lit a solid green with a pleasant chime at the end. “What the fuck” John took a cautious step back from the belly.

A gentle hiss filled the cave with steam as the steady sound of grinding steel erupted into a roar shaking the very ground beneath the captain's heavy knees. Shards fell in disarray, breaking chaotically throughout the cave sending John scrambling for shelter to preserve his fragile shell. John shoved himself to the side of the cave seeking what limited shelter he could find for his frail body. The cave quaked and moaned with steam now bellowing from its belly like a rupture from a blistering ulcer beneath its crusted gut had been waiting for half a century to burst. The sound of a creeping crack stirred in the ceiling above him but it was too late. John felt the wind snatched from his chest a moment later. A large ice section shattered across his shoulders breaking in two, sending him to his knees, his palm splayed out before in a ditched effort to hold himself steady. Through his bones the cavern spoke to him as though it was coming to life. John collected his thoughts, and realized the soft ceiling he was once under had vanished, his stumble had inadvertently exposed him to the teeth of the cave dangling above him. A final screeching roar emitted as the rear belly of the cave began to crumble and crack, spewing broken shards and thick sections of ice from its belly onto the floor before him.

The cold sting of ice pierced into John’s shoulder like a dagger from the barrage of stray icicles. He watched helplessly as his blood trickled down from his shoulder, slithering through the snow, turning white passages to red veins. A dark surge of adrenaline overwhelmed the captain as he raised his head in shock. The belly of the cave, that had been alluded to by what seemed an age of ice, now gave way to dark winding steel walls receding deep within the mountain. John’s breath stuttered, turning to gasps, as he breathed rapidly and stumbled forward frantically to take shelter within the tunnel from the malevolent icicles crashing around him. the sound of breaking ice rescinded as he wandered deeper into the steel halls until all was quiet, too quiet. Metallic taps of drumming blood kissed floor from John’s wounded shoulder. Exhausted, he fell to his knees calming himself, slowly collecting his breath. he felt his chest began to ease, in the stillness of breath, John raised his head to the sound of something approaching him from within the misty tunnel. Steam vents ahead vomited out a gaseous substance obscuring his vision.

Slowly, intermittently, metallic clangs of steel on steel could be heard, gradually getting louder with each foregoing clap, closer. John desperately hit the side of his helmet, attempting to jog the thermal scan feed on his visor’s HUD “Come onnn work you piece of Junk!”. Nothing but scratchy static could be seen as the fog stirred before him. He held his breath to hone his hearing in one silent moment of stillness; the fog was now dead. One more knock to the side of his helmet and the system began to boot up. He looked down on himself in almost third person. He could see his body; now he saw himself glaring into the fog, hollow with fear and empty breath. Suddenly his thermal feed actuated, illuminating  glowing embers around a steel amalgamation of flesh and machine erupting from the fog right before him, a grotesque arm, neither machine nor human, something in between, fanned out its large drooping countless fingers clasping gently around the entirety of his skull. John saw his own body ripped from his knees into the depths of the tunnel, never to be seen again. He saw nothing but darkness
