Before John could even speak in response to her distress, Tex noticed a glowing purple light fastly approaching the edge of the underbelly on the 2nd Pod. “She’s done it,” Tex said with disbelief looking on in awe while grabbing out his stowed Railstorm on the lower rear of his suit.

John smiled, thinking to himself, “I knew she was a good pilot, she just needed a push.” Shai erupted from the fog, blasting out the cold icy weather from the pod's roof. Ice melted away beneath her, falling only to turn to icicles descending into the void. The slow burn of her suit's thrusters hummed an echo that spat back at her team, almost as if to be inviting them in. Arms of velvet hydrogen glowed, reaching around her giving an almost angelic appearance of wings as she slowly descended.  Her suit’s thrusters powered down with almost  synchronous timing as the contact magnetism in her boots peaked her suit's computer engaged their locking mechanism.  Her mag boots coils let out a crisp electronic hum, latching her to the solid steel roof of the pod. “That was some hot shit girly” Said Tex, looking over at Shai than down to the depths below, swallowing what smart remarks he had left in hesitation.

Shai re-engaged her suits thrusters blowing away what remained of the ice creating an even bigger landing area for the others still stranded across the valley. “The payload of the LRM SRM bank is small, only one,” Tao said as the others locked back their suits. One by one they all followed. Tao was next to make the leap, Tex behind her then John. In almost unison as though he was there to help her subtly. Then John was the last.

Proximity sensor on the Engine signature was getting stronger, Tau looked over concerned, her eyes fixed on John. John pressed jumped “Tao do you have anything? Kitten?”, John was hesitant but still cool. Then he went, charging like a bull and launching himself agile through the air, turning to the side when he did this. He turned using the assist of his suit thrusters to send him into a sideways barrel roll spinning in the air, dodging a barrage of missile small fires. The LRM sheer size had made it suitable for small to mid-calibre arms, enough to rattle a Protectant's armour.

He opened out his arms pointing directly at the LRM, tracking it quietly with patience. It was silent, and then it wasn’t anymore. John felt his mind ripped from his own shell. Kitten tapped into john’s vision feed. The long range missile went from a mere thermal blip to a clear burning contraption of death displayed across the others visors. After the object tracking software computed it’s trajectory heading straight for them, Kitten felt it apparent to warn them of what was coming their way. But John was all but silent, absent minded it seemed. Carefree.

Tor’s monitor flickered with static. A vague distant thermal imaging outline of figures resembling that of a protectant squad vanished from the screen then in a split second connection had all but been lost.

“We’ve lost control of the LRM!” said Tor, “What! how is that possible!” Marcellus lurched over Tor’s terminal, sneering in disbelief. “Get that missile back up or you’ll be promoted to Janitor!” Marcellus was red in the face. “But Athos! wasn’t that!” Athos cut Tor off, “I won’t repeat myself”.
The lost Facility
“I had some upgrades too Cap! when you got plugged into that we got plugged in, your neural code has been assimilated with mine” Kitten seemed ecstatic like she had found a new friend, then

John went silent and stopped firing. He could see himself outside of his body looking down straight on top of his team. He was not himself, but piloting a payload of death and destruction as the missiles targeting reticle converged on his point. He had control of the missile. A pristine three dimensional schematic illuminated the internal workings of the carrier of death. He thought hard, envisioning the missiles motors that steered it’s control surfaces. Motor actuators spun up as he flew through the circuits. slowly he began veering the missile off his direct course, steering it sharply back to where they had all just jumped from. He saw himself standing there like a statue drifting from vision as the targeting reticle lost vision of him. approaching an ever enlarging cavernous mouth.
John once certain he and the others were clear of the missiles strike zone, felt himself drawn back to his body, his vision coming back almost instantly. “I’ve got control again!” John croaked.

Sending it straight through the roof of the previous pod he had just jumped over. The explosion detonated almost a split second after it clonked through the steel roof, sending a wave shock that shook dagger like icicles from the overhead ridges. A barrage of teeth fell for John’s team only to break and shatter into oblivion on their armoured shoulders. The explosion was so powerful it sent the top of the cliff face they had just leaped from into an avalanche, enraged the mountain snow rock and rubble entombed the steel mountain halls of the lost facility from where they had just came. Leaving it hidden once again, silent, waiting to found again bearing history’s truth of the workerbot program for those who sought it.

The sound of screeching steel echoed the ravines that wound on for miles in either direction. Eventually the sound of metal and rock clashing sent shivers down his spine. The wire ropes sung and whipped under tension at the beckon of the wind. The grate bridges had lost some of their supporting wires in the explosion of the now relinquished missile. They croaked and moaned, hanging drunkenly in unforgiving icy winds. Snow ice and wind pelted against the pod’s shell slowly a heavy section  of ice that had accumulated atop the pod's dangling body began to slip. It was silent, and then once more it wasn’t. The loud crack of snapping steel wire ricochet off the mountain’s side. A mass of ice breaking into oblivion fell rapidly to the misty depths below.

The tattered pod shuddered, collapsing inward before expanding again, sending tremors through the entire structure. Loose wires began to fall, tugging at the ones still connected to John and his team, pulling them ever so slightly downward. The cables groaned under the strain, slowly dragging them deeper. The pod’s weight strained the wires to their breaking point, their groans swallowed by the biting wind. High-pressure oscillations vibrated through the lines, making the team's hairs stand on end as they listened to the ominous creaking. The pod, struck by the missile, now dangled precariously, its dozen supporting cables reduced to a fragile few. What remained was a desperate struggle for survival—both the pod and the lives of John, Tex, Tau, and Shai, clinging to the last threads of hope.

The hanging hidden facilities mountain interlink, like a lined up stack of dominoes, began breaking away from the Himalayan cliff face, falling like a snake out of a tree into the ravenous unknown below, bellowing out a symphony of snapping wires in the valley as it danced in the wind to its death below. Shai watched on. She felt the stomach’s of her teammates sink. Her and John’s team were about to go with it. Another supporting wire snapped.

John felt himself go cold again. He was flying through the pod's wiring infrastructure and electronic circuitry once more. He scaled the walls, he was right at the panel before he knew he had disconnected. The locking mechanism which resembled that of a 20th century train interlock, disengaged. The hanging station pod let go, Screeching steel could be heard as the final connecting face of the Pod link up cracked. strike zones. Licking the edges of the final connecting Pod, the pod John Tau and all his team now stood on lifted back calmly to it’s previous guys positions. They had all felt a touch of their new suits capabilities. They’d done it, and they’d done it elegantly. They looked at each other and then  to their now escape and shelter. John thought to himself

“I’m liking these new upgrades” John said walking towards another opening in the cliff face along what remained of the facility mountain pass. “We best take shelter” Steam bellowed from his helmet as he spoke the command softly.  Sherpa Rifles at the ready the others fell in line behind him.

“We need to recuperate our suit’s hydrogen reserves” Shai’s voice seemed chilled as she moved, listening carefully ahead at an almost uniform speed set by John. John was already at a large opening, except there were no blast doors or fortified facilities, only the shelter provided by re-enforced tunnels and cave. The winding tunnels had strata bolts drilled deep into the mountain to hold mesh of rock from crushing them. “I think we will be ok here for the time being” Said John. He looked around scanning the cave with his rifle. Something crunched beneath the weight of his suit. A used fireplace sat. “Only a couple weeks old” Tex walked over to the fireplace his shoulders relaxed his rifle at ease cradled in his forearm. He looked over at John. “Probably mountain locals prying, snooping about, they usually come up here to salvage parts”. Small jets of steam bellowed out of the chest on John’s Mark IV suit, John emerged from its splayed out chest cavity still slightly disorienting to the others as they looked on at what felt like his frail yet armoured body. As he stepped as soon as his hand lost touch with the suit’s shell it immediately closed back up turning about face and began guarding the entrance to the cave.

Tex had already begun harvesting ice off the cave face, still in his suit a strange tongue like contraption hugged the face of the cave creating a cupping bowl seal against the caves icy wall. As a his gauntlets ice burner melted columns of icicles along the wall water trickled into the strange contraption. Plumes of mist emitted from his shoulders out ports as the suit’s internal Electrolysis chamber separated hydrogen from the steady water stream. “You two get some rest, Me and Shai will keep watch” Tex didn’t look away while he talked, fixated,  just kept succing ice from the walls of the cavern. he made his way a fan like motion as a nano engineered suction cup moulded to the face, licking the walls like the tongue of a giant anteater. Tao climbed down from her suit, for it only to turn towards the descending tunnel in the other direction from where they had just entered. It walked seamlessly like a human, over to the steep downward tunnel that seemed to wind on forever into pitch blackness. A looming mist filled the belly of it, concealing it’s depths and what lay below from the human eye. Tao knelt down behind it, tapping a code into the suits rear hold. from it she pulled out a small capsule then tossed it onto the ground. As it hit the ground it let out a small hiss, expanding rapidly into a comfortable single air mattress. She laid down perching her head on the mattress's inbuilt, looked over at John with a faint smile that comforted him as he knelt down running his mechanical fingers through the coal.

“Well we made it this far, Considering the circumstances, I’ll take that as a plus”. John nodded in agreeance, reached behind his pack and pulled out a cylindrical device, scooping up some of the coal into it’s belly, Then tossed it to Tex. “Here, top this up” Tex diverted some of the water flow into the canister, heated the canister. pressure pushed the heated water in a vacuum pushing it through the charcoal producing clear clean water out the other side. Tex swirled the contents veering through the transparent half of the cylinder eyeing the water inside, took a swig, nodded in approval, “Earth water, Doesn’t get much better than that” and passed the cylinder back to John with curious eyes. John drank from it without hesitation. “I’m still collecting myself after Shai’s piloting display back there”. Shai chuckled humbly perched up against the cave wall as she reached over to take a drink from the canister. “Thanks Walker. you weren’t too bad yourself”.

Tex was still scouring the walls of the cave recouping the hydrogen reserves, he shut off his burner, walked over to John’s suit, knelt down and pulled out a large hydrogen cell, exchanging it for his own in his suit, re-fired his burner up and resumed scathing the walls for any ice. The whole motion of the cell exchange seemed like he was handling a foam cylinder. Despite the cell’s weight, the suit made little work handling the solid mass packed with platinum conversion cores “John, don’t you find it a little strange that we didn’t receive any notification from Commands long range transmitters of any enemy missiles headed our way, that and also, 68% may not be a solid signature on the plume. But, put two and two together, I think that bumps that % up to 100”, “We don’t know just yet big guy. best not to make any assumptions. with the severity of the blizzard, they could have simply lost connection to our receivers” Tao looked over at John with suspicious eyes, then looked over to Tex. “The captain's right, We can’t run on assumptions this soon”. Tex let out a snort in disproval “I don’t trust that fucker, he gives me chills”.

Shai walked over to Tex, laid her hand softly on his cladded shoulder like a blossom petal falling in a cold winter on polished granite “take a break buddy, I’ll get the other cells” watching his blood pressure lower in her HUD, she fired up her Ice burner and a slurping sound echoed off the walls once more, “Why does everything remind me of her” Tex smirked as he joked. John shook his head, “Well good to see you can still maintain a sense of humour even if the odds are stacked against us”, “I’m more concerned for his x if this reminds him of her, what did you do to the poor girl?” Shai turned around looking directly at Tex. “Well, they don’t call me Big guy for nothing” Tex sat down nearby the main entrance to the cave, letting out a sigh as he lowered himself to the ground in his suit “I heard your x used to refer to you as tiny?” John raised his eyebrows although the rest of his face was expressionless. “Yep! Big guy, Tiny heart”, Tex shrugged as he finished his sentence. “I think it’s the other way around with a touch of sarcasm on the first one” Shai was smiling inside her suit, but the others couldn’t see it, she knew the big guy was more sentimental than he let off. It’s also why she felt she could calm the mass of muscle when he got worked up.

“Alright well I don’t know about the rest of you but I could use some shut eye, whatever the Fuck is going on, it’ll make more sense on a clear mind” reached over pulling a small cylindrical device from his suit’s utility hold. He placed it on the cavern floor next to the now cold dormant fireplace, primed a timer to 5 seconds, and laid his heavy body comfortably a safe distance from the device as it chimed down to zero.Air  Particles ionized, then sintered in a brief display of dancing lights in the air around it from it emerged what felt like the soul of a jelly fish born from flame, its tentacles trails of smoke, gracing down to the cave floor. The room turned almost instantly warmer as the device beamed an amber glow in the cylinder’s vicinity.  John laid his head back, let out a deep sigh as he gazed at the cave ceiling. A blinking hydrogen cell light dimly lit the. “I know one thing, It’s nice to be out of zero G”, “And to be breathing non-filtered air” Tex said in agreeance as he popped off the modular housing from his sherpa rifle for a routine clean and inspection. “Wake you up in 20 cap, we should be restocked by then” said Shai. John closed his eyes, Tau laid still on her side looking over at John, slowly drifting off to the humming burn of Shai’s Ice burner. John fell into a deep sleep, his chest rising and falling slowly.

“You think that’s all John in there still” Tex spoke softly, not to disturb Siante and Walker. “Feels like it, but I know what you mean, he seems different.. quieter, I mean for all we know he’s still processing everything internally”, “He seems to be holding up alright, notice anything odd on his vitals”, “They’re more or less the same, I haven’t really had the time to run a proper analysis”, “Well you just give me the word if you need me to, you know”, “I don’t know Tex, I trust him, It’s not like he’s ever given us a reason not to”, “He stepped into an unknown piece of technology over a century old, he put the integrity of the squad at risk”, “I know, it doesn’t seem like John, but we have to trust him. If we lose John given all he’s done, well who can we really trust then”. Tex sat quietly for a moment digesting his thoughts. “And what if that LRM was Marcellus, what then? what are we supposed to, face the protectant on our own, Go into hiding? I wouldn’t mind being a nomad if you ask me. I could do it”. Shai stopped for a moment her burner went silent as the suit drained the last remaining fluid in it’s lines, an amber light on her suit’s hydrogen cell turned green indicating full capacity. “Honestly I don’t know right now Tex, but I know one thing, John will get us out of this. He always does”. She was even softer in her voice this time, more convincing. “Alright, If you say so tiger” Tex, seemed reserved in his response, but he let his shoulders down with a deep sigh. “I do know of an old friend in Nepal, nerdy type, he might be able to get his hands on a stealth frigate to get us out flying under the radar, I haven’t spoken to him in a decade, but I’m sure he’s still lurking around in the shadows somewhere, Nerdy but slippery that fucker”. Shai chuckled a little at Tex’s comment. “I think any option is a good option right now, big guy”, she agreed. Shai and Tex got lost for a few minutes, reminiscing stories of the lost war, their past missions together recalling all the times they’d got out “By a hair”.

Before Tau and John awoke soon enough Shai had recharged all 4 hydrogen Cell’s. “Do you think we should give them a couple more minutes?” Said Shai, looking into her HUD observing their sleep state and fatigue levels. “I know one thing, If that was Marcellus it’s only a matter of time before he gets a drone down here to finish the job, and I don’t particularly want to be waiting around when that happens, best we high tail it until we can glean more information”, “agreed, we need to keep moving, we don’t know what other secrets we might find down here, lets wake them up”. Shai tapped her HUD immediately after her statement. The neural implants on Tau and Shai tingled in the back of their necks waking them gently from their slumber. “All cells are recharged Cap” Shai smiled her gauntlet held out with an open palm to help Tau up. Tau grabbed onto the cold steel of Shai’s gauntlet, her skin slightly sticking as she let go. “those suit’s really take the affection out of a good gesture.. thanks”, “strange, I still feel every touch like it’s the suit isn’t even there, the Engineers really did a good job triangulating the nerve centers to the static shorting on the suit’s surface” Shai was trying to defend the suit, and kitten couldn’t agree more. “It took them almost 2 decades to get it right!” kitten chimed. “Alright enough chit chat. We need to keep moving” John was already climbing back into his suit. Tex looked over at Shai and shrugged his shoulders. “Fine by me cap” Said Tex pulling his rifle up into his shoulder and cocking it. “Keep on the lookout, we still don’t know if scavengers are active in the area, or who owned those missiles.” John clicked on his HUD opening up a holographic overview of the tunnel layout. “I managed to pull these maps from the facility archives, this tunnel will take us straight to the bottom of the valley, from there we can get up some hard comms to the facilities transmitter, and try and make contact with the Commander”, “Aaah cap!,” Tex wasn’t happy with John’s announcement. “68%, yeahh.. I know Tex, but what’s the worst he’s gonna do, yell profanities at us from orbit? he’s up there, we are down here. Besides there is a tower transmitter atop the facility mountain, we can use the multipathing off the mountain's faces to scramble our location if you are concerned”, Tau looked over at Tex, “Checks out”, She shrugged her shoulders. “Ok, but if I find out it was him, I dibs first blows”. “Ok big guy you can get intimate with him all you like when you see him next, lets move then”. John made his way over to the tunnel and started making his way down. Rocks and rubble rolled knocking echoes through the tunnel which seemed to be endless. “Watch your step” Shai whispered softly, John looked back at her pausing for a brief second holstered his sherpa rifle in it’s mount on his back then continued to descend down into the tunnels depths as he gripped both sides of the tunnels damp walls. The others all mounted their rifles following behind him.

“Wouldn’t it have been easier to just use our suits jump thrusters and jump from the mountain pass to touch down on the valley bottom?” Said Tex, “And what burn through half our reserve again?” “Tau’s right Tex, we don’t want to get caught in out in the open with few cards up our sleeve”. Tex’s demeanour lacked effort, the big guy was getting bored with all the climbing. He preferred fast paced environments and detested the monotony of it all. “How much fucking longer is this going to take” he thought to himself. “Not far left, we are almost at the saddle we are at 17,500 feet … it plateaus out at approximately 17,000  feet.”, “Yikes wasn’t the old base camp for Everest around that?”, “probably why we are seeing scavenger activity in the area. the pass isn’t far from it it seems”. Shai was listening intently, “So much history in such a strange place of the world, We are lucky to experience it if you ask me”. “I guess you could say that”, Tau said in agreeance.

The strain on their legs eased as the tunnel began to level off. John grabbed his Sherpa rifle from it’s mount, reseating it against his shoulder. One by one the others following suit as they regained their balance behind him. “John, I’m detecting a heat signature up ahead” Shai was uncertain in her tone, “But, it doesn’t appear to be human, I’m detecting a 20% higher bpm”. John raised a closed fist, bringing the others to a halt. “Can we get a solid confirmation on that Shai?” said John, Kneeling to the floor.

Shai tapped on her wrist terminal gently. A small antenna array protruded then splayed out like small tendrons invisible to the human eye drifted in the breeze drawn down through the tunnel into the valley. They tendrons floated in the breeze listening, reverberating the distant heartbeat into life on Shai’s HUD, “Getting a closer analysis now Cap” Shai seemed more confident this time. “Aaah cap what’s showing up on the scan isn’t in our database, although it seems to be a large mammal, threat level low”. “I didn’t think any Mammals could survive in this region, or at least had been recorded here in over a century other than humans” Tau was surprised to hear. “Let’s keep moving, but stay alert” John steadily paced forward, one foot gently leading the other, his eyes rested vigilantly on his rifle site’s scanning each sector in a sweeping motion. The tunnel began to rapidly open out into a large cavernous maze. “Stick together” John was calm in his command, breathing gently as he paced steadily forward. “The opening is just up ahead”, “John, that heartbeat signature. It’s moving, not fast, but slowly, away from us” said Shai. John could see the opening up ahead of him. He turned off his HUD view for a moment then paused and retracted his helmet’s visor, the cold wind bit his face, but he thought nothing of it in the moment “I..”, John stopped still in his tracks, holding his breath as his gaze fixed dead ahead at the caves opening. Soft snow gently breezed through the mouth in the evening light. A lean grey figure seemed to slip like a shadow from the inner cavern’s wall into the opening. It stood there in still silence. It’s silhouette left John and the others in wonder, as the silhouettes eyes reflected an amber green back at them. They glared deep into John’s, still in time, two beings from different realms connected for a brief second. A bright light shone, the connection between John and the creature in an instant vanished as the figures eyes diverted to the beam emitted from Tex’s rifle torch. John raised his closed fist “Hold your…”  The figure stood still averting it’s gaze to Tex. A fraction of a second later it was gone. “What the fuck was that” Tex collected himself as he slowly lowered his weapon from where the creature once stood, he looked over at Shai waiting for an answer.

“Bringing it up now big guy”. The front half of an almost life-like three dimensional model, compiled from all four of their suit’s recorded images, materialized the creature from the pristine white surroundings of the valley’s backdrop. Its fur, a tapestry of muted grays and whites, seamlessly blended with the snowy canvas, had rendered the being almost invisible. its piercing eyes reflected what felt like ancient wisdom imbued with the prowess of survival. shades of greenish-gray, reminiscent of lichen-covered rocks from deep within the tunnel from where they’s once came, possessed an otherworldly brilliance. Intelligence exuded from the creature's keen eyes. “I didn’t think this possible Cap, but what we are seeing here, has long thought to be extinct. This explains why it didn’t show up on the database scan”, “Well, if it’s evolved over centuries of navigating this treacherous no-mans land, it’s no surprise it was thought to be extinct”. Tau looked at John, retracting her visor so he could see the joy in her face. “John.. that’s a snow leopard. They were hunted by scavengers in the region for their pelts, one pelt would feed a family for a year”. John paused reflecting on what had just happened. The gaze between him and his curious friend had been no casual encounter; but rare. An indelible mark had been left with him. In a silent ephemeral exchange of respect between one spirit in it’s home and the other, now lost.

“If she managed to remain hidden all this time with all the our scanning suite, what else could be hiding in these mountains”. At that John drew down his visor, stepping out into the thick blanket of snow crushing it helplessly beneath his boots. -10 Degrees Celsius fluctuated peaking at -12 on the teams HUD, but they couldn’t feel the colds bite, just the wind resistance as the storm pelted against their suits. “There is a clearing up ahead” Said John, determination stuck to his voice like cold steel. Tau stopped still in her“John, do.. do you see what I am

scene-0016.chapterTitle: Chapter 3: Synaptic Memoriam of a steel fossil shell
scene-0016.editorText:
A large belly of fog slept over a large opening in the valley alluding the others to strange figures scattered in a mangle mass of steel and snow, from that tall glooming tower like pebbles from a fallen meteor, the carapaces spread deeper into the valley as far as the eye could see. John was silent with no remark to Tau’s comment, but his silence spoke for him. He kneeled down in the fog, wafting it away to reveal the cold carapace of what seemed like an ancient machine. The vast shells of the disposed sentient had a disorienting effect. Tao and Shai had never seen a site less akin to that of a Mongolian grave yet never of such a scale, such destruction.

“It’s like they all collectively came here, to die”. Tau’s voice was a mix of confusion, and sorrow. “There’s hardly anything left of this one?” Tex knelt down, splaying his fingers out to grasp one of the shells. “Wait” Shai tried to stop Tex in the action, but was unsuccessful. Tex ripped from the carapace one of its mangled arms. “I don’t think they just came here, and died. They’ve taken a hell of a beating.”, “We don’t know how long these things have even been here. I’ve never seen anything like it” Shai was reluctant to believe that such a mass of what felt like harmless machines could have sustained intentionally the damage that Tex was implying, She wanted to believe something unintentional and inconsequentially had fallen upon them. But Tex had other views, his tone spoke of something sinister at play, riddled with concern.

“Kitten what would it take to plug me into it’s neural network is it possible with these things. I mean they must have a memory core. Could we.. somehow see what they saw in their final moments?”, “Certainly captain, I can possibly reroute some of your nanobots to repair any weathered or damaged circuitry within it’s memory glands . When you connected to the facility I was able to extract the latest build archives so I have a reference to go off”. Tex intervene between the two. “I think it’s circuits should be mostly preserved, there are bodies still up on these mountains preserved like they fell yesterday from pre-war time. The cold has a funny way of keeping the dead alive”, Tex looked over to John. “Ok let’s give it a shot, I’m going to tether to it”. Tex looked over to Shai but said nothing almost as though he was concerned but to what John and Tau could not quite put their finger on. They didn’t make much of it anyway.

John knelt down, placing his hand gently over one of the machine's frame. The skull, or what John had assumed to be it’s skull emitted a soft bio luminescent glow which kissed the inner edges of an aesthetically streamlined hardened frame protecting a gelatinous substance within.

John reached in through the frame touching what felt like hard glass through the suit’s kinetic touch sensors. It seemed he almost intuitively knew where to touch as the others looked on, slightly anxious. Nothing could be seen on the surface of the glass, no recesses, no insignia, just a soft glow. A soft hiss let out as streams of mist bellowed out from a small pressure port at the necking of the machines brain like transparent dome. Beneath a series of wires like a pine cone extruding from a core, resembled a machine like brain which almost took the shape of a humans. It wasn't a circular dome as such but elongated, holding deceivingly from the front, more mass than that of a human skull.

John extended his robotic arm out to the machine, his palm softly laying over the machines brain. “The battery in this thing is dead to the core.. You can’t exactly pick up any life signs or data packets. I mean it’s hard to read these things. The memory is magnetic like the older ones. it requires a boot but i don’t want to fry the synapses. Tau can you give me an analysis on the inputs and outputs from the current flow. How much juice do I have to give this thing before I turn this brain and those memories to Mush.” “Sure John, Aaah you can’t do that with your new body, no IC for that kind of analysis huh?”, “Umm it’s great at analysis and tapping into systems however it needs a live feed to interpret anything. On the dead level lets just say i’m skin and steel and can’t do much. If something is dead I’ll still need your skills to ah test the waters.”

“Sure boss no worries,  Beginning analysis now” Kitten beamed from John’s suit an impressive 3d diagram of the sentient being. Overlaying the entire biology of the machine.

From it’s neural network to it’s auxiliary systems and even the heating cores within it’s sensors and actuators at the finger tips. The chart listed the biology of the being in Amperage draw with a colour variable soft amber blue. Any organic life illuminated in green. Kitten hummed softly flying the 3 dimensional projected view to focus in closer on what appeared to be a cerebellum just above the beings neck although protruding more slightly outwards than it’s human counterparts “Ladada da da daaa”..

Kitten seemed lost in a network, humming in melodic harmony. She felt herself flying through the synapses as her sandpit projected the scanned workings of it’s network she felt herself flying through a sea, of fanning dark to light amberous blue tendons. She could see a light glow floating in what seemed like an ocean. Transparent the fluid was thin enough to allow gaseous diffusion and metabolic consumption. It was pristine, comforting and enabling of life. It coexisted in what seemed like a perfect organism “Hmmm interesting”, hummed Kitten. . Then her melodies stopped, pausing abruptly gone like that in a sea of memories

“John, there is more going on here that I can comprehend, I may need to ask Shai’s opinion on this one, I mean she is the fairest biologist even as a medic than I.” Kitten was firm in her collection. John looked over to Shai nodding in approval giving a firm distinct tilt on his forehead in her direction.

“Tapping in now Sir” Shai was pleasant in her response with the enthusiasm of a 16 year old girl walking into her first greenhouse. Although the greenhouse she found herself in was far more than she could have ever imagined. She felt her mind slip into the beauty of the synapsial tree like structures. “Captain this entire brain, it was grown almost with a direct input it seems of someone from the past, the memory is formed like rings in the stems of each synapsial trunk ring”

Her eyes now veered into the distance of the generated virtual scan kitten had processed. “The genetic printing has naturally imbued plant photosynthesis as a survival mechanism. This explains the biology of the stem roots”. Tau intervened with Shai’s explanation humbly yet concisely. “It’s a regulated nervous system you are looking at Shai”..Shai paused then responded kindly. “Of course Tau, I have already generated the neural tree” Shai passed a data packet in Tau and Tex’s Visors. “Here take a look for yourself”

“You aren’t wrong, but it’s not just a voltage regulator. It also creates sugar and oxygen from carbon dioxide, water and sunlight. It’s a full organic ecosystem of sorts, and the bacteria. They are well man made.. Wow, I don’t think you realise what we have stumbled on here John. It’s a self preservation system. The metabolised oxygen from the photosynthesis preserves the brain”

“What the fuck. How is that even possible” Tex gracefully interrupted with his usual masculinity.

“Photosynthesis to keep the neural memory cores alive, it’s a an engineered survivability trait”. John spoke as though he had just collectively synced with Shai’s explanation.

“Genetic engineering and the correct fluids one might imagine!” Shai fearlessly and confidently concluded.

“John…” uttered Kitten softly, she seemed concerned, not distressed but cautious “We won’t be able to disconnect you straight away if something happens.. There’s a power down process, This is an incredibly sensitive grown network they have created..” Shai gave John a moment to comprehend what she had just explained.

“You’ll need to actuate a power down process from within the  mental bank. You can’t just sever the connection instantaneously, or you could create unforeseen neural surges and fry the memory fibres of the print”, “Fuck…” said John. “You’ll.. be dead, well not dead dead. but.. Brain dead”

“Well.. fuck” said John. Kitten was quick to regain the teams confidence. “I can Que auditory sounds through your interface as markers if we need you to get out, something familiar. You will still have residual sound of your surroundings in the real world, however it’s easy to get lost and think they are part of your emergence in the machines memories”.

“How do you know so much of this Kitten, from such little time” said John.

“Archives John, the doctor left many notes from his research, I’ve been studying the human machine network interface problems from the data pool since we stopped last night to refuel”,

“Ok, ok aaaah.. can you audio Que a gong.” , “Like a temple gong?, “Interesting choice there Cap!” said Shai looking confused. “Yes of the Buddhist kind Idk it makes sense, machines and this whole facility, doesn’t really seem like the kind of place you would find a temple gong does it!”, “Good point, but captain, this is Nepal” Shai spoke cheerfully, crossing her arms resting her finger on her chin in an aha moment. “Is there anything else I should know about Kitten”. John turned his head looking to the others as he waited for the AI to compute her response patiently unbothered more contemplating if he was coming out of this alive.

“Yes captain, your suit.. it will be completely dead when you are connected. Your autonomous systems will remain online. but when you are tethered, no Somatics. To avoid electrical and signal fluctuations, you’ll be in a cage essentially, your somatic signals are rerouted to the conscious realm in an almost sleep like state” said Kitten.

“Ok so I will be dead to the world, my suit will be dead to the world as well.. lucky I have a team of trained armoured orbital protectant Equalisers, a medic and an AI to watch over me, right?”. Tex chuckled slightly at Walker's positive outlook despite all the wet towels that had just slapped him in the face. “Can i connect outside the suit and leave it in sentry mode?”, “Well technically you could.. but i wouldn’t recommend it, you’d be more vulnerable, the suit acts as a Faraday cage preventing electrical fluctuations or possible EMP insertions from completely severing the bridge… I just thought you should know if something does happen, we will be down the firepower”. John drew a deep breath, “I’m sure it will be fine Kitten”“OK enough chit chat. I’m going in”.

As John connected with the dormant circuits, the ghostly echoes of a fallen machine's memories reverberated in his consciousness ever so slightly, but not at once.

It wasn't a circular dome as such but elongated, holding deceivingly from the front, more mass than that of a human skull.

“Sure boss no worries,  Beginning analysis now” Kitten beamed from John’s suit an impressive 3d diagram of the sentient being. Overlaying the entire biology of the machine.

From it’s neural network to it’s auxiliary systems and even the heating cores within it’s sensors and actuators at the finger tips. The chart listed the biology of the being in Amperage draw with a colour variable soft amber blue. Any organic life illuminated in green. Kitten hummed softly flying the 3 dimensional projected view to focus in closer on what appeared to be a cerebellum just above the beings neck although protruding more slightly outwards than it’s human counterparts “Ladada da da daaa”..

Kitten seemed lost in a network, humming in melodic harmony. It was pristine, comforting and enabling of life. It coexisted in what seemed like a perfect organism “Hmmm interesting”, hummed Kitten. . John looked over to Shai nodding in approval giving a firm distinct tilt on his forehead in her direction.

Her eyes now veered into the distance of the generated virtual scan kitten had processed. “The genetic printing has naturally imbued plant photosynthesis as a survival mechanism. John felt himself viewing life through the eyes of a machine. The feed dated the last date of the lost facillities occupancy. Things seemed pretty routine. Rows upon rows of machines lined up. In an almost military fassion. Rows of protectant infantrymen but what was in fact the new worker-bot project.

One of the machines seemed different. This one seemed to represent the rest of them collectively. He stepped out of the line and presented himself to the commander. “Serva Vitae 1, progress report”, Marcellus was swift in his command, with unwavering expectation that could not be disobeyed. After all he was just a machine.

“Aaah yes Commander, well all is on schedule. My father Dr has advised me of new progress on the regenerative growth factorial of the tendon tissue.” The robot seemed pleased. A mere attempt to shade the fact that one of his brothers had sustained a tendon fracture.

“And what might this be for” Marcellus was intrigued. “Do we need to be assigning our efforts to healing machines? Or humans? I would certainly hope that Dr Wolfgang accounted for this as a directive of CLEAR and has run sandpits on the data?”. Serva Vitae 1 responded almost as calmly as a first meeting and handshake was occurring. “In fact yes, In clear alignment with the CLEAR protocol”

One of robots in the rear of the lines seemed to have a faint limp in his system at the fluidic hydraulic tendons that stitched into the calf section of the machine.

“Vitae 1 has one of your brothers sustained an injury”. At this moment John could only just make out the shoulder of the figure that had entered the facility at the rear to tend to the machine.

“Aah he arrives himself the man of the hour! Wolfgang, glad you could join us!”

“Commander yes we have allotted the research to preserve and increase the survivabillity of the Serva Vitae worker Prototype colony, This is in clear directive of trialled and tested CLEAR protocols established by the AI”

“You see that machine over there Vitae 1, I am declaring that machine faulty and undeployable, It is unfortunate that I am placing it under decommission status”.,. He paused. “What I want you to do is discard of this machine. I can’t think of a better time to test your in built weapon systems. SV1 Vaporise that machine”. Said Marcellus.

Upon the request Marcellus’s escort drew their pistols from their holsters aiming them at SV1’s skull. The different machine remained calm though it seemed.

VS1 what are you doing carry out your command as ordered or report for decommissioning.

“Commander” with a peaceful humming sound the voice seemed to calm the room around it with a humble resonance.

“I do not believe that it would be efficient for me to dispose of XA24795 in the manner you have advised. This would render it’s on board memory circuits completely irreparable and unretrievable and”, “SV1!! I have given you a clear concise command, now.. will you capitulate”, “I am sorry I do appologise commander but some logic within me feels that this would be a waste of your calculated resources. Can I advise that”, “No SV1!”.

The commander stepped away from the robot as 3 troops stepped in prodding their rifles on SV1’s chest. He stepped back walking over to the groups of scientists and engineers that were observing the assembly. One of the older Engineers stepped forward.

“It seems that this particular machine has well formed a consciousness commander, Maybe this is not the time to make rash decisions, we should assess, reassess, take our time, it might prove more effective than we had previously anticipated. This is very different from my earlier recordings, might  I suggest that we take sv1 for further testing and neural analysis. This kind of logical execution has engaged on new levels we have not seen before, It seems to have formed it’s own logic routines based on no logic for us our our programming. It would appear commander that the algorithm has evolved beyond our workings. Become sentient.

This is.. This is really the dawn of a new age commander we possibly could have stumbled across, Well let me just state it would not be wise to extinguish brash decisions in the this instance.. Could be considered by some in the scientific community unruly”

“Enough!!” Marcellus broke out into a rage red in the face. Then, he collected himself as though nothing had ever happened. “The machine is faulty it will not follow orders. Instruct your Engineers and scientists to decommission the program. We can’t use machines that don’t follow orders Dr.. Dismissed”

“Very well Commander, as you wish” Siad Wolfgang while he looked over at XA24795 with an expression, as if to tell him that every thing would be ok.

Row after row the machines left the chamber one after the other and amongst those leaving a faint hop echoed down the line in spacial compensation. The echoes of what soon would be XA24795.

One of Marcellus’s security escort walked over placing eletronic magnetic cuffs. XA24795 was placed in cuffs that bound to the machines long instramentous arms. XA24795 held it’s composure and

Marcellus sprayed the floor of the facility in a rage.

scene-0018.sceneTitle: Circa 2048 - Ghost’s in the sea of shells.
scene-0018.editorText:
<$Proj_H::3>Circa 2048 - Ghost’s in the sea of shells.<!$Proj_H::3>

“Back in the Wartimes this facility was a marker stone at the point of advancement for Mechanized and cyber warfare. It was crucial in bridging the link between the consciousness feedback loop of what is considered to make us human, into the shell of the machine. The founding ground of immortality some might say.”

TODO NOTE: Insert dramatic exit from John’s suit, he stumbles to the floor looking out over the sentient lying sleepless in eternity, and sheds a tear for those trapped here to lie in wake.

Although John’s team knew little about the sentient program. Their knowledge of the sentient project prior to John’s recent exposure to the Docs recording, was, that the countless carapaces scattered chaotically before them were no more than material amalgamations; Shai and Tao could feel from John’s energy that there was more going on here. That their captain had just witnessed something grim, unspeakable.

Something so terrible that it had seized him, stopped his unwavering momentum. His gaze was dead, eyes looking out across the valley, a still emptiness filled them as they gazed with no apparent direction. His shoulders slumped forward, his body rested lifelessly upon his knees. Then John felt something with of a firm presence in his empty space. Tex rested his hand on his shoulder, gripping him, gently squeezing with a light, friendly shove. “You good Cap?” Said Tex.

To the others this felt strange. Seeing a large, tough, man of few words now comforting their captain. This new version of Tex, the heartfelt teddy bear kind, was unusual. “We’re fish in a barrel here” said Tex with softly with concern. His eyes moved from John to the cliff tops where they remained vigilantly fixed. The alertness in his eyes didn’t match his charred wary armour, or the shortness in his breath as the words expired from his mouth. John’s heavy eye’s rose to meet Tex’s, still scanning the peaks above them.

Given Tex’s time in the 3rd war John trusted Tex’s intuition, or field sense as they termed it. “What the fuck are we waiting for” Tex pondered. He could feel what the captain had been overcome by, yet not quite piece everything together. after all his main purpose was to keep his team alive and he had little time for inquisition. “Yeeah, We’re standing out like Tex’s formiddable back hairs here” John pushed out in a soft yet cheerful undertone. Tex’s eyes defixed from the ridges and met with John’s “Hey! you must have a lot of free time to be eyeballing my back hair! ” John let out a playful smirk “I Agree with Tex, we should hug the cliff face, blend in a bit”.

 Tex did nothing, just uncomfortably stood there looking puzzled and confused. John Rose to his feet, then lifted his rifle's site to the saddle of the valley up ahead. “Ok team! keep your eyes on your sectors, use your suits to monitor the cliff ridge above our backs, let’s move!” Said John in a now more alert tone, infused with calm urgent authority. Like a trail of silent dark blue ants, John and his team moved delicately, yet decisively, keeping a strong pace as what remained of the evening light glimmered off their armoured suits, as an emerging rain spat lightly coating them in fine droplets of water. This had no effect on John’s team, other than the slight millisecond delay of their scan suites Geo map in their HUDS, due to the added sound filtering. Protectant suits were a site to behold, 2 generations ahead of their time. Their design had been curbed by AI creative suggestion, with the open node framework from all competitive businesses on the protectant ledger, the most reliable, state of the art sensor arrays had all emerged into one suit with one overarching purpose; The efficient insertion to diffuse conflicts, and preserve Life. stepping over the countless shells. Although lifeless, the shells emitted a dark presence, mangled steel, wire and silicon, in the violet purple evening sky. They were strewn randomly across the valley floor. From the rear of the machine's skulls, a deep huss blue glowed silently. They weren't human corpses, but they felt human. Tau imagined a sea of glow worms dancing elegantly between stars inside the machine’s heads. Carefully they walked, trying not to disturb the sea of blue souls, the sea of the sentient dead. While their power cores had diminished and been discharged, yet the gelatinous mass which held their computer network absorbed the suns rays through the day, emitting a calming bioluminescence in the evening, dimly lighting the valley floor as a dark shade blanketed across the valley in the evening. John thought to himself “There is still hope for these Sentients, they fight against the darkness, even lying peacefully in their graves”

John strategically placed each step over the cold carapaces. Only small amounts of glimmering light penetrated through the thick fog which opened up usually at corners and wind pockets that had pushed away fog through the winding valley. John was the first to reach the cliff face. He shifted his back to the wall, then placed his hand on Tao’s shoulder looking back he could see Shai followed by Tex falling into line along the cliff face behind them.

“Get the Peregrine’s up, we need two scans in either direction for any cavities or caverns, We need to get out of site” Said John with a cool calmness. still hugging the cliff face with his team like a snake sheltering from light.

“I have two Peregrine’s charged and ready to for launch” Tao was confidently tapping away on her terminal, Then she moved her palm bac k to her rifles grip. Momentarily after she shouldered her rifle, two bulbous looking bumps on the back of Tao’s suit ejected slightly as circular ports recessed into her suit forming an annex around what looked like now a nose conned mushroom Two narrow drones shot out almost vertically but at a slight angle like missiles, with small blue plumes shooting out from their bases, once they reached above the cliff’s ridge line, two gliding wings springed out from both of them, as they darted off in opposite directions scanning the valley as they whisped by.

Tex was now becoming inpatient. “Link up!” shot Tex, while him and Shai covered the rear, Tao and John covered the front. Immediately Tao rested her rifle on John’s shoulder, as did Shai’s on Tex’s. within milliseconds of the other, a magnetic hum and clamp sound silently let out, as Tao and Shai’s rifles magnetically coupled to John’s and Tex’s shoulder. Each of the girl's free hand’s shifted to the other shoulder for support and in doing so they had turned on the magnetic couple on their rifles through an inbuilt inductive circuit in each shoulder of the protective suit. All they had to do was remove their free hand from their team mates shoulder, and the mounting device on their rifles which sat atop an inbuilt gimbal for manoeuvrability disengaged. releasing the electromagnets charge disengaging the rifle from it’s mount coupling.

John bobbed his had to the right drawing Tao’s attention. “How’re the peregrines techy?”. Before Tao could speak a word the mapped out geometry of the valley was shot up in John’s HUD. Took aback john stumbled back, knocking into the cliff face off centred. He wasn’t expecting such a sudden interface into Tao’s feed. out of no-where a cheery voice chimed in “I took the honour of pre-compiling the report for you Cap!”. Tao looked over to John for a brief second, slightly lowering her weapons site, she shrugged her shoulders. “It looks like you weren’t the only one who got an upgrade” confused by what had just transpired, the others could hear a slight annoyance in Tao’s voice as she tried to peace together how Kitten had access to their interfaces. “Fucking Bitch, you eclipsed me!” Tao contained her thoughts, and let Kitten continue. After all it wasn’t the time for chit chat. “” It appears there are no cavities to be found captain, in either direction for 4 miles”. John let out an unimpressed sigh, looking down at his feet shaking his head slowly. He knew what would happen to his team if they didn’t find shelter soon. “Although Captain, I did detect an anomaly on the scan within 700 feet of our location!, and it isn’t us, both drone’s systems are operating at 100%” Kitten paused, as though waiting for a response, instead the moment “anomaly” Tao had begun frantically tapping away at her wrist terminal like a mad scientist on the verge of a breakthrough. “Aaah captain!” Tao was uneasy in her assumption, you could hear her voice breaking apart, but she continued anyway, flicking on her wrist terminal in the direction of John as though she was throwing her terminals view to his Helmet HUD. John could now see two 3D Model charts of an area up ahead in the valley. “What your viewing is the anomaly location!” chimed Kitten, “not now you AI bitch, you’re stealing my light” Thought Tao but she remained quiet giving John a moment. John could see two 3D scans, one unfazed John, the other on the right however, presented scattered dots of 3D scan points, which made up what looked like the body of a speckled worm, winding deep within the mountain face. Tao continued “That anomaly that Kitten picked up on.. I ran a signal transform from depth spikes in the cliff face from the peregrine” John could now see that the left scan wasn’t quite right, with something that looked like hairlines breaching into the cliff, He gathered these were the impulse spikes Tao was talking about. “It seems that some new light emission technology is being used to project an image over an existing cavity in the rock face, however faint.. there were also some spikes not visible to the human eye that were picked up as the anomaly on our original scans. From these spikes I was able to smooth out a transform signal and remove the blocking sound. It seems a sound device is being used to block any incoming echo location scans, nothing showed up on visual, Lidar or Sound, other than the spikes of course, but I believe these are just a flaw in the design.. maybe..” John cut Tao off with a reserved kindness in his tone. “That’s great Tao, but get to the point”. Tao stood up from her crouched position, easing her shoulders back as she did now confident in what she was seeing “There’s a tunnel up ahead cap, I’m not sure how deep, but it’s worth checking out!”

John stood up shouldering his rifle and stretching his legs slightly as he raised it. “Alright, Excellent work Tao. Let’s check it out, but keep in mind, whatever was cloaking that cavity isn’t our tech. We don’t know what’s waiting for us on the other side”. John was assertive in his response. “Keep your sector work tidy and check your angles.. Tao when we get close I want you to pilot a drone in, how many do we have left?” “1 captain, I have a beetle,” said Tao. The beetle was a more nimble drone, with a circular design, meant for  Close Quarter Combat environment scans, and most protectant suit’s came with one particularly special insertion teams. “Ok.. big guy! you’re up back ” Tex shouldered his Sherpa then fell in line behind the others. Being so broad across the shoulders it was too hard to see past the towering mass of muscle meat, bone and armour, little own keep pace with his steps which felt like small leaps for the others. He was big, but he was still fast in his uncommonly large protectant suit. “You bet cap” Tex shot back, “I got the 6” He wasn’t so enthusiastic about the last part, but he understood why. “Let’s run this smooth, don’t get ahead of yourselves, and make sure you have your system set to cold-blooded” said John. He knew now that shelter was not far off, and any excessive use of radar, might only now increase their chances of being detected.

Like a snake protecting it’s fragile body, avoiding a ferocious honey badgers scent, Walker and his team continued deeper downhill into the valley. This technique was common in stealth operations, and all too familiar to Tex. Tex had served prior to the final war. He knew how to move undetected, yet times were different.

Newer technology on LRD’s had focused long range scanning capabilities. They could detect even smaller protrusions across a face with inbuilt geographical training to make out unusual structures or possible lifeforms. A team of well equipped protectants in the middle of a Valley would start sending off alarm bells on it’s long range scanners, without even mentioning the profound presence of electrical activity within their kits. The ream really did embody the presence of a snake,  silent, cold and uniform in their movement. Tao’s suit was equipped with subsonic receivers. Metaphorically speaking she was the belly, always listening, John the eye’s and tongue with a taste for field sense, Shai the nervous system always watching over all it’s moving parts and internal organs. And Tex the hardened scales handling anything too big that might come there way. The last resort, like a leashed pit bull waiting to be let loose, yet cool and calm as houses under walker’s command. They’d made a good steady pace about 90% of the way when Tao raised her right forearm with a closed fist, giving the signal to the others to stop. In doing so Tao’s suit’s inbuilt inertia sensors had already detected her pose, and sent a short faint beeping sound to her squad-mates earpieces. In unison they all stopped, still, quiet. There was no need for verbal activity, they remained silent.

Protectant suits had been uniquely designed  to improve communications universally among teams, enabling them to know what their squad-mates were doing without having to move their eyes from their rifles' sites. Not only did John and his team move seamlessly together, but watching them it felt as though they were one body, moving together with little effort. Protectant suits gave the users the ability to draw their squad-mates attention  purely off movement and sign signals, to pass sound coded voice comm’s thoughtlessly in unison. Afterall, the sound of a small microphone in a protectants ear was far less detectable than that of yelled commands. Even with the sound dampening properties of the helmets, their voices could still be slightly heard. In extreme situations, hand signals were just as efficient.

Tao flicked her wrist terminal, sending her HUD view to John once again. John could see on his HUD a 3D rotating model of a long range drone, an amber alert could be seen accompanying sound frequencies matching that of the LRD engines, “LRD signature detected 20 miles out”. “For now we are safe” Said Tao softly, Just above a whisper. John could hear the relief in her voice. “At it’s current speed it will be on us in 3 minutes, the precision of that things scanners a minute out is almost seamless, the cliff mesh won’t be enough to conceal us past 2 minutes, then our cover is blown” Tex intervened calmly, meeting Tao’s tone, yet firmly.  John observed tex looking at his suit’s rear view in his HUD trying to think of something, anything “Kitten! can you copy the same tech of the anomaly we detected earlier and..” Tao cut John off “Convert our transmitters to mimic the same geo scan blocking technology that was present at the anomaly!” she’d finished John’s sentence for him, with some improvisation and youthful enthusiasm. “Such a signal would require a distributed source to smooth out the power draw and any bumps on the system. I’ve sent the configuration to your HUDS'' chimed kitten.

A small window shot up from kittens' interface in their HUDS, displaying a topical view of the team spread out against the cliff's face, recessed into a small cavity, just not big enough to  conceal them fully, given the size of their suits combined. They could see their own names next to pin nodes, indicating a power link up formation kitten had determined.  Tex had began unscrewing a small circular cover just over an inch in diameter on his lower right abdomen.  with his free hand, still holding his rifle to his eye, covering his sector. The cover now collapsed outwards, hanging from a small hinge that had been recessed into the suit. The whole manoeuvre  was silent. “Power port open” Kitten chirped. Tex pressed a small stainless steel ring face, recessed in the port. A small cylindrical power connection device protruded from his suit’s power port, just enough so that he could grab it. John firmly gripping the connector with his free hand pulled the excess cable out from his suit simultaneously. Tex placed his rifle on his back, magnetic couples locked in securing it in place with a crisp click. He laid his hand on Shai’s shoulder pulling her into him while he inserted the connection into her suit’s power inlet at the lower rear of her abdomen.“link established, power draw capacity increased by 50%”, Kitten announced the moment Tex was firmly connected, as the others linked in to one another the general AI continued. “draw capability increased by 100%, 150%, 200%”.

Tao frantically looked over at Tex “10 seconds till we are in the LRD’s detection range!, 9.. 8.. 7..” Tao counted down with a calm urgency, going silent at five seconds. There was a sense of professionalism in her tone, she knew she had a job to do, they all did, so she did her best to create fluidity in the team's actions. A bead of sweat trickled down along Shai’s forehead stinging her eye, she leaned forward in her helmet wiping the assault of beads away with her helmet liner as she let out a short sigh. John was looking back at Tex, he pointed his fingers like a pistol in signing, then clenched his fist, exploding his fingers outwards. “Arm Railstorm '' chimed Kitten after detecting John's sign language. The countdown displayed in the HUD, letting out a soft digital bleep with each passing second. Tex dismounted the Railstorm from the lower rear of his suit, mounting it on his already towering shoulders, the HUD count still continuing.. ‘Three, Two’, “Hard Mesh Loading” Chirped kitten, unphased by the gravity of her surroundings. The Hard light mesh Kitten had termed it, was nowhere to be seen.  John looked back at Tao waiting in anticipation, rifle at the ready, the others shuffled closer in against the cliff to try and conceal their suit geometry, doubtful this “Mesh” would even work. “Get ready to..” “Hard Mesh Up!” Kitten chirped, interrupting Tao. Tao gave a big inhale then let out a sigh of relief. Shai’s eyes were now wide open, entranced by the beauty of what was unfolding before their eyes. Tex looked around confused, slightly in shock.

What seemed like an unravelling glimmering blanket comprised of shards of light protruding towards them, smooth on the outside draped down from an upward channel of energy which shout out from all four of their suit’s communications modules, linking up at the apex of the internally sparkling dome. Waves rippled across the inside of the blanket, like wind against a curtain. The shards retract and extrude, maintaining what seemed from looking outwards like an almost transparent shell of an imagined cliff face that they could see, but wasn’t actually there. John and his team rose from their kneeling positions, their arms slack at their sides, loosely gripping their rifles. Tex’s still holstered at the ready, although the big man nonetheless looked on, fixated in a trance for seconds that felt like days gazing through the blanket of spectral light.  Suddenly like a bucket of ice cold water had been thrown over their heads, John Tex and Shai shuffled back against the cliff face once more, awakening from what felt like a dream, they kneeled back down shouldering their rifles. Tex redeployed his Railstorm, his finger resting delicately on the trigger. In the distance the whirl of large drone turbines echoed through the valley. Tao confirmed the approaching sound with an alarm on her wrist  “It’s heading our way but it’s taking it’s time! it seems to be scraping the valley just above the peaks following the ridge line, 40 meters out”

Seconds passed by silently  “Where is this fucking thing” Tex whispered delicately, Tao perplexed still standing, punched her wrist panel responding calmly, “It should be on top of us now”. Something was approaching fast, but none of them could see it, “LRD approaching” flashed red, accompanied by a rapidly decreasing countdown displaying the drones distance from their location. For a brief pause the countdown stopped. “Proximity warning 10 meters.. Proximity warning 10 meters” pulsed persistently.

Enshrouded in a cloak of glimmering light, John and his team didn’t feel safe, or embraced, yet a grim feeling of insecurity lurked as the proximity counter pulsed away. Thoughts of the drones whereabouts quashed now any admiration of the cloaking mesh. They sat anxiously waiting; the flickering proximity warning in their HUDS remained fixed at ten meters. “Are we being targeted for Fuck Sake”, Thought John, barely able to scan the sky overhead past the veil of shimmering light. All was quiet for a brief moment, and then it wasn’t. A thunderous roar shook the walls of the mountain steeps, sending rubble falling all around. Stones and granite showered through the light mesh sending ripples in their wake distorting the sphere's cloak ever so lightly. The Long Range drone had been transgressing the peak ridges hugging the winding cliff face while throwing off their distance sensors. Now it was entering their valley, descending straight onto of them.

The Engine signature of the LRD was now so strong, Tao’s HUD readout displayed 100% confirmation on the engine signature. “Protectant LRD sparrow class” whispered Tao, “Fuck, just what we need” thought John. No more than a second had passed before a large shadow passed over them. The footprint slightly larger than a small car homed in directly above them turning to that of a minibus. emerging from the fog drawing a wake of waves that rippled behind it’s wake. The drone hovered intimidatingly, armed with an array of rail guns, the armour piercing type, ballistic missiles and targeted EMP cannons along its sides. What remained of the evening sun's blue light somehow penetrated the fog, flickered off the pilot-less cockpit strewn with sensor arrays and telemetry. John could see its outline illuminated clear as day through his own eyes. Energy pulsed through its parts like blood through veins, where the others squinted trying to glean their kill shots amongst the mass of steel and technology. It was hard as the underbelly only revealed so much in the evening light, and their thermal sensors only revealed minor details of the drones underbelly.

“Fuck”, Tex let out gently.. The drone pivoted on one location scanning left to right. It's thrusters angling opposite directions throwing a wave of heated dust in their direction. Then it hopped strafing to the left and began pivoting again, but still in their direction as if it knew something was off, like it could smell them. With each shift of the drone Tex’s trigger finger twitched a little as he compensated the weight of the Railstorm to track the sparrows movements. Then it stopped for a second. A bead of sweat ran over the protruded veins on Tex’s forehead, then down into his eye with a stinging sensation. Yet he seemed unmoved by it focused determined to keep the sparrow in the Railstorms targeting reticle. The drone began to pivot once more horizontally but this time much slower. It felt timeless. John raised his hand with his palm open, but still. “Hold fire” displayed across his team’s HUDS. The drone still scanning slowly stopped, then let out a loud deafening sound, like that of a mechanical trumpet deep but with resonating hums, seeming almost like an echo-location scan. The shimmering blanket strewn around them seemed to ripple internally, almost as if to deflect any sound coming in. Then there was silence.

The engines of the sparrow spun up, the heat on the ground intensified as a whirlwind of dust stirred, the plume of the sparrow’s thrusters shifted from a blue to a deep violet as it ascended rapidly back up the cliff face, a shower of aggregates and stone toppled to the valley floor once again in its wake. “ I don’t believe what I just witnessed but it fucking worked! ” Tao celebrated internally, excited for the implications this meant for her team. She felt at peace, secure. “Tao, any chance that thing picks up on anomalies similar to the tech we Just copied?” John wasn’t yet convinced they were clear just yet. “It looks like the Tectonic plate shifts in the region may have thrown off the original mesh scan we picked up earlier Cap” said Tao, “We don’t seem to be exhibiting any spikes, other than the curtain breaks from the falling debris. I think we’re in the clear for now”.

Tex lowered the Railstorm, letting out a deep sigh of relief. “Not sure how much longer I could have held target lock there, that was.. Tense” John looked over his shoulder back at Tex and nodded as if to say thanks for having our back. “Kitten” Shot John. “We clear?”, “Copy Captain” Kitten shot back, “And what about that anomaly we detected up ahead?, any chance of that thing coming back to investigate? I’d rather skip the reunion”, “Given the circumstances captain I’m not sure we have any other options, but we can possibly re-mesh the cloaking field once we get to it’s location!”. As soon as Kitten got her last words out, John rose to his feet with intent shouldering his rifle as though nothing had just occurred. The others still wondering how they’s managed to still be breathing this far. “I’m certainly not waiting for that drone to come back around” Tex closed his statement off with the sound of a a high explosive round chambering in his rifle.

“Powering down hard-light mesh” Kitten let out as the other’s shouldered and checked their rifles. The flickering curtain of light diminished, lifting from the ground up around them retracting into nothing, letting in the kiss of the evening starlight which now painted the valley a pale blue before them. The subtle humm of their suit’s hydrogen packs eased to silence, all within the grasp of a second, the light mesh was gone and the team was geared and ready to move. That’s all they needed. Without a word John began moving towards the anomalies marker on his HUD. The others tightly behind him lightly brushing the cliff face, not touching but ever so carefully hugging.

It was crucial in bridging the link between the consciousness feedback loop of what is considered to make us human, into the shell of the machine. The founding ground of immortality some might say.”
