He laid his hand on Shai’s shoulder pulling her into him while he inserted the connection into her suit’s power inlet at the lower rear of her abdomen.“link established, power draw capacity increased by 50%”, Kitten announced the moment Tex was firmly connected, as the others linked in to one another the general AI continued. “draw capability increased by 100%, 150%, 200%”.

Tao frantically looked over at Tex “10 seconds till we are in the LRD’s detection range!, 9.. 8.. 7..” Tao counted down with a calm urgency, going silent at five seconds. There was a sense of professionalism in her tone, she knew she had a job to do, they all did, so she did her best to create fluidity in the team's actions. A bead of sweat trickled down along Shai’s forehead stinging her eye, she leaned forward in her helmet wiping the assault of beads away with her helmet liner as she let out a short sigh. John was looking back at Tex, he pointed his fingers like a pistol in signing, then clenched his fist, exploding his fingers outwards. “Arm Railstorm '' chimed Kitten after detecting John's sign language. The countdown displayed in the HUD, letting out a soft digital bleep with each passing second. Tex dismounted the Railstorm from the lower rear of his suit, mounting it on his already towering shoulders, the HUD count still continuing.. ‘Three, Two’, “Hard Mesh Loading” Chirped kitten, unphased by the gravity of her surroundings. The Hard light mesh Kitten had termed it, was nowhere to be seen.  John looked back at Tao waiting in anticipation, rifle at the ready, the others shuffled closer in against the cliff to try and conceal their suit geometry, doubtful this “Mesh” would even work. “Get ready to..” “Hard Mesh Up!” Kitten chirped, interrupting Tao. Tao gave a big inhale then let out a sigh of relief. Shai’s eyes were now wide open, entranced by the beauty of what was unfolding before their eyes. Tex looked around confused, slightly in shock.

What seemed like an unravelling glimmering blanket comprised of shards of light protruding towards them, smooth on the outside draped down from an upward channel of energy which shout out from all four of their suit’s communications modules, linking up at the apex of the internally sparkling dome. Waves rippled across the inside of the blanket, like wind against a curtain. The shards retract and extrude, maintaining what seemed from looking outwards like an almost transparent shell of an imagined cliff face that they could see, but wasn’t actually there. John and his team rose from their kneeling positions, their arms slack at their sides, loosely gripping their rifles. Tex’s still holstered at the ready, although the big man nonetheless looked on, fixated in a trance for seconds that felt like days gazing through the blanket of spectral light.  Suddenly like a bucket of ice cold water had been thrown over their heads, John Tex and Shai shuffled back against the cliff face once more, awakening from what felt like a dream, they kneeled back down shouldering their rifles. Tex redeployed his Railstorm, his finger resting delicately on the trigger. In the distance the whirl of large drone turbines echoed through the valley. Tao confirmed the approaching sound with an alarm on her wrist  “It’s heading our way but it’s taking it’s time! it seems to be scraping the valley just above the peaks following the ridge line, 40 meters out”

Seconds passed by silently  “Where is this fucking thing” Tex whispered delicately, Tao perplexed still standing, punched her wrist panel responding calmly, “It should be on top of us now”. Something was approaching fast, but none of them could see it, “LRD approaching” flashed red, accompanied by a rapidly decreasing countdown displaying the drones distance from their location. For a brief pause the countdown stopped. “Proximity warning 10 meters.. Proximity warning 10 meters” pulsed persistently.

Enshrouded in a cloak of glimmering light, John and his team didn’t feel safe, or embraced, yet a grim feeling of insecurity lurked as the proximity counter pulsed away. Thoughts of the drones whereabouts quashed now any admiration of the cloaking mesh. They sat anxiously waiting; the flickering proximity warning in their HUDS remained fixed at ten meters. “Are we being targeted for Fuck Sake”, Thought John, barely able to scan the sky overhead past the veil of shimmering light. All was quiet for a brief moment, and then it wasn’t. A thunderous roar shook the walls of the mountain steeps, sending rubble falling all around. Stones and granite showered through the light mesh sending ripples in their wake distorting the sphere's cloak ever so lightly. The Long Range drone had been transgressing the peak ridges hugging the winding cliff face while throwing off their distance sensors. Now it was entering their valley, descending straight onto of them.

The Engine signature of the LRD was now so strong, Tao’s HUD readout displayed 100% confirmation on the engine signature. “Protectant LRD sparrow class” whispered Tao, “Fuck, just what we need” thought John. No more than a second had passed before a large shadow passed over them. The footprint slightly larger than a small car homed in directly above them turning to that of a minibus. emerging from the fog drawing a wake of waves that rippled behind it’s wake. The drone hovered intimidatingly, armed with an array of rail guns, the armour piercing type, ballistic missiles and targeted EMP cannons along its sides. What remained of the evening sun's blue light somehow penetrated the fog, flickered off the pilot-less cockpit strewn with sensor arrays and telemetry. John could see its outline illuminated clear as day through his own eyes. Energy pulsed through its parts like blood through veins, where the others squinted trying to glean their kill shots amongst the mass of steel and technology. It was hard as the underbelly only revealed so much in the evening light, and their thermal sensors only revealed minor details of the drones underbelly.

“Fuck”, Tex let out gently.. The drone pivoted on one location scanning left to right. It's thrusters angling opposite directions throwing a wave of heated dust in their direction. Then it hopped strafing to the left and began pivoting again, but still in their direction as if it knew something was off, like it could smell them. With each shift of the drone Tex’s trigger finger twitched a little as he compensated the weight of the Railstorm to track the sparrows movements. Then it stopped for a second. A bead of sweat ran over the protruded veins on Tex’s forehead, then down into his eye with a stinging sensation. Yet he seemed unmoved by it focused determined to keep the sparrow in the Railstorms targeting reticle. The drone began to pivot once more horizontally but this time much slower. It felt timeless. John raised his hand with his palm open, but still. “Hold fire” displayed across his team’s HUDS. The drone still scanning slowly stopped, then let out a loud deafening sound, like that of a mechanical trumpet deep but with resonating hums, seeming almost like an echo-location scan. The shimmering blanket strewn around them seemed to ripple internally, almost as if to deflect any sound coming in. Then there was silence.

The engines of the sparrow spun up, the heat on the ground intensified as a whirlwind of dust stirred, the plume of the sparrow’s thrusters shifted from a blue to a deep violet as it ascended rapidly back up the cliff face, a shower of aggregates and stone toppled to the valley floor once again in its wake. “ I don’t believe what I just witnessed but it fucking worked! ” Tao celebrated internally, excited for the implications this meant for her team. She felt at peace, secure. “Tao, any chance that thing picks up on anomalies similar to the tech we Just copied?” John wasn’t yet convinced they were clear just yet. “It looks like the Tectonic plate shifts in the region may have thrown off the original mesh scan we picked up earlier Cap” said Tao, “We don’t seem to be exhibiting any spikes, other than the curtain breaks from the falling debris. I think we’re in the clear for now”.

Tex lowered the Railstorm, letting out a deep sigh of relief. “Not sure how much longer I could have held target lock there, that was.. Tense” John looked over his shoulder back at Tex and nodded as if to say thanks for having our back. “Kitten” Shot John. “We clear?”, “Copy Captain” Kitten shot back, “And what about that anomaly we detected up ahead?, any chance of that thing coming back to investigate? I’d rather skip the reunion”, “Given the circumstances captain I’m not sure we have any other options, but we can possibly re-mesh the cloaking field once we get to it’s location!”. As soon as Kitten got her last words out, John rose to his feet with intent shouldering his rifle as though nothing had just occurred. The others still wondering how they’s managed to still be breathing this far. “I’m certainly not waiting for that drone to come back around” Tex closed his statement off with the sound of a a high explosive round chambering in his rifle.

“Powering down hard-light mesh” Kitten let out as the other’s shouldered and checked their rifles. The flickering curtain of light diminished, lifting from the ground up around them retracting into nothing, letting in the kiss of the evening starlight which now painted the valley a pale blue before them. The subtle humm of their suit’s hydrogen packs eased to silence, all within the grasp of a second, the light mesh was gone and the team was geared and ready to move. That’s all they needed. Without a word John began moving towards the anomalies marker on his HUD. The others tightly behind him lightly brushing the cliff face, not touching but ever so carefully hugging.

scene-0019.chapterTitle: Chapter 3: Synaptic Memoriam of a steel fossil shell
scene-0019.editorText:
“Captain, the cavity is just up ahead, 20 meters out”. John slowed his pace to a quiet walk upon Tao’s announcement, the others meeting his pace. They were silent, rolling their feet onto the ground as they walked so no sudden cracks from the rock bed beneath them might announce their presence. Their suit’s heel’s articulated with every tendon’s pull and ease. “2 meters” Tao whispered. John looked ahead but saw nothing. He wasn’t surprised though given what had just transpired. He knew the technology's capabilities. “It should be right here” Tao’s words gently flowed from her mouth as heat expelled from her helmet’s exhaust vents. A cold wind rose from silence stirring around them, a small howl erupted, ripping through the valley stirring up snow from the ground, shedding any stray icicles to thin from the cliff's face.

“Our suit’s power reserves cores have been exhausted, We won’t last much longer out here in the cold”. In response John raised his hand to hip height, his fingers splayed out level with the ground. He was silent, still, the others waited with anticipation. He took two more steps closer still with his left shoulder to the cliff face. He raised his rifle barrel then poked the cliff face with his rifle muzzle, although as he suspected his muzzle didn’t meet the sound of crunching steel against rock, but the soft static crackle that he had heard when the debris fell through their own Mesh. His muzzle dipped into the cliff like a stick in a still pool of water. “This is it” John stepped back, ice crushing beneath his heel as his weight sunk into the piling snow. “Your up techy!”,

Tau knelt down into the snow crushing it beneath her,gleaning into her wrist terminal. “Prepping echo” She took a moment to think then began tapping away again “Annnnd.. that should do it!” her voice seemed a little less confident this time but confident enough. “Confirm flight plan” pulsed on her wrist terminal. “What’s the hold up” said John “I needed to set a recorded flight path for the time I’ll pilot it manually through the Mesh. Once on the other side I’ll lose comms due to the sound barrier, it will finish it’s scan then return to the recorded flight paths final origin then exit, I just threw the vectors in reverse so it comes out when comes back to the other side of the Mesh. “Oo k” Said John, pretending to understand. “it should stop recording a second after it enters the mesh or loses comms either way we will get her back” Tao seemed more confident now she had reassured herself it seemed. Shai looked back at Tex, Tex shrugged his shoulders.

“Deploying Echo” Tao moved smoothly in her actions. From the rear of her suit’s shoulder blade, the same port the peregrine had ejected from slid open, each blade which formed the port window retracting within the suit’s armoured shell. Everything about the port seal had been carefully crafted. The edges of the seal blades pushed outward against the edge of the next blade, meaning that any positive pressure from within the suit would force a seal in a vacuum environment, making it user friendly in space. Shai found her confidence in the Mark IV increasing as she observed the intricate operation. Before John had even given a thought to what could possibly lie behind the mesh, a light whisper hummed over his shoulder. A small drone no larger than the size of a rhinoceros beetle buzzed past vanishing into the mesh consumed by the cliff face as the ripples from it’s wake dissipated in microseconds into an illusion. To the human eye the small glitch in the mesh couldn’t be seen. Only visible really by the high frequency echo location scanners performed by sonic sensors. A trained engineer might pick up on the pattern, although to anyone else.. it appeared merely as instrument sound without proper curve fitting transforms. Tao had proven this earlier. The inbuilt autopilot program of the Echo had not been designed to detect these “light mesh” instances yet alone pass through them.

“I’ve lost contact with the drone”, said Tao tapping away on her terminal, her suit activating sentry mode as she became occupied with the task ahead. “What’s the hold up” John was getting impatient, “We wait for the data link when it gets back”, “How”, Tao intervened “I’d say a minute at most”. Tex and Shai were huddled together up against the cliff face. “Starting to Prune up in this Dam suit” Tex groaned moving in discomfort. “Big guy wants some action” Chuckled Shai softly under her voice.

“Careful what you wish for”. Tao had a certain unease in her tone, her head fixed still in her wrist terminal. “My suits long range scanners have picked up the engine signature of the LRD from earlier” This time she was less calm, but still controlled. “Persistent fucker!” Said John, “I thought we shook that thing already”, “It’s Engineer probably picked up on the impulse anomaly I detected earlier” Tao flicked her HUD view to the others. “It’s turned around for a second run, heading our way”

“We’re sitting ducks here”, Said John as he nodded over at Tex triggering him to reach for his Railstorm. “Power reserve for hard light mesh will only give us about 10 seconds of concealment Cap” Kitten had understood the stress in John’s tone anticipating his question before he’d even asked.

the charging of coils let out a winding high pitched humm. Tex mounted the Railstorm on his shoulder. His eyes fixated through the targeting reticle on the ridge lying in wait for the drone’s return run.

“20 seconds John till we’re in short range scanners”. Tau seemed calm more than the others. “I think I’d rather take my chances with what's on the other side”, said John, “Second that” said Tex, still with his sites locked on the ridge above. A second later a crackling static let out startling John. He stood back locking his sites on the the ripples of where echo had just zipped out of. Echo had emerged from the mesh unscathed, it stopped, pivoted on it’s axis then headed straight towards Tau. Like a friendly companion it tapped it’s docking bay on the back of her suit then re-coupled with it’s landing arm. The arm drew the drone back into Tau’s suit ready to be deployed again. “Collating the data, I need a few seconds”. “Get it done” John seemed collected, but you could hear the grinding in his tone alone. A frustration of silence lingered among the others as tension built in the air. “The structure inside seems natural but.. scans picked up heartbeat harmonics of a life-form..  it appears to be.. human”. John turned his head to Shai, confused more than concerned “I’ll take my chances with a human over an assault Drone”. John’s rifle muzzle dipped into the cliff wall like a like a drop entering a pool. ripples rose up humming from the entry point with a wave of crackling static. As he stepped through the mesh his body gradually disappeared swallowed by the cliff face leaving behind a silent wisp. The static crackling stopped.

Tao, Shai and Tex all filed in behind where John had just entered, Tex walking backwards letting the suit’s suggested kinematics pairing with Shai. The formed retreat closed out the sky ridges tightly as Tex’s shoulder turrets watched in opposing directions gyrating along the walls seamlessly. The hum down of Tex’s Railstorm cells brought the tunnel to a silence. Charged hydrogen focused light beams packed enough electrons in the punch to disable any incoming drone within milliseconds. Tao had worked on the development of the charging system herself, although she kept this to herself.

Shai was busy looking at her HUD’s life form signatures within their proximity watching for any unwanted visitors. “John, that life form echo picked up I’m running it through the computer”, “That LRD will be at the mesh by now not far behind us” said Tau abruptly. “We should keep moving” said John. “We don’t know how, inquisitive our old friend will be”. He raised his sites moving forward in a smooth motion. After a few steps into the tunnels depths a beam of red light shot out scanning the wall directly in front of him, his armours outline shadowed on the wall within the scan print, Whatever it was, he was in it’s sites, he knew this It wasn’t his rifles targeting laser or any of the others scanning arrays it was too large. John stopped dead in his tracks taking to the ground immediately. “Take cover!” The red cone of lasers flickered past him deeper into the tunnel. John turned around on the ground, aiming his sites at the direction of the tunnel entrance. An explosion erupted through the cave sending rocks and debris on his back and pummelling directly into the others who were now huddled against the tunnel walls where what small crevasses offered minimal protection. John didn’t hesitate, returning fire at the large metallic monstrosities sensor dish. Sparks flew from the drone around it’s shell as what remained of it’s rear slowly emerged through the hard light mesh. The heavily armoured assault sparrow forced it’s way deeper scraping the tunnel walls in it’s wake to the sound of grinding steel and rock. “It must have detected the curtain breaks in the mesh when we entered the cave” shouted Tau.

They had nowhere to go. If they stepped out that would be the end. John’s shoulder turrets were both firing rapidly, sending a barrage of fire at the drone scattering any proper reading it could make out ahead. “I can only suppress it for so long, it’s armour is too thick… Tex!” Shouted John. Tex  reached back over his shoulder and retrieved his Storm Rail. He clenching his fist around the Storm rail’s handle waiting for a break in the curtain of fire. “Hold fire” Kitten chimed in an almost complete calm monotone pleasantly easing the tension as John and his team regained their focus. The LRD was at a stand still, re-priming it’s cannon, echoes of charging wires hummed through the tunnel.  The sound of Tex’s Railstorm charging had complimented that of the Drones, He wouldn’t let it have a chance to open fire again. Collected he stepped out with the drone clear in his Storm Rail’s site. His would sing first and have the final clap as it’s coils let out a loud clap through the tunnel behind him.

The drone shuddered in it’s place moving from side to side crashing into the walls, disoriented  like a drunken belter trying to find his way home from the star bar. It moaned in electronic groans and splutters, as it’s main turret powered down.

“It still has it’s kinetic turret!” Tau was trying to contain herself, sweat ran down her forehead as the held back the images from her blown apart comrades that took blows from rail rifles in the previous war. It wasn’t pretty watching your closest friend be ripped in two, their organs splayed out on the ground by a 12 inch thick iron slug leaving an unscheduled painting along the hull of an Icarus. She knew that while they might survive most shock penetrations now with the new suit’s built nervous network, in the moment they would not be able to recover to finish the job.

“It’s video feeds are disabled but I’m still picking up a sounding scan”, Tau held her breath, speaking quietly. Their Mark IV suit’s dampened out any internal sounds, but instinct still took over as though they were hiding their frail exposed bodies, Shai turned her attention to her heartbeat scanner heightening the tension in her voice. “Aah guys, that life form I picked up earlier it’s getting closer, it’s coming from the other side of the tunnel, We’ll be pinched”. Tex began reaching for a slug to load into the Railstorm’s kinetic chamber. “Whatever it is, it’s not going to like what I’ve got in store”, “Stay where you are Tex! That drone can still turn you to pink mist!” said Tau frantically, Tex chambered the slug in his Storm rail then hugged his back hard up against the tunnel wall.

“The signal.. it appears to be human”, Said Shai. She looked up at Tex from the other side of the tunnel, her voice edged mixed with relief to confusion. “It’s… it’s getting closer, 20 meters and closing on our 6”. John remained fixed in position, prone his sites perched still fixed on the drones direction. His shoulder turret pivoted 180 degrees covering the rear of the tunnel behind them. “I got it covered, we have bigger problems right now, focus on that fucking drone…” Said John.

Everything was quiet, awkwardly quiet. The Sparrow hovered vigilantly, fixed, waiting for a positive read to be picked up on one of John’s team. “It’s operating on Autopilot” Tau began to explain but more for herself than anything “It must have lost contact with command when it crossed the mesh barrier” She whispered, then the tunnel fell to silence once more. The walls began to vibrate and hum, like the mountain was becoming alive, gently. A loud thud shook the tunnel sending rubble and debris clamouring over their armoured suit’s. An ensemble of metallic clangs as their suit’s took the grunt of the falling debris announced their positions even more.

“It’s trying to echo-locate us!” said John. “Fuck this!” said Tex, reluctant to stand there like a rabbit in the headlight. They all knew the sparrow would soon determine their positions with it’s advanced AI, differentiating the sound of rubble against steel would be no hard feat. Tex had waited long enough in his mind, He selected the highest charge possible on the Rail Storm, and listened to the purr of the  coils as they began to prime, just enough, then kneeled down in the open of the tunnel, Storm Rail at the ready, converging his targeting reticle on the sparrows main processing unit. “Covering Fire!” yelled John. Instantly Tau pivoted from the left side of the tunnel just off to the front left of Tex raising her rifle as she did in a smooth motion. The spacing was tight between them, with just enough opening for John to lay down fire between Tex and Tau, an unconventional and completely unorthodox manoeuvre by any training standard, but what choice did they have?

A barrage of fire opened up toward the Sparrow as soon as John had gave the order. Sparks of splintering, hot molten amber ricochet off the armour cladded drone as John and Taus Sherpa rounds did nothing to damage the drone. It was akin to throwing sand in the face of the schoolyard bully, only delaying a heavy handed punch to the face. The sparrows sensor arrays lit up, overwhelmed by molten rain, it’s scans became completely useless. Tex watched on anxiously, as the Storm Rail hummed while it charged for it’s next shot, seconds felt like days, as he willed the last bar of the charge gauge in his HUD to green light him so he could let all hell loose. Tex’s sights finally fixed their lock on the target with a lock. Meanwhile Shai observed the sparrows targeting lasers track up along his chest, but the reticle didn’t stop there; it kept rising up past Tex, past John, flickering through the billowing fog deeper into the tunnel where a deep recessed void appeared that hadn’t been there before.

“Storm Rail Charged” strobed in the top left of Tex’s HUD, Suddenly in a bright unison flash of blue and amber, the tunnel walls lit up in rapid succession. Blinding the others from both directions within milliseconds of the other. The Sparrow let loose it’s Kinetic rifle, Tex steadfast in his firing stance arched back slightly as a thick metal slug left the Storm-rails barrel. A tight crisp cloud of steam tailing it’s trail.

Tex felt a  percussive ripple fly through his suit, sending tingles down his spine. A scattered shock wave belted through the tunnel with a deafening disorienting effect. Adrenaline coursed through his body, sending tingles down his veins from head to toe. Tex closed his eyes, and thought of what it would be like to die, imagining the emptiness of it. He knew if he’d failed in his shot, the others wouldn’t stand a chance. He thought he was done for anyway, so he took the risk to save them, and he found comfort knowing they might make it out alive.

The Sparrow let out a howling bionic scream, jumbled static mixed with corrosive high pitched piezoelectric buzzing, gnawed at their skulls, seamlessly bypassing their suit’s built in decibel filters.

It stumbled uncontrollably, it’s steaming railgun aimlessly spinning about flagging the others in the process, snapped and twisted against the tunnel walls into spaghetti as it thrashed about helplessly. Eventually it plummeted into rock and snow sending debris flying deeper into the tunnel peppering it’s targets.

Tau gritted her teeth as she tweaked settings desperately to block out the frequencies. Finally the buzzing stopped, their ears still ringing with tinnitus as they reoriented. A softening static slipped from the tunnel as the machines last hum whispered down into the cold embracing of silence. For a split moment it felt like as though a ghost had escaped from its now lifeless armour cladded shell. It now laid peacefully blocking the tunnel entrance behind it.

Tex’s Storm-rail still had steam billowing from it’s glowing muzzle as it slowly found it’s resting place down his chest. His body like a ragdoll fell forward powerless, caught in a kneeling cradle hunched over his forward knee as he tried to move, but he felt no response. He could think of doing it, but his body remained still. His heavy head followed his chest dropping forward resting to the side against the shaft of the cooling Storm-rail. He gazed down at the ground, his thoughts began to wander aimlessly. The monstrosity clad in his oversized suit's thick armour knelt dead still, like a statue in the middle of the tunnel. The atmosphere from the entrance of the tunnel propelled forward like a small wave from the sparrows' impact. the waves of mist clashed around Tex, settling like a resting pool of fog by a sleeping obelisk, it rippled along his calves, kissing his lifeless hands gently. “Tex!!” A tear forced its way out of Shai’s eye straddling the bottom of her eye lid, filled with the internal blue glow from within her helmet, a small galaxy seemed to flicker within it as all the body functions of her teammates pulsed in a barrage of information. She wasn’t checking them, She wasn’t thinking, she was in a sea of rage and sorrow.

With Shai preoccupied and John still covering the front, Tau looked back through the thick fog at the rear of the tunnel. A burning blue glow caressed her gaze drawing her in. “John” Tau whispered  slowly, easing her way deeper toward the void. “There is something..” she switched her HUD to thermals “someone..  behind us”. “Get it together Shai” said John with sharp authority.

“OK, ok, ok cap”, Shai collected herself and began checking Tex’s vitals through her HUD. “I’m still picking up neural activity but it’s limited to involuntary functions, he’s still breathing”. John closed his eyes with a sigh of relief. “It’s locked in syndrome, His neural link was disconnected impromptu… from an EMP charge..” Said Shai.  “We took out that things fucking EMP!”, John’s voice tremored, he had done this as routine, he clawed in his mind at the possibility of a storm rail critical misfunction. “I’m tapping into his suit and initiating an emergency reboot”. Shai, was beginning to gain composure again.

Tex, groaned, moaning in discomfort, his eyes rolling from the back of his skull back to their resting place, druel dripped from his bottom lip. His jawline twitched as he observed a notification pulsing in his HUD. “Reboot initiated”. He felt the life pouring into the back of his neck like freezing water, then his shoulders, arms, torso, legs and eventually his toes. His body ached and burned buzzing and twitching, like a bed of needles pierced his soul as he urged himself forward, One knee up, then the next  he raised himself in agony from the ground.

“What the fuck..” Tex’s groaned in annoyance, as he locked his jaw back and forth regaining voluntary muscle control.. “That Sparrow take down … Nice work! I didn’t even hit the darn thing, I lost control of my arms just as I pulled the trigger,” his eyes drifted from what remained of a steaming splintered hulking wreck of the sparrow. His eyes climbed their way up the tunnels edge, eventually to find a watermelon sized cavity his stray shot had carved, the slug or what remained of it sitting proud in the middle of it. The cavity sat proud just above where the sparrow once hovered before it had dramatically met it’s end.

“Johnnn!!” Tau croaked with annoyance still trying to edge his attention. She had made her way to the rear of Tunnel, “You’re going to want to see this.” the sound of crushing ice and stone beneath her boots turned to a metallic thud. She knelt down, running her fingers through the ice and ruble to reveal an unnatural metallic floor.

Tex, realizing as his senses came too he was the only heavy gunner in the squad, turned about face throwing his storm-rail back on his shoulder it’s reticle now locked directly on the void. Silence took a hold of them as they locked sites at the end of the tunnel in anticipation. Slowly, a falling belly of fog and steam spilled endlessly through a wall that seemed to breathe. By now the blue glow that had drawn Tau in had diminished to nothing.

Suddenly a belly of fog and steam hurled toward them from as the breathing wall gave way, scattering their sensors and vision. A cloak field like that at the face of the cliff powered down revealing an unnatural structure behind it, seemingly organic yet also steel.

 They could hardly believe what they were seeing. An EMP cannon the size of a minibus had been hidden within the tunnel. It’s positioning  well planned. A defensive vantage point overlooking the tunnels opening, encapsulated behind a seamless cloaked wall with only an opening small enough to allow for the Cannons muzzle to sit ever so proudly, concealed behind the cloaking field which was no more.

The electric hum that had taken them by surprise eased down to a whispering static. Something was moving behind the turret, seated at it’s control centre. Immediately rifle sites raised at the mysterious figure to the rear of the cannon as they hugged the walls of the void closing distance between them.

“Waaaa hooooo!!, I’ve been waiting to use this bad boy for over a century now!”, A joyous victory chant filled the tunnel with a voice slightly inorganic. At John’s direction the others lowered their arms, Tex’s rifle still slightly raised untrusting. “A century yet before this cowboy leaves town you protectant genocidal bastards you!” Tau look

Once on the other side I’ll lose comms due to the sound barrier, it will finish it’s scan then return to the recorded flight paths final origin then exit, I just threw the vectors in reverse so it comes out when comes back to the other side of the Mesh. “Oo k” Said John, pretending to understand. “it should stop recording a second after it enters the mesh or loses comms either way we will get her back” Tao seemed more confident now she had reassured herself it seemed. Shai looked back at Tex, Tex shrugged his shoulders.

“Deploying Echo” Tao moved smoothly in her actions. From the rear of her suit’s shoulder blade, the same port the peregrine had ejected from slid open, each blade which formed the port window retracting within the suit’s armoured shell. Everything about the port seal had been carefully crafted. The edges of the seal blades pushed outward against the edge of the next blade, meaning that any positive pressure from within the suit would force a seal in a vacuum environment, making it user friendly in space. Shai found her confidence in the Mark IV increasing as she observed the intricate operation. Before John had even given a thought to what could possibly lie behind the mesh, a light whisper hummed over his shoulder. A small drone no larger than the size of a rhinoceros beetle buzzed past vanishing into the mesh consumed by the cliff face as the ripples from it’s wake dissipated in microseconds into an illusion. To the human eye the small glitch in the mesh couldn’t be seen. Only visible really by the high frequency echo location scanners performed by sonic sensors. A trained engineer might pick up on the pattern, although to anyone else.. it appeared merely as instrument sound without proper curve fitting transforms. Tao had proven this earlier. The inbuilt autopilot program of the Echo had not been designed to detect these “light mesh” instances yet alone pass through them.

“I’ve lost contact with the drone”, said Tao tapping away on her terminal, her suit activating sentry mode as she became occupied with the task ahead. “What’s the hold up” John was getting impatient, “We wait for the data link when it gets back”, “How”, Tao intervened “I’d say a minute at most”. Tex and Shai were huddled together up against the cliff face. “Starting to Prune up in this Dam suit” Tex groaned moving in discomfort. “Big guy wants some action” Chuckled Shai softly under her voice.

“Careful what you wish for”. Tao had a certain unease in her tone, her head fixed still in her wrist terminal. “My suits long range scanners have picked up the engine signature of the LRD from earlier” This time she was less calm, but still controlled. “Persistent fucker!” Said John, “I thought we shook that thing already”, “It’s Engineer probably picked up on the impulse anomaly I detected earlier” Tao flicked her HUD view to the others. “It’s turned around for a second run, heading our way”

“We’re sitting ducks here”, Said John as he nodded over at Tex triggering him to reach for his Railstorm. “Power reserve for hard light mesh will only give us about 10 seconds of concealment Cap” Kitten had understood the stress in John’s tone anticipating his question before he’d even asked.

the charging of coils let out a winding high pitched humm. Tex mounted the Railstorm on his shoulder. His eyes fixated through the targeting reticle on the ridge lying in wait for the drone’s return run.

“20 seconds John till we’re in short range scanners”. Tau seemed calm more than the others. “I think I’d rather take my chances with what's on the other side”, said John, “Second that” said Tex, still with his sites locked on the ridge above. A second later a crackling static let out startling John. He stood back locking his sites on the the ripples of where echo had just zipped out of. Echo had emerged from the mesh unscathed, it stopped, pivoted on it’s axis then headed straight towards Tau. Like a friendly companion it tapped it’s docking bay on the back of her suit then re-coupled with it’s landing arm. The arm drew the drone back into Tau’s suit ready to be deployed again. “Collating the data, I need a few seconds”. “Get it done” John seemed collected, but you could hear the grinding in his tone alone. A frustration of silence lingered among the others as tension built in the air. “The structure inside seems natural but.. scans picked up heartbeat harmonics of a life-form..  it appears to be.. human”. John turned his head to Shai, confused more than concerned “I’ll take my chances with a human over an assault Drone”. John’s rifle muzzle dipped into the cliff wall like a like a drop entering a pool. ripples rose up humming from the entry point with a wave of crackling static. As he stepped through the mesh his body gradually disappeared swallowed by the cliff face leaving behind a silent wisp. The static crackling stopped.

Tao, Shai and Tex all filed in behind where John had just entered, Tex walking backwards letting the suit’s suggested kinematics pairing with Shai. The formed retreat closed out the sky ridges tightly as Tex’s shoulder turrets watched in opposing directions gyrating along the walls seamlessly. The hum down of Tex’s Railstorm cells brought the tunnel to a silence. Charged hydrogen focused light beams packed enough electrons in the punch to disable any incoming drone within milliseconds. Tao had worked on the development of the charging system herself, although she kept this to herself.

Shai was busy looking at her HUD’s life form signatures within their proximity watching for any unwanted visitors. “John, that life form echo picked up I’m running it through the computer”, “That LRD will be at the mesh by now not far behind us” said Tau abruptly. “We should keep moving” said John. “We don’t know how, inquisitive our old friend will be”. He raised his sites moving forward in a smooth motion. After a few steps into the tunnels depths a beam of red light shot out scanning the wall directly in front of him, his armours outline shadowed on the wall within the scan print, Whatever it was, he was in it’s sites, he knew this It wasn’t his rifles targeting laser or any of the others scanning arrays it was too large. John stopped dead in his tracks taking to the ground immediately. “Take cover!” The red cone of lasers flickered past him deeper into the tunnel. John turned around on the ground, aiming his sites at the direction of the tunnel entrance. An explosion erupted through the cave sending rocks and debris on his back and pummelling directly into the others who were now huddled against the tunnel walls where what small crevasses offered minimal protection. John didn’t hesitate, returning fire at the large metallic monstrosities sensor dish. Sparks flew from the drone around it’s shell as what remained of it’s rear slowly emerged through the hard light mesh. The heavily armoured assault sparrow forced it’s way deeper scraping the tunnel walls in it’s wake to the sound of grinding steel and rock. “It must have detected the curtain breaks in the mesh when we entered the cave” shouted Tau.

They had nowhere to go. If they stepped out that would be the end. John’s shoulder turrets were both firing rapidly, sending a barrage of fire at the drone scattering any proper reading it could make out ahead. “I can only suppress it for so long, it’s armour is too thick… Tex!” Shouted John. Tex  reached back over his shoulder and retrieved his Storm Rail. He clenching his fist around the Storm rail’s handle waiting for a break in the curtain of fire. “Hold fire” Kitten chimed in an almost complete calm monotone pleasantly easing the tension as John and his team regained their focus. The LRD was at a stand still, re-priming it’s cannon, echoes of charging wires hummed through the tunnel.  The sound of Tex’s Railstorm charging had complimented that of the Drones, He wouldn’t let it have a chance to open fire again. Collected he stepped out with the drone clear in his Storm Rail’s site. His would sing first and have the final clap as it’s coils let out a loud clap through the tunnel behind him.

The drone shuddered in it’s place moving from side to side crashing into the walls, disoriented  like a drunken belter trying to find his way home from the star bar. It moaned in electronic groans and splutters, as it’s main turret powered down.

“It still has it’s kinetic turret!” Tau was trying to contain herself, sweat ran down her forehead as the held back the images from her blown apart comrades that took blows from rail rifles in the previous war. It wasn’t pretty watching your closest friend be ripped in two, their organs splayed out on the ground by a 12 inch thick iron slug leaving an unscheduled painting along the hull of an Icarus. She knew that while they might survive most shock penetrations now with the new suit’s built nervous network, in the moment they would not be able to recover to finish the job.

“It’s video feeds are disabled but I’m still picking up a sounding scan”, Tau held her breath, speaking quietly. Their Mark IV suit’s dampened out any internal sounds, but instinct still took over as though they were hiding their frail exposed bodies, Shai turned her attention to her heartbeat scanner heightening the tension in her voice. “Aah guys, that life form I picked up earlier it’s getting closer, it’s coming from the other side of the tunnel, We’ll be pinched”. Tex began reaching for a slug to load into the Railstorm’s kinetic chamber. “Whatever it is, it’s not going to like what I’ve got in store”, “Stay where you are Tex! That drone can still turn you to pink mist!” said Tau frantically, Tex chambered the slug in his Storm rail then hugged his back hard up against the tunnel wall.

“The signal.. it appears to be human”, Said Shai. She looked up at Tex from the other side of the tunnel, her voice edged mixed with relief to confusion. “It’s… it’s getting closer, 20 meters and closing on our 6”. John remained fixed in position, prone his sites perched still fixed on the drones direction. His shoulder turret pivoted 180 degrees covering the rear of the tunnel behind them. “I got it covered, we have bigger problems right now, focus on that fucking drone…” Said John.

Everything was quiet, awkwardly quiet. The Sparrow hovered vigilantly, fixed, waiting for a positive read to be picked up on one of John’s team. “It’s operating on Autopilot” Tau began to explain but more for herself than anything “It must have lost contact with command when it crossed the mesh barrier” She whispered, then the tunnel fell to silence once more. The walls began to vibrate and hum, like the mountain was becoming alive, gently. A loud thud shook the tunnel sending rubble and debris clamouring over their armoured suit’s. An ensemble of metallic clangs as their suit’s took the grunt of the falling debris announced their positions even more.

“It’s trying to echo-locate us!” said John. “Fuck this!” said Tex, reluctant to stand there like a rabbit in the headlight. They all knew the sparrow would soon determine their positions with it’s advanced AI, differentiating the sound of rubble against steel would be no hard feat. Tex had waited long enough in his mind, He selected the highest charge possible on the Rail Storm, and listened to the purr of the  coils as they began to prime, just enough, then kneeled down in the open of the tunnel, Storm Rail at the ready, converging his targeting reticle on the sparrows main processing unit. “Covering Fire!” yelled John. Instantly Tau pivoted from the left side of the tunnel just off to the front left of Tex raising her rifle as she did in a smooth motion. The spacing was tight between them, with just enough opening for John to lay down fire between Tex and Tau, an unconventional and completely unorthodox manoeuvre by any training standard, but what choice did they have?

A barrage of fire opened up toward the Sparrow as soon as John had gave the order. Sparks of splintering, hot molten amber ricochet off the armour cladded drone as John and Taus Sherpa rounds did nothing to damage the drone. It was akin to throwing sand in the face of the schoolyard bully, only delaying a heavy handed punch to the face. The sparrows sensor arrays lit up, overwhelmed by molten rain, it’s scans became completely useless. Tex watched on anxiously, as the Storm Rail hummed while it charged for it’s next shot, seconds felt like days, as he willed the last bar of the charge gauge in his HUD to green light him so he could let all hell loose. Tex’s sights finally fixed their lock on the target with a lock. Meanwhile Shai observed the sparrows targeting lasers track up along his chest, but the reticle didn’t stop there; it kept rising up past Tex, past John, flickering through the billowing fog deeper into the tunnel where a deep recessed void appeared that hadn’t been there before.

“Storm Rail Charged” strobed in the top left of Tex’s HUD, Suddenly in a bright unison flash of blue and amber, the tunnel walls lit up in rapid succession. Blinding the others from both directions within milliseconds of the other. The Sparrow let loose it’s Kinetic rifle, Tex steadfast in his firing stance arched back slightly as a thick metal slug left the Storm-rails barrel. A tight crisp cloud of steam tailing it’s trail.

Tex felt a  percussive ripple fly through his suit, sending tingles down his spine. A scattered shock wave belted through the tunnel with a deafening disorienting effect. Adrenaline coursed through his body, sending tingles down his veins from head to toe. Tex closed his eyes, and thought of what it would be like to die, imagining the emptiness of it. He knew if he’d failed in his shot, the others wouldn’t stand a chance. He thought he was done for anyway, so he took the risk to save them, and he found comfort knowing they might make it out alive.

The Sparrow let out a howling bionic scream, jumbled static mixed with corrosive high pitched piezoelectric buzzing, gnawed at their skulls, seamlessly bypassing their suit’s built in decibel filters.

It stumbled uncontrollably, it’s steaming railgun aimlessly spinning about flagging the others in the process, snapped and twisted against the tunnel walls into spaghetti as it thrashed about helplessly. Eventually it plummeted into rock and snow sending debris flying deeper into the tunnel peppering it’s targets.

Tau gritted her teeth as she tweaked settings desperately to block out the frequencies. Finally the buzzing stopped, their ears still ringing with tinnitus as they reoriented. A softening static slipped from the tunnel as the machines last hum whispered down into the cold embracing of silence. For a split moment it felt like as though a ghost had escaped from its now lifeless armour cladded shell. It now laid peacefully blocking the tunnel entrance behind it.

Tex’s Storm-rail still had steam billowing from it’s glowing muzzle as it slowly found it’s resting place down his chest. His body like a ragdoll fell forward powerless, caught in a kneeling cradle hunched over his forward knee as he tried to move, but he felt no response. He could think of doing it, but his body remained still. His heavy head followed his chest dropping forward resting to the side against the shaft of the cooling Storm-rail. He gazed down at the ground, his thoughts began to wander aimlessly. The monstrosity clad in his oversized suit's thick armour knelt dead still, like a statue in the middle of the tunnel. The atmosphere from the entrance of the tunnel propelled forward like a small wave from the sparrows' impact. the waves of mist clashed around Tex, settling like a resting pool of fog by a sleeping obelisk, it rippled along his calves, kissing his lifeless hands gently. “Tex!!” A tear forced its way out of Shai’s eye straddling the bottom of her eye lid, filled with the internal blue glow from within her helmet, a small galaxy seemed to flicker within it as all the body functions of her teammates pulsed in a barrage of information. She wasn’t checking them, She wasn’t thinking, she was in a sea of rage and sorrow.

With Shai preoccupied and John still covering the front, Tau looked back through the thick fog at the rear of the tunnel. A burning blue glow caressed her gaze drawing her in. “John” Tau whispered  slowly, easing her way deeper toward the void. “There is something..” she switched her HUD to thermals “someone..  behind us”. “Get it together Shai” said John with sharp authority.

“OK, ok, ok cap”, Shai collected herself and began checking Tex’s vitals through her HUD. “I’m still picking up neural activity but it’s limited to involuntary functions, he’s still breathing”. John closed his eyes with a sigh of relief. “It’s locked in syndrome, His neural link was disconnected impromptu… from an EMP charge..” Said Shai.  “We took out that things fucking EMP!”, John’s voice tremored, he had done this as routine, he clawed in his mind at the possibility of a storm rail critical misfunction. “I’m tapping into his suit and initiating an emergency reboot”. Shai, was beginning to gain composure again.

Tex, groaned, moaning in discomfort, his eyes rolling from the back of his skull back to their resting place, druel dripped from his bottom lip. His jawline twitched as he observed a notification pulsing in his HUD. “Reboot initiated”. He felt the life pouring into the back of his neck like freezing water, then his shoulders, arms, torso, legs and eventually his toes. His body ached and burned buzzing and twitching, like a bed of needles pierced his soul as he urged himself forward, One knee up, then the next  he raised himself in agony from the ground.

“What the fuck..” Tex’s groaned in annoyance, as he locked his jaw back and forth regaining voluntary muscle control.. “That Sparrow take down … Nice work! I didn’t even hit the darn thing, I lost control of my arms just as I pulled the trigger,” his eyes drifted from what remained of a steaming splintered hulking wreck of the sparrow. His eyes climbed their way up the tunnels edge, eventually to find a watermelon sized cavity his stray shot had carved, the slug or what remained of it sitting proud in the middle of it. The cavity sat proud just above where the sparrow once hovered before it had dramatically met it’s end.

“Johnnn!!” Tau croaked with annoyance still trying to edge his attention. She had made her way to the rear of Tunnel, “You’re going to want to see this.” the sound of crushing ice and stone beneath her boots turned to a metallic thud. She knelt down, running her fingers through the ice and ruble to reveal an unnatural metallic floor.

Tex, realizing as his senses came too he was the only heavy gunner in the squad, turned about face throwing his storm-rail back on his shoulder it’s reticle now locked directly on the void. Silence took a hold of them as they locked sites at the end of the tunnel in anticipation. Slowly, a falling belly of fog and steam spilled endlessly through a wall that seemed to breathe. By now the blue glow that had drawn Tau in had diminished to nothing.

Suddenly a belly of fog and steam hurled toward them from as the breathing wall gave way, scattering their sensors and vision. A cloak field like that at the face of the cliff powered down revealing an unnatural structure behind it, seemingly organic yet also steel.

They could hardly believe what they were seeing. An EMP cannon the size of a minibus had been hidden within the tunnel. It’s positioning  well planned. A defensive vantage point overlooking the tunnels opening, encapsulated behind a seamless cloaked wall with only an opening small enough to allow for the Cannons muzzle to sit ever so proudly, concealed behind the cloaking field which was no more.

The electric hum that had taken them by surprise eased down to a whispering static. Something was moving behind the turret, seated at it’s control centre. Immediately rifle sites raised at the mysterious figure to the rear of the cannon as they hugged the walls of the void closing distance between them.

“Waaaa hooooo!!, I’ve been waiting to use this bad boy for over a century now!”, A joyous victory chant filled the tunnel with a voice slightly inorganic. At John’s direction the others lowered their arms, Tex’s rifle still slightly raised untrusting. “A century yet before this cowboy leaves town you protectant genocidal bastards you!” Tau look

scene-0020.chapterTitle: Chapter 3: Synaptic Memoriam of a steel fossil shell
scene-0020.editorText:
<$Proj_H::1><!$Proj_H::1>

A strange little Mechanoid being, not dissimilar from John’s newfound body in appearance, placed his hand on the sides of the cavern. “Little guy looks like me..” John thought to himself looking over at Tau as his rifle sites reticle readjusted to capture the figure sheltered by a wall of mist and steam billowing outward into the tunnel as the cold atmosphere bathed the battery cells nested beneath a large EMP cannon.

“Seems friendly enough” Shai looked back at Tex who was still coming too with a smirk. Tex thought for a moment it to be a straw. It wasn’t a man, but it had a heartbeat. Completely  “We’re protectant.. said Tau, but.. bastards?” She questioned the integrity of the little machine mans analysis and to whom it was directed, thinking it awfully suspicious. “Marcellus” John thought quietly to himself. Tau was confused. She was expecting to be torn apart by a barrage of fire only to find ths friendly little machine man. “It was aiming at you ya daft bastard, that means your it’s enemy and my enemies foe is my friend..”  “Seems more human than machine.”, john through to himself”. “your a , your a hybrid too!”. Said John walking over now with a friendly body language his rifle at his side. Johns voice softened like he had met a long lost friend at a tech conference. “Yep, tasked by the Dr to maintain this facility”. What the hell are you doing so close to the surface? We thought this place was uninhabited. only investigated because we picked up on the break in your sound barrier”.:Tau was puzzled.. “Aaah yes, I was up here fixing the dam transformer thermal cell. The tectonic shifts in this region can be troublesome to all this hardware. We are still perfecting the Nano bots..” The little machine man knelt down pulling a cylinder from his hip. It ejected from a well formed storage capsule intricately and conveniently blended into the stream line of his frame where intestines would normally be on a human. “That drone picked up on your Barrier break as an impulse anomaly when you entered into our little sanctuary and broke the sound/light barrier”

Tau stood up brushing the dirt from her suits targeting reticle. “That explains why it still showed up even after we were behind the curtain, it detects large breaks in the curtain, and drew a sound profile of our suits from the static crackles,

“What do we call you?” said Tau in a motherly tone. “Our Ally?” Said John, leaning his back into the tunnel wall as he caught his composure, his rifle slouching at his side.

The little machine man rested the lid of the cylinder on the grate below him, gently nursing a small straggling mass from behind a chrome trail of liquid thick substance within an oil based medium. “We are still working through the transition medium to increase repair times. But these guys will shift the transformer plates in time to correct the bump in our hard light emitter by noon” The being tightened the cap resealing the remaining nanobots inside it, then reinserted it into it’s holder in his waist. “” He said seeming awfully pleased with himself. “To a spiritual awakening? are these mushrooms going to teleport us to another dimension” Tex seemed amused with his little joke as he squished some of the lichen and moss between his fingers, flicking it to the ground.

Spending months on end in an airtight can in space had invoked a child-like curiosity in the man. His visor retracted as he indulged his senses. “Some might call it another dimension, my gentle giant!” said Tbone leaning up against the cavern wall, a mischievous smile was stretched across his face. “Cap” Whispered Tau. “I’m picking up allot of electrical activity”. Taus visor was locked shut still as she observed a plethora of signal activity. While Tex found it hard to contain impulsive thoughts, she had remained reserved still, unsure with their new acquaintance. “It’s fine” Said Walker, unbothered by the humm which began to reverberate through the cavern. The rear of the cavern wall glitched for a moment, John, Tau Shai and Tex all stepped back harrowed for a moment, squinting, gleaning whether what they had just seen was real. They’d seen small Hard mesh cloaks before but something of this scale seemed unusual, new, unexpected. A sudden beeping sound chimed 5 times. Then a deep electronic voice gauged their ears in a horrid cryptic language they had never heard before. The sound entered the room like a bus horn easing down with electronic inflections, whips and clack's as the frequencies twisted and turned, it was almost painful to the others but John seemed unphased.

“What the fuck was that” Tex raised his rifle straight at Tbone’s head his finger on the trigger ready to paint the walls with his brains or whatever the fuck was inside he thought to himself. John croaked gently in a dissuasive tone, “Tex! lower your weapon”, accompanied by a restraining wave at his side. The tension in the air receded but not fully. Tex’s rifle muzzle dipped to the ground as he let out a deep sigh in a mix of relief, then disbelief. He gasped in awe wide eyed as the entirety of the cavern's rear wall dissolved into nothingness.

“Hard Light Mesh Technology, but.. of this scale!?” Tau spoke with admiration as the young Engineer stepped forward with inquisitiveness Tex looked on at her. Her rifle now mag-locked across her back, Tex shrugged his shoulders then holstered his rifle in its place. An electronic humm filled the cavern's belly with an otherworldly presence emitting from towering blast doors which spanned the entirety of the cavern rear.

“Have we inhaled some funky mushroom spores?” Tex wondered aloud, his voice tinged with wonder and confusion. Tbone, arms folded in contemplation, posed a question that hung in the air like a riddle awaiting unraveling. “How do you think those mushrooms got there?” he explained, his gaze filled with pride spanned the belly of the cave like a fathers eyes resting on the womb containing his child. "Artificial light breathes life into this abyss, sustaining us in secrecy.”

Tbone had his arms crossed waiting for an answer from Tex, but more he seemed disappointed he had so swiftly raised his rifle straight at his head. He didn’t think he would pull the trigger, but he could sense the distrust in the man. He didn’t blame him either. His whole squad had just been crossed by their own faction, everything they knew. “So much remains hidden from all of you, you’ve all been fooled” Tbone thought to himself, then unfolded his arms walking over to the towering blast doors. The Doors looked ancient. Their scale projected a sense of Alien Majesty, as they hummed like an ethereal soul. Tau was shaken by how someone or something could have amassed the material to procure such a feat of engineering so deep underneath the mountains, little own withstand the active shifts in the tectonic plates and hold it’s structural integrity. “How on earth did this all get here?” Tbone unfolded his hand resting it on a small recessed face at the edge of the blast doors frame. “This is just the tip of the iceberg my friends” Tebo smiled at Tau, then the same harrowing sound from before let out, but this time less intense than the first.

The colossal blast doors shuddered in the wake of the sound as though they had been awoken. They slowly began to retract inch by inch they disappeared into the stoney mass of the cavern walls. As they opened an emptiness of thick mist bellowed out in waves, engulfing them up to their knees pushing past them to settle along the top of the water runs at the foot of the green room mother tree.

A fine sand like dust trickled down from the giant doors weathered crevasses gently caressing the foundation at it’s base, as though to bestow those before her with the majesty of her scale and meaning. The cave seemed to rattle and shake, yet in reality it remained still, a deception cast over the mind due to the sheer scale of the towering doors as they carried the room as they moved making it hard to determine what was actually moving.

“Why all the theatrics? That sound!” said Tex, “We figured any scavengers might be deterred by something they couldn’t understand should they stray too far. Nonetheless, most of them, the curious few that slipped through only made it to the green room, I think they thought it was cursed or something because they never stayed too long within its hold. In total over the last half century only 4 have made it to the green room”. As the last words slipped from the little machine man’s mouth the blast doors let out a heavy clap as they finished their retreat into the walls, then everything was silent. The others retracted their visors looking out gleaning into the darkness with questions. A cold chill blew in through the massive opening kissing Tex and the others on the face. The force of the wind whispered to the scale of the open space before them.

John was the first to step forward, a slight metallic thud after each step but with minimal echo. The steel beneath him was thick and he could feel it, like a foundation to support the towers of an empire. With each step his eyes toyed with intricate patterns interweaving along the structure's surface, they were unlike anything he had seen before, a cryptic lingual dance of an unknown civilisation. They spanned the entirety of the structure, beckoning him forward, further to a pronounced edge where the patterns cut in then down to the depths. John’s rifle rested quietly in it’s maglock cradle as the captain let the suit carry him carelessly forward. John Stood firmly now at the edge.The tension in his shoulders eased off as they as his gaze lay rest over an industrious underground womb. John’s pupils dilated in a euphoric state gleaning deeper into the depths of something beyond the realms of the human mind.

John's part-sentient eyes gifted him with a true understanding of the depths and scale of the realm before him. As his eyes crept down the ledge from beneath his armour clad toes, the ledge beneath him began to violently glow. Thermal ducts sprawled out - a vast network of energy, violently glew, transitioning from dark blues to amber clouds as electrons swirled in intricate turbulence dancing with one another interlocked in a perpetuating dance amidst a web of steel, stone, ice, and flora.

Tau was the next to make it to the ledge, her rifle slightly raised in caution she stood to the left of John, trailing behind her Shai and Tex together looking out almost symmetrically together in opposite sectors, the little machine man wandered carefree behind the group, his hands and fingers interlocked behind his back, resting behind his metallic hips. He allowed the silence to stagnate, curious to see how his new-found friends would perceive his birthplace.

“How long have you been down here?” Tau couldn’t hold her thoughts any longer, curiosity cutting through the silence like a Niten Ichiryu blades edge. “What do you mean?” Said the little robotic man. He stopped for a moment pondering the question “Well since the Dr brought me into this place, what I remember of it anyway. He said I was a mechanic before he repurposed me here, and well I’ve been looking after Genesis ever since”, “Two heavens as one” Tau looked at Tebo, all was quiet as he made eye contact with her. “Yes, my second heaven”. Shai stepped forward to the ledge with the others, looking out over a utopia teeming with organic life.

Suspended networks of interwoven thermal ducts all tied into a larger cylindrical tower at the center of the cavern. The cylinder glew a dim blue in John’s eyes as the ducts pulsed bringing it to life. Tau could not see the thermal duct taps into the earth's crust like John, but the Engineer inside her appreciated the design before her.

“John.. Do you mind if I..”,  “Tap in?” John finished Tao’s sentence like he could feel her curiosity creeping up on him. “Kitten bridge my optics to Taus viewport please” .Tau was silently appreciating the beauty of the gardens as they hung like a window, veering deep into the past, she felt like a child walking through the gardens of Babylon. Streams of quartz clear water trickled down overgrown structures, her mind riding on a journey to the depths of another realm. Thickets of vines writhed around massive hydraulic legs, entangling themselves in a fumbling dance to grip to any impurities that presented a hold on the seamlessly immaculate towering steel structures. Finally they found purchase, digging into and around the milder steel wings assisting them as they held the rubble from crushing below. Their tendrils seemed to reach down ever searching, as they looked back over their new companions' wandering heads. Shai's neck worked up a mild whiplash as she tracked their movements with awe."

As the Little Machine Man Tbone stepped forward he opened his arms out wide softly pronouncing. “I present to you.. Genesis”.. The moment the name emitted from the little machine it echoed through what felt like an eternity, Taus' vision blew up with life and heat signatures dancing underneath the structures foundations, every pillars roots shooting down, glowing like a giver of life, feeding a chasm of systems both natural and artificial the warmth and energy needed like a tree from the depths. “Now you see what I see huh” Tau looked into John's eyes and smiled, with a hint of intimacy, although John didn’t pick up on it. He was gone, his gaze lost, gleaning deeper into the center of the cavernous underground superstructure in wonder of what lay within its embracing depths.

A strange little Mechanoid being, not dissimilar from John’s newfound body in appearance, placed his hand on the sides of the cavern. “Little guy looks like me..” John thought to himself looking over at Tau as his rifle sites reticle readjusted to capture the figure sheltered by a wall of mist and steam billowing outward into the tunnel as the cold atmosphere bathed the battery cells nested beneath a large EMP cannon.

“Seems friendly enough” Shai looked back at Tex who was still coming too with a smirk. Tex thought for a moment it to be a straw. It wasn’t a man, but it had a heartbeat. Completely  “We’re protectant.. said Tau, but.. bastards?” She questioned the integrity of the little machine mans analysis and to whom it was directed, thinking it awfully suspicious. “Marcellus” John thought quietly to himself. Tau was confused. She was expecting to be torn apart by a barrage of fire only to find ths friendly little machine man. “It was aiming at you ya daft bastard, that means your it’s enemy and my enemies foe is my friend..”  “Seems more human than machine.”, john through to himself”. “your a , your a hybrid too!”. Said John walking over now with a friendly body language his rifle at his side. Johns voice softened like he had met a long lost friend at a tech conference. “Yep, tasked by the Dr to maintain this facility”. What the hell are you doing so close to the surface? We thought this place was uninhabited. only investigated because we picked up on the break in your sound barrier”.:Tau was puzzled.. “Aaah yes, I was up here fixing the dam transformer thermal cell. The tectonic shifts in this region can be troublesome to all this hardware. We are still perfecting the Nano bots..” The little machine man knelt down pulling a cylinder from his hip. It ejected from a well formed storage capsule intricately and conveniently blended into the stream line of his frame where intestines would normally be on a human. “That drone picked up on your Barrier break as an impulse anomaly when you entered into our little sanctuary and broke the sound/light barrier”

Tau stood up brushing the dirt from her suits targeting reticle. “That explains why it still showed up even after we were behind the curtain, it detects large breaks in the curtain, and drew a sound profile of our suits from the static crackles,
“What do we call you?” said Tau in a motherly tone. “Our Ally?” Said John, leaning his back into the tunnel wall as he caught his composure, his rifle slouching at his side.

The little machine man rested the lid of the cylinder on the grate below him, gently nursing a small straggling mass from behind a chrome trail of liquid thick substance within an oil based medium. “We are still working through the transition medium to increase repair times. But these guys will shift the transformer plates in time to correct the bump in our hard light emitter by noon” The being tightened the cap resealing the remaining nanobots inside it, then reinserted it into it’s holder in his waist. “” He said seeming awfully pleased with himself. “To a spiritual awakening? are these mushrooms going to teleport us to another dimension” Tex seemed amused with his little joke as he squished some of the lichen and moss between his fingers, flicking it to the ground.

Spending months on end in an airtight can in space had invoked a child-like curiosity in the man. His visor retracted as he indulged his senses. “Some might call it another dimension, my gentle giant!” said Tbone leaning up against the cavern wall, a mischievous smile was stretched across his face. “Cap” Whispered Tau. “I’m picking up allot of electrical activity”. Taus visor was locked shut still as she observed a plethora of signal activity. While Tex found it hard to contain impulsive thoughts, she had remained reserved still, unsure with their new acquaintance. “It’s fine” Said Walker, unbothered by the humm which began to reverberate through the cavern. The rear of the cavern wall glitched for a moment, John, Tau Shai and Tex all stepped back harrowed for a moment, squinting, gleaning whether what they had just seen was real. They’d seen small Hard mesh cloaks before but something of this scale seemed unusual, new, unexpected. A sudden beeping sound chimed 5 times. Then a deep electronic voice gauged their ears in a horrid cryptic language they had never heard before. The sound entered the room like a bus horn easing down with electronic inflections, whips and clack's as the frequencies twisted and turned, it was almost painful to the others but John seemed unphased.

“What the fuck was that” Tex raised his rifle straight at Tbone’s head his finger on the trigger ready to paint the walls with his brains or whatever the fuck was inside he thought to himself. John croaked gently in a dissuasive tone, “Tex! lower your weapon”, accompanied by a restraining wave at his side. The tension in the air receded but not fully. Tex’s rifle muzzle dipped to the ground as he let out a deep sigh in a mix of relief, then disbelief. He gasped in awe wide eyed as the entirety of the cavern's rear wall dissolved into nothingness.

“Hard Light Mesh Technology, but.. of this scale!?” Tau spoke with admiration as the young Engineer stepped forward with inquisitiveness Tex looked on at her. Her rifle now mag-locked across her back, Tex shrugged his shoulders then holstered his rifle in its place. An electronic humm filled the cavern's belly with an otherworldly presence emitting from towering blast doors which spanned the entirety of the cavern rear.

“Have we inhaled some funky mushroom spores?” Tex wondered aloud, his voice tinged with wonder and confusion. Tbone, arms folded in contemplation, posed a question that hung in the air like a riddle awaiting unraveling. “How do you think those mushrooms got there?” he explained, his gaze filled with pride spanned the belly of the cave like a fathers eyes resting on the womb containing his child. "Artificial light breathes life into this abyss, sustaining us in secrecy.”

Tbone had his arms crossed waiting for an answer from Tex, but more he seemed disappointed he had so swiftly raised his rifle straight at his head. He didn’t think he would pull the trigger, but he could sense the distrust in the man. He didn’t blame him either. The Doors looked ancient. Their scale projected a sense of Alien Majesty, as they hummed like an ethereal soul. Tau was shaken by how someone or something could have amassed the material to procure such a feat of engineering so deep underneath the mountains, little own withstand the active shifts in the tectonic plates and hold it’s structural integrity. “How on earth did this all get here?” Tbone unfolded his hand resting it on a small recessed face at the edge of the blast doors frame. “This is just the tip of the iceberg my friends” Tebo smiled at Tau, then the same harrowing sound from before let out, but this time less intense than the first.

The colossal blast doors shuddered in the wake of the sound as though they had been awoken. They slowly began to retract inch by inch they disappeared into the stoney mass of the cavern walls. As they opened an emptiness of thick mist bellowed out in waves, engulfing them up to their knees pushing past them to settle along the top of the water runs at the foot of the green room mother tree.

A fine sand like dust trickled down from the giant doors weathered crevasses gently caressing the foundation at it’s base, as though to bestow those before her with the majesty of her scale and meaning. The cave seemed to rattle and shake, yet in reality it remained still, a deception cast over the mind due to the sheer scale of the towering doors as they carried the room as they moved making it hard to determine what was actually moving.

“Why all the theatrics? That sound!” said Tex, “We figured any scavengers might be deterred by something they couldn’t understand should they stray too far. Nonetheless, most of them, the curious few that slipped through only made it to the green room, I think they thought it was cursed or something because they never stayed too long within its hold. In total over the last half century only 4 have made it to the green room”. As the last words slipped from the little machine man’s mouth the blast doors let out a heavy clap as they finished their retreat into the walls, then everything was silent. The others retracted their visors looking out gleaning into the darkness with questions. A cold chill blew in through the massive opening kissing Tex and the others on the face. The force of the wind whispered to the scale of the open space before them.

John was the first to step forward, a slight metallic thud after each step but with minimal echo. The steel beneath him was thick and he could feel it, like a foundation to support the towers of an empire. With each step his eyes toyed with intricate patterns interweaving along the structure's surface, they were unlike anything he had seen before, a cryptic lingual dance of an unknown civilisation. They spanned the entirety of the structure, beckoning him forward, further to a pronounced edge where the patterns cut in then down to the depths. John’s rifle rested quietly in it’s maglock cradle as the captain let the suit carry him carelessly forward. John Stood firmly now at the edge.The tension in his shoulders eased off as they as his gaze lay rest over an industrious underground womb. John’s pupils dilated in a euphoric state gleaning deeper into the depths of something beyond the realms of the human mind.

John's part-sentient eyes gifted him with a true understanding of the depths and scale of the realm before him. As his eyes crept down the ledge from beneath his armour clad toes, the ledge beneath him began to violently glow. Thermal ducts sprawled out - a vast network of energy, violently glew, transitioning from dark blues to amber clouds as electrons swirled in intricate turbulence dancing with one another interlocked in a perpetuating dance amidst a web of steel, stone, ice, and flora.

Tau was the next to make it to the ledge, her rifle slightly raised in caution she stood to the left of John, trailing behind her Shai and Tex together looking out almost symmetrically together in opposite sectors, the little machine man wandered carefree behind the group, his hands and fingers interlocked behind his back, resting behind his metallic hips. He allowed the silence to stagnate, curious to see how his new-found friends would perceive his birthplace.

“How long have you been down here?” Tau couldn’t hold her thoughts any longer, curiosity cutting through the silence like a Niten Ichiryu blades edge. “What do you mean?” Said the little robotic man. He said I was a mechanic before he repurposed me here, and well I’ve been looking after Genesis ever since”, “Two heavens as one” Tau looked at Tebo, all was quiet as he made eye contact with her. “Yes, my second heaven”. Shai stepped forward to the ledge with the others, looking out over a utopia teeming with organic life.

Suspended networks of interwoven thermal ducts all tied into a larger cylindrical tower at the center of the cavern. The cylinder glew a dim blue in John’s eyes as the ducts pulsed bringing it to life. Tau could not see the thermal duct taps into the earth's crust like John, but the Engineer inside her appreciated the design before her.

“John.. Do you mind if I..”,  “Tap in?” John finished Tao’s sentence like he could feel her curiosity creeping up on him. “Kitten bridge my optics to Taus viewport please” .Tau was silently appreciating the beauty of the gardens as they hung like a window, veering deep into the past, she felt like a child walking through the gardens of Babylon. Streams of quartz clear water trickled down overgrown structures, her mind riding on a journey to the depths of another realm. Thickets of vines writhed around massive hydraulic legs, entangling themselves in a fumbling dance to grip to any impurities that presented a hold on the seamlessly immaculate towering steel structures. Finally they found purchase, digging into and around the milder steel wings assisting them as they held the rubble from crushing below. Their tendrils seemed to reach down ever searching, as they looked back over their new companions' wandering heads. Shai's neck worked up a mild whiplash as she tracked their movements with awe."
