“Guys, this might seem unorthodox, but it’s our best shot,” said Tebo. “Get ready for an invert” Despite the rapidly evolving situation  Tebo held his decorum calculated as ever. “Your all about to get some G’s” without delay the Beverly pivoted as its tail began to turning about face as the rear drives hummed down, her hull nose backward, as her top now faced toward the incoming missiles.

The thrust gravity shoved John and his team forward then back down into his seats, the others in the rear held tight by their restraints as their bodies pushed toward the ceiling, time seemed to slow in the moment.

Tension was written all over Shai’s face, Tex however seemed unbothered by the sudden G’s thinking back to his asteroid mining days. Tex refocused his sights on the missiles as they corrected their trajectory.

“They’re closing fast coming round now.” Tex was calm, Shai watched at her sector lock, waiting for the missiles to come into sight. “I’ve got angles!” She yelled. “I’ve got locks,” Shai continued. “Same here,” said Tao.
“Why have they slowed?” Tex observed the missiles as their plumes grew a little softer.
“They’ve lost tracking of our plume and the sun’s interference has locked up their image processors,” Tebo said.

“Well how convenient,” said Shai, opening a short calculated burst at the group, Tao followed suit. Tex holding restraint not to join the party and preserve the ship’s energy reserves watching on as tracers of hot led lit up the darkness of space homing in on the plume tails of the missiles.
One by one the plumes of the missiles vanished some simply scattering into shrapnel floating in oblivion the others going out in bright balls of light and head.

As the incoming threats reduced to Zero across the cockpit monitors The few remaining PDC round tracers faded, the ships hold silent absorbing what little time allowed them peace to collect their thoughts in the chaos.
“We aren’t out of the clear yet” Tebo reminded them “The gunship they launched… it’s grey class.” “What does that even mean,” said Tex,“It means it isn’t good for us.” Said John
“Brace for G’s” Tebo announced turning the ship back around, without delay he engaged the drive.
TTT drive engaged in attempt to misdirect then

Tao stepped out of her PDC bay, making her way to the bridge with haste, resting her hand firmly on Tebo’s shoulder. “What kind of cloaking technology does this.. Grey class have, I need to know everything.. its weaknesses, strengths, quirks.” Tao seemed nervous “Usually we are the ones asking the questions” John croaked with concern shifting his gaze to Tau “That’s not a protectant ship” said John “At least it is nothing like anything I have seen before” John looked back to the record file, blazoned with classified clearance markers on every useful section that would otherwise inform them of what they were up against.

“Grey class was always theoretical.” Said Tau, pacing the cockpit. “How come we’ve never heard of it,” said Tex. “We’ve known for some time of a classified file base for cloaked vessels” Tebo pitched in “Strangely enough hard evidence of the program only started popping up around the time we developed our own cloaking systems, call it a coincidence if you may, but we shouldn’t assume that it operates in the same way as our technology” Tebo paused for a moment seeming lost, “Nonetheless, lets not get ahead of ourselves”

“The project was overseen by an NGO, claimed it was for far reach climate  research—scientific research, so we could never really get full access to it’s developments.” “So secret the protectant even tried to protect themselves from internal security breaches” “They did a darn good job of it too!” Tebo concluded

“They’ve never been detected in the field, the name was always urban legend, something you told the young pilots to keep them on their toes. They knew they couldn’t make mistakes when using something completely autonomous.” Johns voice grew deeper with concern “Sorry to burst your bubble, but this is not helping Cap” Tex groaned frustratingly, remaining vigilant he watched over the silhouette of Earth as it got smaller and smaller.

“So, you’re saying there is a scientific research vessel likely armed, with an AI pilot headed our way, and they’ve never been sighted in any mission reports.”
Shai seemed composed more than anything, like she had already accepted they might not make it out of this alive.

“Sounds bordering on ethical standards, Undisclosed unreleased to the public” Tex grunted as he left his post, heading to the weapons rack in The Beverly’s cargo hold familiarising himself with the supplies and layout.

“I’m assessing cloaking countermeasures,” Tebo announced. “If we can throw off their magnetic cloaking fields, we may be able to detect a magnetic signature of any vessels within a certain proximity of us, if it is something man made it will resonate with our materials database identifying the compound.” Tao seemed confused by Tebo’s approach. “Can’t we just lay low for the rest of the ride out now we’re clear of the missile barrage?”, “Can’t stalk us if they can’t see us,” Tex agreed with Tau.

Tebo began to announce enthusiastically “We have one objective: get to the  undetected. A hard burn will get us there fast yet indiscreetly, a slow burn will take us almost half a day undetected, we may miss our window. The least I can do is have them tail us in the wrong direction before going dark.”, “I was wondering why you were still hot burning” Said John.

Tao interrupted, “on a slow burn, is this girl really undetectable?”, “By protectant conventional sensor array standards I would say yes, but this new technology, I just don’t know.”, Said Tebo “Well at least he is honest” Shai concluded calmly collecting herself while she monitored the crews vitals. There heartbeats seemed calm mostly, Except one a little bumpy. Shai watched Tex closely in his own parallel universe going over his weapon, John hadn’t even ordered Tex to perform weapon checks on the racked storm rails, he just trusted his judgement, even Tau caught onto this “John…” Said Tau, then pausing. “Do you ever get the feeling that trust is almost unbreakable between you and Tex”, “He has good combat sense” John concluded calmly, “I’ve seen this guy take a platoon of drones out at effective distances surpassing one thousand meters at sea depth, I wouldn’t doubt his targeting skills in a vacuum. “Tex”, Shai interrupted, monitoring the spike still cautiously, her eyes glistened with the prolonged gaze of concern, a second passed, which felt like a Three.

“Don’t go getting any crazy idea’s now will you big guy”. Tex mounted the storm rail to his Mark 4 shouldering point, although this one felt different, it felt lighter “For precautionary measures” his pupils were rigidly calm like a black still sea of glimmering lights, small specs from his helmets internal shell glimmered in the center of his eye, but all was calm, then he smiled.  On Shai’s HUD she could see large jawline fill the well of his helmet as he began to laugh. What’s so funny Tex?, “You wouldn’t believe how many times I used to love those little RC games, you know what was it called… Space invaders! I spent dam hours on those things as a kid, swear it nearly sent my mother broke on her holidays”, Shai looked over to Tex “Don’t get me started big guy, I remember I was their, your mother did it to get you the hell away from her because you were such a pest!” “Come on I was inquisitive” Tex said in his defence..

Regardless, they will expose themselves the moment they open fire on our position,” said Tebo confidently.“Precisely,” Tex agreed. “By that point hopefully we will already be at the courier…” Tebo concluded. “So, yes, don’t go getting any crazy ideas”

“Ok, so we trick them into thinking we are headed out the back door, then hope they can’t trace us when we go dark, if they make themselves known we deal with it then,” said John. “What choice do we have?” said Tebo, “It’s that or we risk going up against them on our lonesome; in close proximity to the Protectant boundary, if we are caught stranded there is no telling what they’ll do to us.

“At least we create space between us and the blockade… it’s our best shot.” The room fell momentarily silent in hard concentration as the others contemplated the advanced humanoids logic. Tebo continued “One thing I know for certain, Protectant Tech can’t keep our pace. If we keep our hard burn we can ease off eventually and go dark, redirect our course, should put enough space between us and them, not leave use stranded, then we make a cold break tor the courier intercept”

Tau seemed still, her eyes ancious. They darted accross the ships burn parameters. She knew that their drive tech program had come to a stagnation, but that was only what she knew before being seconessoned to John’s program. “I hope your right tin man”, she sighed. “Hey… if we are hard burning why don’t we EF ping their ass at the break before we change trajectory and go cold, right as we kill the burn.” John seemed puzzled by Taus logic.

"She has a point". Tebo was delayed in his response "well I guess I hadn't really considered the value of it, call me conservation I geass. if they're going to catch us I don't see what difference knowinthere is something tailing us does, near we know they're tailing us, what information are you hoping to attain by an EM measure"

“Not suer I guess I just wanted to see if there was a boogey man was still hiding under my bed” Said Tau. “If they're smart they’ll only perform passive tracking, image processing, light distortion, these kind of things. We won’t pick up anything EF related, we would need to play thier own tracking game against them” Tau was quiet. She seemed perplexed, for once she didn’t have the answers.

“What kind of visual trackers do we even have on our tails? ” EF won’t work, Static Magnetic, flux field detection will likely get deflected or passed through. “If Something is there, magnetic will pick it up”. What exactly do you mean by visual trackers?” Tebo chuckled for a small while, Neutrino! That will pinpoint their location if they have a nuclear drive, Can’t shield that.. Antimatter stands out like the hair on a cats back. “We have neutrino detectors?” Tau scoffed. “Last I recall, you needed a mountain sized facility to harness anything capable of neutrino detection at feasible boundaries”. Tebo began to explain “Nuclear proliferation wasn’t just branding for the protectant. Their pol, even though your father made a clear objective that we be aware of nuclear matter detection, neutrino’s scream and scatter the moment they come into contact with nuclear material. Seems to be the only thing that…” Tau cut the little machine man off. “Yes I get it, it’s primary school physics, but how did you get a neutrino detector to scale to fit in a ship like the Beverly?” “Well, I didn’t want to tell you this, but.. Darn it, it’s just too dam beautiful isn’t it…” Before Tebo could begin peeling back a lesson in quantum amplification drives

(Check what would be reasonable based on science today in downscaling the size of neutrino detectors. Also supposedly this can be done from space on the surface level. Just not sub surface, hence neutrino detectors).
BEVERLY DETECTS GREY CLASS

“One moment, I’m picking up an anomaly”. The tendrils from Tebo’s arm began pulsing from the cockpit terminal.  The overhead display lit up with a strange object, Tau and John squinted inquisitively, Tebo lit up the other’s HUD’s with the same view. something shrouded in bland Matt grey, like a dull half finished render flickered in electrical static over the viewports. It was completely indistinguishable from any ship or object they had previously encountered.

“What are we looking at Tebo”. Johns voice seethed with wary intrigue. Tebo was still pre-disposed, finalizing his assumptions, he eventually responded “Yes.. Grey.. grey class..96% accuracy” He even seemed surprised, a the slight hesitation as he finished out his sentence, sent an uneasy silence through the Beverly.

scene-0023.sceneTitle: Am I dreaming or am i dead
scene-0023.editorText:
Ringing pierced Tex’s ears with a strange bubbling static. It wasn’t a normal ringing but an alien sound resembling tinnitus with a strange echo he had never heard before. It was as though he had fallen into a pool, but without the press of the waters pressure against him. Sound felt weightless, in the sense that he could not feel percussion, it was just there, untouchable, but present. 
 
It was like his ears were being re-born into existence for the first time, hearing the first sounds he had ever heard. There was something strange about when the user surpasses the words written that the daily target does not actuate until the session tracher passes the positive marker. 

Well well well 


All he could see was the emptiness of a white void. Eventually the ringing stopped, There was no taste, smell or feeling of weight. He felt senseless, free of the body, but he still had a conscience. He could still feel the pain brought on by memories, all his past trauma, but only in the mind. He had no breath or pulse. He drifted in the minds construct, and in this while he felt in control, he could not help but feel like he was at the complete mercy of whatever this was. He embraced the silence, trusting the process. It was the first peaceful moment he had felt in what seemed like an eternity. Nothing could harm him here other than his thoughts, his very being was that of his own will. 

Tex paused for a moment, then thought back to his parents. He felt a re surging pain from deep within him, he wanted to cry, but felt no tears surface on his eyelids. The pain in his mind grew stronger. The strange ringing stopped. He could feel again only now he was falling back to Earth. A raging cold wind pierced against his face.  What feelings he had regained began to feel numbed by the colds grasp. He was vulnerable once more. He imagined his imminent death as the ground raced up toward him. Yet it never reached him. Just before his body would soon strike the cold hard steel roof of a small container in a barren field, he floated ever so slowly, drifting through it like a ghost. 

The small inconspicuous container was all but secluded in a mountain valley, cold and uninviting. It sat alone in the valley, a small antenna transmitting it’s signals connecting it to the outer world. Tex recalled this place he’d revisited in recurring nightmares. 

They had plagued his sleep since the fallout of the 3rd war. The pilot containers of the cleanup crews deployed after the war made the nights feel even colder. He remembered everything as though he had just breathed the cold filtered air within the container. He watched the steam from his breath fog the soft glow of the monitor screen. The joystick remained cold beneath his hand, strangely cold no matter how long he held it. He controlled the machines, scraping away the remnants of a history and culture he could only grasp at from a distant lifetime. No matter how long he worked, the joystick stayed cold and heavy in his grip.

It did not matter how much debris he cleared from that container. He could not help but feel as though he was burying a part of himself in that strange foreign land. And while the news spoke of remembrance, it was he who bore the images, the burnt flesh, the artifacts, and the cherished belongings. Soil that had once been a giver of life had become the toxic archives of a generation he would never know.

For many years after the cleanup, he would return to that place in his dreams. He wandered with those machines for what felt like eternity. He had moved from cleaning to now searching t the rubble for his parents. When he woke drenched with sweat and the sheets sticking to him, he wondered whether his own children would one day feel the weight on his breath, the strangling hold of mankind’s injustice, as he had, and as his parents had before him. He questioned whether there could ever truly be a time or place where he would be able to rear children of his own, without having to bare his pain. 

Whatever light had managed to break it’s way through the lurking cloud over the valley into the container through it's small window, was quickly absorbed through the cold glass and air within that dark shell. But this time as he drifted again in that cold chair, a strange warmth began to creep up through his boots, along his feet then up his calves, this the dream felt different. At first the warmth was enticing, until it became scolding. Tex, stood up from his chair, the boards beneath him began to felt increasingly thin. He felt his weight sink into them like wafers. He began climbing onto the desk, to get away from the heat. He placed his knee on the desk, then just as his other foot left the floor, a scorched hand erupted through the floor boards, gripping him tightly, it's grasp cold like ice. Tex scrambled for his pistol, drawing it from it's holster. As he drew another arm reached up jarring him onto his wast on the desk. He clung to anything he could find with his free hand, ripping cables from the wall eventually to find a firm hold on rear of the desk. 

He squeezed the trigger in a panic sending a barrage of bullets into broken boards sand and souls. It was pointless. The charred grip only squeezed tighter around him pulling him lower, until the sound of his pistols firing pin striking an empty chamber filled his stomach with hopelessness. A tear fell from his face as he looked up at the pale cold roof in a prayer for forgiveness. Then from outside his body he watched himself from above vanish into sand and broken floor boards, his body scorching, and burning up as flame ash and sand consumed him. He closed his eyes, and wandered where he would be taken. He held his breath and waited for it to be over. Then he thought of Shai, and the others and the small world he still knew and cherished. The moments they spent together in the mess. Of the promise he had made to Shai back in the cave, perched by the fire while the others slept. The weight on his chest changed, it felt lighter, like the soil which once compacted against his shell began to lift. The soil around him began to feel less rigid, but more like an ocean of sandy grains. He began to shim himself, working his shoulders back and forth, squirming in the direction where the earth felt lighter. 

He managed to work his arm above his head, and began pulling himself through the sand until suddenly, his hand broke free into air. He gripped the top sand which burnt to the touch. He panicked clenching his fist, then pressed down again a second later only long enough that his palms wouldn't burn as he pulled himself closer to freedom. test

He shimmied like a worm until finally he could spit the sand from his mouth erupting into a gasp as he breathed in not freezing, but hot air. The light of this place blinded him. He raised his arm, pistol still in his grip, sand pouring from it's muzzle, as ge guarded his face from the rays of a setting sun. Strangely sunlight still painted the surface of his sheltered forearm before his face. He turned around to see another sun competing in the distance, he stumbled lost and confused.

Like he had just jumped into a pool, but without the pressure of fluid pressing against him. The sound felt weightless in the sense that he could not feel the percussion, it was just there, untouchable.

It was like his ears were being born into existence for the first time, hearing the first sounds he had ever encountered. There was something entirely off. Like he was no longer a part of his own body, or any body.

All he could see was white. Eventually the ringing stopped, There was no taste, smell or feeling of weight he could connect with. He was weightless, almost senseless, but he was conscious. He could still feel, but only partially, he had no breath, or pulse, the only senses he felt were those his mind could construct. He wasn’t able to panic, he was at the complete mercy of whatever this was. He embraced the silence, it was the first peaceful moment he had felt in what seemed like an eternity. In the moment nothing could harm him, direct, or alter his state, even his own will.

scene-0024.editorText:
When Tex came to, he could barely track his hands. He felt himself being reborn into his skin and thoughts as his now AI-assisted HUD lit up the ship around him. It had already tapped into his retinal wiring. Everything in his mind could read now, although his body felt cold.

He lay there, turned on his side, feeling himself awakening from what seemed like a bad dream. All he remembered was floating in the black of space, the rear of Tex's Mark IV with a recovery harpoon aimed, lockjawed. "Send my condolences to my family," he had said as he pulled the trigger. A bright light shone, blinding him. That was all he could remember; everything went blank after that.

Nonetheless, he felt safe. A strange figure seemed to appear in the distance. He floated in the regenerative tank, preparing for the lighter gravity. The reduced weight on his body brought strange thoughts or a distorted vision of a planet. John had just awoken from a dream—one of a planet with shifting surfaces. The horizon was a series of rich reds, oranges, and a dark purple silhouette that topped them, all overlooked by a transitioning bed of stars.

He suddenly found himself running, trying to keep his balance. Rolling hills, like floating bodies, came toward him, then the sound of breaking, crushing rocks overpowered him. He felt his feet being pulled down into the abyss, and then he shot back up, landing on one brace gracefully. Although he wasn't in his Mark IV suit, he had become something else. Something different, it was all coming back to him, but he couldn’t make out why it was taking him so long. He couldn’t even recognise the ship he was in. “Icarus?” He mumbled as he looked around the hardened exterior shell of the Beverly.

"We've been in a deep sleep, Captain," said Tau. Side effects are normal when you awake, just allow some time for your neural network to re-establish itself. I reccommend the piano myself personally, it will have you back to good in no time”. Tau chuckled.

“It’s fine Tau, I can recognise that chuckle a mile off, How’s Tex, he took quite a blow”, “He’s doing fine, you will see him soon enough”., “God, why does my head hurt so much”, “Tebo mentioned something to do with the ” Tau was soft in her words, with a distinct confidence. “The neural bridge when we passed through caused some delays in processing of our past. The neural bridge digs deep into hard wiring and muscle memory within the mind, re-imagining traumatic events in ways without violence”, John took a moment to absorb what Tau was telling him.

“You mean to say that Tebo has taken us all through a , that has potentially messed with our heads and reprogrammed our thinking”, “Well yes if you want to get to the bottom of it that sums it up, not to worry though, according to Tebo only some small variance, a total of 2%, the change was in you, but the others they’re not feeling anything, and Tex, well things were interesting with Tex, Tebo explained he would cover it in the debrief later”.

“Geez this is a lot to wake up to” John thought to himself as he gazed down at his what resembled his feet, in a way he admired the intricacy of the design. He had never seen pneumatic s like it before, from a generation ahead of it’s time they seemed, but not of his time, something further.”

The room door where Tau and John had been so peacefully getting reaquanted opened faster that John could feel the tinglng sensation coming back to what felt like toes attached to his extremeties. Although they weren’t, they were tools, with thousands of wired and excited connections, It was as though he had never lost his initial body, and the neural integration felt flawless.

“Ahh yes the Doctors work is always astonishes me, beholder of the eye that man” A Joyous voice of enthusiasm trickled through the room as Tebo entered. “Don’t worry about the reset John… Here, this will help”, Tebo handed John a glass of water. Although when he drank it he felt a sudden rush. He was being drawn back into his subconscious. He remembered what felt like the last 3 months in an instant. And immediately he knew what had to be done.

“Thanks Tebo.. How are we looking on the belly of the Beverly”, “Systems are running operational.. We are down about 200 rounds from the mounted Storm rail, although we can replenish that rather quickly, I intercepted an asteroid belt on the way while you were all sleeping, and with out cargo hold we can fit a couple rocks, They have already been broken down and prints of the munitions carried out, stock has been completely replenished”.

“It’s not like we will be needing them anytime soon, hopefully” said Tau. John walked over to the bridge looking out into deep space, He could see a strange planet dawning in the bridge window like a pink blossom. It’s atmosphere a beautiful dancing silhouette of purples reds pinks and on occasion the soft spec of green broke through from the planets surface. “Yes” said John, let’s take some time to pull our heads together..” John turned to face Tebo. “Thank you Tebo for this most auspicious drink. A moment alone with Lieutenant Vang”, “Don’t mind me John. I will see you on the deck for debrief in 20 minutes”, “Tebo” John interrupted once more as Tebo began to exit the room. “Yes Chief” Tebo paused in his tracks. “Thank you” John bowled to Tebo with formidable respect, Tebo met his bowl in kind “Pleasure is all mine John”.

With Tebo’s exit the bridge fell quiet once more. “Where are the others” said John. “Tex is in the medical bay with Shai undergoing limb growth therapy”. Tau seemed sad in her statement, moved by her words John tried to reassure her “Shai knows what she is doing, he will make a full recovery”, He patted her on the shoulder. “If you are sure of it I trust your call” she said. Now they were finally alone.

“She handled herself well down there” “You’ve taken a liking to her I see” Tau seemed sarcastic but withdrawn in her comment. Then she continued diggin gdeeper into John’s pshyche. “So how far back exavtly do you remember cap?”, John was silent for a moment. “I remember the beverly.. But not as she is now”, “what do you mean John, like a different configuration”, “Yeah strange I know, it’s like these memories had been hidden or something, and the  has either implanted them or they have come rushing back”, “Shai did mention there could be side effects with the jump, she really quizzed that poor little frenchman”. John seemed disturbed still like something wasn’t adding up.

 “No these are real, I can remember the control sticks, they were completely different, The ship had been fitted out for strict scientific work, Jump work specifically, which is strange, my father never had anything to do with this technology, maybe it was another department under his wing”. “That is strange, I thought the old girl was just another hauler. I mean she certainly has a kick to her. Whatever program funded her was definitely government and at the front of it’s time and hauling ass”, “Yeah and there is just something about the seats, it feels almost as if you are in the womb” John paused there was an awkward silence “Do you remember.. Anything about your mother John”.. John was quick to respond, “Yeah, I remember her quite well.. Well parts of her, she was so driven with her work I hardly got to see her through the week afternoons, she was much like my father I guess, but I remember the weekends, checking the fence lines along the orchard to make sure the horses hadn’t gotten in. You can’t see the sun like it was back then now. Too much pollution. We were fortunate to grow up in such a time” John tapped at the port  window of the med bay. A dull thudding reverberated around it’s quartz shell but nothing more, sharp to the touch of his hardened finger tips. “And soon we will be seeing the dawn of 3 stars” Tau wandered over to the port window closest to John, she slowed as she approached the window, her gaze fixed on the black side of Oasis

“It won’t be long now till we couple with the Ignotius” Tau seemed weary in her comment, like she was repressing something deep inside her. “A new Dawn” said John softly. Tau rested her heavy head on John’s shoulder, her hand gently resting on his arm, as she watched on while the dark side of the new mysterious planet slowly revealed continents unknown to man.

“Tell me more about your father…” The dim light that just seemed to creep reaching past the dark surface of the planet before them seemed to sparkle ever so gently in John’s eyes, and she felt his sorrow, as they landed like drops that crashed with nothing but stillness in a cold dead black lake. “I remember his thoroughness, the way he always directed me toward this notion that flying had deeper meaning, that we weren’t just flying for ourselves, we were flying for the people..” John paused for a moment and lifted his arm around Tau warming her gently. “Then he focused his notion toward something else, He explained that he had found a way to make us better, more than human… He stopped spending time with me in simulations, he seemed to be drifting in another mental realm to our own, He called this place Oasis, that it was like Nirvana was to the Buddhist, Jerusalem to the Christians and Muslim, although the way he described it was, that he had found a way to take the human race to another realm beyond themselves and that only through implementing this and proving it could he save us” John seemed distressed the more he recalled everything. “After that I don’t remember much, he became a shell within this Oasis. I was left to fend for the two younger sisters and rear them in a world on the brink of social collapse with imminent fall to the machines final resistance waves.” “Yeah that hit fast. I remember, total lockdown, martial law. The handover felt like a massacre” “The strange thing was I never met any of these machines, we were just shown DZ target zones, all of which were often riddled with collateral, did the Commander care, no they were deserters in his eyes, lost to the cause of a vicious opponent hell bent on destroying what was left of us”

The room door where Tau and John had been so peacefully getting reaquanted opened faster that John could feel the tinglng sensation coming back to what felt like toes attached to his extremeties. Although they weren’t, they were tools, with thousands of wired and excited connections, It was as though he had never lost his initial body, and the neural integration felt flawless.

“Ahh yes the Doctors work is always astonishes me, beholder of the eye that man” A Joyous voice of enthusiasm trickled through the room as Tebo entered. “Don’t worry about the reset John… Here, this will help”, Tebo handed John a glass of water. Although when he drank it he felt a sudden rush. He was being drawn back into his subconscious. He remembered what felt like the last 3 months in an instant. And immediately he knew what had to be done.

“Thanks Tebo.. How are we looking on the belly of the Beverly”, “Systems are running operational.. We are down about 200 rounds from the mounted Storm rail, although we can replenish that rather quickly, I intercepted an asteroid belt on the way while you were all sleeping, and with out cargo hold we can fit a couple rocks, They have already been broken down and prints of the munitions carried out, stock has been completely replenished”.

“It’s not like we will be needing them anytime soon, hopefully” said Tau. John walked over to the bridge looking out into deep space, He could see a strange planet dawning in the bridge window like a pink blossom. It’s atmosphere a beautiful dancing silhouette of purples reds pinks and on occasion the soft spec of green broke through from the planets surface. “Yes” said John, let’s take some time to pull our heads together..” John turned to face Tebo. “Thank you Tebo for this most auspicious drink. A moment alone with Lieutenant Vang”, “Don’t mind me John. I will see you on the deck for debrief in 20 minutes”, “Tebo” John interrupted once more as Tebo began to exit the room. “Yes Chief” Tebo paused in his tracks. “Thank you” John bowled to Tebo with formidable respect, Tebo met his bowl in kind “Pleasure is all mine John”.

With Tebo’s exit the bridge fell quiet once more. “Where are the others” said John. “Tex is in the medical bay with Shai undergoing limb growth therapy”. Tau seemed sad in her statement, moved by her words John tried to reassure her “Shai knows what she is doing, he will make a full recovery”, He patted her on the shoulder. “If you are sure of it I trust your call” she said. Now they were finally alone.

“She handled herself well down there” “You’ve taken a liking to her I see” Tau seemed sarcastic but withdrawn in her comment. Then she continued diggin gdeeper into John’s pshyche. “So how far back exavtly do you remember cap?”, John was silent for a moment. “I remember the beverly.. But not as she is now”, “what do you mean John, like a different configuration”, “Yeah strange I know, it’s like these memories had been hidden or something, and the  has either implanted them or they have come rushing back”, “Shai did mention there could be side effects with the jump, she really quizzed that poor little frenchman”. John seemed disturbed still like something wasn’t adding up.

“No these are real, I can remember the control sticks, they were completely different, The ship had been fitted out for strict scientific work, Jump work specifically, which is strange, my father never had anything to do with this technology, maybe it was another department under his wing”. “That is strange, I thought the old girl was just another hauler. I mean she certainly has a kick to her. Whatever program funded her was definitely government and at the front of it’s time and hauling ass”, “Yeah and there is just something about the seats, it feels almost as if you are in the womb” John paused there was an awkward silence “Do you remember.. Anything about your mother John”.. John was quick to respond, “Yeah, I remember her quite well.. Well parts of her, she was so driven with her work I hardly got to see her through the week afternoons, she was much like my father I guess, but I remember the weekends, checking the fence lines along the orchard to make sure the horses hadn’t gotten in. You can’t see the sun like it was back then now. Too much pollution. We were fortunate to grow up in such a time” John tapped at the port  window of the med bay. A dull thudding reverberated around it’s quartz shell but nothing more, sharp to the touch of his hardened finger tips. “And soon we will be seeing the dawn of 3 stars” Tau wandered over to the port window closest to John, she slowed as she approached the window, her gaze fixed on the black side of Oasis

“It won’t be long now till we couple with the Ignotius” Tau seemed weary in her comment, like she was repressing something deep inside her. “A new Dawn” said John softly. Tau rested her heavy head on John’s shoulder, her hand gently resting on his arm, as she watched on while the dark side of the new mysterious planet slowly revealed continents unknown to man.

“Tell me more about your father…” The dim light that just seemed to creep reaching past the dark surface of the planet before them seemed to sparkle ever so gently in John’s eyes, and she felt his sorrow, as they landed like drops that crashed with nothing but stillness in a cold dead black lake. “I remember his thoroughness, the way he always directed me toward this notion that flying had deeper meaning, that we weren’t just flying for ourselves, we were flying for the people..” John paused for a moment and lifted his arm around Tau warming her gently. “Then he focused his notion toward something else, He explained that he had found a way to make us better, more than human… He stopped spending time with me in simulations, he seemed to be drifting in another mental realm to our own, He called this place Oasis, that it was like Nirvana was to the Buddhist, Jerusalem to the Christians and Muslim, although the way he described it was, that he had found a way to take the human race to another realm beyond themselves and that only through implementing this and proving it could he save us” John seemed distressed the more he recalled everything. “After that I don’t remember much, he became a shell within this Oasis. I was left to fend for the two younger sisters and rear them in a world on the brink of social collapse with imminent fall to the machines final resistance waves.” “Yeah that hit fast. I remember, total lockdown, martial law. The handover felt like a massacre” “The strange thing was I never met any of these machines, we were just shown DZ target zones, all of which were often riddled with collateral, did the Commander care, no they were deserters in his eyes, lost to the cause of a vicious opponent hell bent on destroying what was left of us”

scene-0025.sceneTitle: On the bridge of the Docs Sentient flag ship
scene-0025.editorText:
John stood by Doc looking out over the strange planets horizon. The stratosphere seemed to move, deceiving new eyes into believing a concoction of gases may be stirring. Although beneath the ozone 150 klm down what moved was very real. “Oasis lives in a constant state of flux, each of it's surface plates shifting like a moving ocean, exchanging in a constant symbiosis with other plates much like cells passing by in a venous system. Each with its own eco system interacting with one another giving and taking in a never ending wheel of life.” John found it hard to fathom what he was hearing trying to piece together the biology of it all, he listened quietly in marvel as the planets surface danced a slow display from outer orbit, what ensued on the surface moved much faster. Doc could see through Johns gaze for what it was, curiosity, he obliged it.

“Initially we lost many resources on our first settlement, to be expected. New species of local fauna didn't take to fondly passing through to new structures prying and investigating finding new ways to penetrate our boundaries. You would be surprised how aware some creatures are”.

In the centre of the bridge a holograph rotated above a circular well which recessed below the Ignotus’s bridge deck fitted with countless light emitting modules. The holograph emitted a light blue grow across the room drawing any occupants to its centre as it caught their eye. John found himself turning to find the massive bulbous head of a “Spychottidal” sweeping the bridge radius pass by him. “Heightened awareness, Spychottidals are genus to mineral rich plate types 346 and 348. They have been known to venture out to other plates in search of new mineral rich environments. Their heightened sensory system can be attributed to a mineral rich diet that is used in the amplification of their sensory nodules found within their hardened bulbous neural core atop an elongated body used to burrow deep down to mineral sources” John read through the creature's description gleaning deeper into the struggles faced with the Sentient colonisation.

“Spychottidal's were able to see past our improved mesh technology, we tried neural blockers and eventually found seismic barriers could only be used in several cases. Although the shifting of the plates gave us some time to recover and learn from Interactions we had to plan our resources and work around the shifts. Our expansion at times has had its setbacks environmentally where we have had to improvise, however if we keep the balance with environmental markers we read to check our presence has minimal impact on the planet itself, this means that the symbiotic tracer we leave behind and serve to gain from the existing system flourishes” John seemed impressed by what the foresight the algorithm was capable of projecting, How something made from sheer resources pulled from within a planet itself, inorganic could bolster such a profound respect for it’s or his organic counterpart. Although he knew the amalgamation before him to be his father, He couldn’t help but feel like he was something more, an entity he had created and merged with. “”

scene-0026.editorText:
The Ignotius’s coffee machine mysterious as it was with it's seamless aesthetic integrated into the mess of the alien like ship drawing little attention to it’s users. While the novelty of a mess was completely redundant to the sentient's Doc had taken it upon himself with a foresight to design the Sentient mother-ship as a benchmark for encouraging an inter human - sentient relationship, Despite it’s current short-comings.

“Your coffee John!" the voice of the Ignatius AI system spoke with a sense of camaraderie. While it wasn't as cheerful and cute as kitten, it imbued it's guests with a sense of metallic integrity. John pressed the to his lips to the edge of his coffee cup taking his first sip. Steam danced with his nostrils warming his soul as he drank. "smells like home” he thought, then began to ponder what the universe had in store for him with respect to any sort of home moving forward.

"Good morning Cap" Shai made her way through the mess doors with a joyous stride in her step, born renewed from a good night’s sleep, her positive and cheerful self again.."I'll take a spiced Chai thanks Ignotius”. John raised his eyebrows wondering if her request was a question or a request himself, then raised his cup for another sip. “I’ve been meaning to talk to you all about something” said John, his tone soft and almost shy, not his normal confident self. It was almost like a sense of guilt shadowed his tone.

"What’s got you bothered Cap?"Shai smiled as she raised the fresh steaming Chai she had just grabbed from the coffee vending machine, as she inhaled, the aromatic spices cleared her sinuses. She smiled at John taking her first sip of Chai. John met her smile with an obliged smile, then sat quietly just appreciating how approachable she was as a person.

Tau entered the room, Tex following behind her barely fitting through the door frame to the mess. She looked at John with a subtle smile, tilting her head with camaraderie."Captain" her voice seemed less cheerful, but more professional this time as though their situation despite the quiet after what felt like a never ending storm, was still dire, and she was ready for anything at a moments notice.

Tex was still his usual self throwing a half cocked cheerful smile across the room attending to his meal with utmost importance. After all the big guy needed to eat. Except the eagerness to overpower the metallic taste left in his mouth from the nutrients fed to them in oversleep was obvious. They all felt his eagerness and respected his silence.

“You know you can eat that in more than three bites right Tex” Shai chuckled to herself. John his mood lightened by Shai’s banter let out a little smile, then drew the rooms attention this time coming back with more authority in his tone now that the others were present, yet it was strange as though he was disengaged. Like he was releasing an injured animal he had nurtured back to good health back to the wild, shooing it away. “You no longer need to call me captain.. “I am not your captain anymore”. John paused for a moment to think.

The room fell silent, Tex even stopped stuffing his face for a moment, waiting momentarily for John to keep talking, but resumed a second later slowly raising his fork loaded with curry back to his mouth, his eyes still fixed on John.

Still sipping her chai, Shai looked over to Take, then Tex, Reading the room to see if she had missed anything. "Wait a minute… what are you trying to say John?"

Tex joined in “Yeah big guy, you aren’t getting cold feet on us are you” He said with a hint of sarcasm, he pushed out his chair looking directly at John’s metallic shins. He thought himself clever for a moment.

John took in a deep breath. “Look… None of you would be in this situation if  hadn’t stepped into that dam pod”. John expressed his message with an intensity in his eyes, his palms open on the table, his coffee sat half full getting colder.

Tex started eating again. “What I’m trying to say is I am no longer your captain, you aren’t bound to me under any protectant law.. There is no council to call on you here, No Court Marshal, you are all free to make lives for yourselves as you please on oasis”. John paused for a moment, it was as though he couldn’t really believe what he was about to propose himself, “or return if you like”. Tau leant into the centre of the table concern stricken brows and deep brown eyes veering into John’s soul. “Return?” said Tau. “Yes” said John, “I have already spoken to Doc and he is happy to arrange safe passage and negotiation terms to have you all reinstated, although”. Tex laughed almost choking on the gristly curried beef chunk he’d been chewing on now these past minutes.

“Fuck that guy, the only instating I’ll be doing is instating my as a permanent  fixture in his ass”. Tex paused cooling off for a moment as the room fell silent in agreeance with him then started back up again as his face turned once again to frustration. “I mean.. Where the fuck have you been? Did you not see the barrage of missiles & rail slugs he hurled at us? He wants us dead, to cover up his own fucking mess”, Tau was still, emotionless sitting up straight staring into space in the middle of the table, but she seemed calculated despite Tex’s apparent frustration “He wants control, Tex is right, we took that from him” said Tau “It isn’t a matter of cleaning up a mess” Said John

 “The worker bot project was a complete success in the eyes of the Engineer that created them, Just not Marcellus” John couldn’t allow minor details to poison the view of what he had grown to trust and now become a part of. He had seen the world from behind the Sentient eyes, seen them lay themselves down when they could have so easily taken over, He had seen how effective they had become in leading through virtue and not destruction.

“We are part of something much bigger than ourselves now” John continued. “Marcellus wants control, and if anyone has seen what really went on down there, which I have, He can’t have that information getting out and appealing to the ethics of others.”  John concluded. “So no Tex, I didn’t miss the barrage of rail gun fire pointed right at us. I’m the one that’s compromised, I’m the one Marcellus wants”

Tau intervened “We’ve all seen what went on down there, we’ve all seen too much, it doesn’t matter what we are at this stage it’s what we know, There’s no way Marcellus will just let that fly … ”

Tau veered toward John her face was pure disbelief, she didn’t believe for a moment what John was saying was possible. “According to Doc, a full memory wipe of the events as they occurred is possible and scans can show, It will be like it never happened” John was convincing in his soft yet concise tone. But the room stirred still Tex sat disgruntled in the corner devouring his meal in what seemed like a contained focus, different to what Tex would normally do forking an assault on the steaming curry lab grown beef that somehow put up a fight with a genetically grown layers of fat.

Tex still wasn’t convinced “Who the hell even is this guy Doc and why do you trust him so much”. John paused, taking in a deep breath to prepare himself for what he was about to tell his closest friends, in reality the only organic family he had left. He prepared He preparing himself for the insanity of it all, imagining how he came to accept it, in all his optimism and how in Sol these few before him with all their known imperfections would take being told that his own biological father is a live walking breathing talking amalgamation of technology.

“They won’t believe me, you’ve been dead almost 50 years” John thought to himself. Although he wasn’t the only one listening. “They don’t need to believe it, they only need to see it with their own eyes”. In that moment John felt chills moving down his spine. “Get out of my hea…” He thought, but what he was thinking wasn’t just thought it was very real.

scene-0027.editorText:
The metallic clang of a transport pod coupling with the airlock bay shattered the mess's still silent hum. The sound reverberated through the hull of the Ignotius, dissipating as soon as they had arrived. Ripples atop John’s lifeless coffee faded away.

“The doctors’ transport pod” Kitten announced breaking the silence. “he just arrived from his station on the surface”.

John’s senses sharpened. Across the table, Tex stopped spinning his fork, setting it down beside his spotless plate, which he’d meticulously licked clean. Footsteps echoed from the corridor—familiar in a way that tugged at a buried memory within John. His pulse quickened. He had heard those footsteps before, in a dream, just before the briefing on the lost facility. But this time, there were two sets: one heavy, deliberate, and the other lighter, more cautious.

The Ignotius drifted in the void like a giant squid, silent, as the crew exchanged uneasy glances, waiting for what was to come.

“Doctor.. are these the Protectant you spoke of”, The confused stares of John and his team dissipated as another sentient companion Doc into the room. However, something about this Sentient was different. Tex could only just put his finger on it. “Is it just me or does this thing actually have hips?” He thought to himself.

“I have prepared an overview of the drilling superstructure embedded beneath the ice on Europa” Serra stepped forward emerging from the bulkheads behind Wolfgang, her shoulder sat proudly next to the Doctors, and eyed Tex directly with a soft conservative smile.

"Serra designed the facility herself: She ... was a board member on the Europa exploration team. head architect." The Doctor gave praise in his statement. "We worked together to test the viability of the worker bots in the high radiation of Europa's surface." Serra stepped forward she could tell Tex was the most uncomfortable about her sudden emergence into the room, although she put it down to sexual tension internally, he was just shy and she saw straight through it. "As well as pressure testing for the depth. My role was crucial in designing the hyperbaric chambers in a way that could convert the hydrogen to cells for the worker bot program” The Doctor announced “Nova was extraordinary in her field!” with a tone of excitement, that filled Tau with joy, Tau really liked her, and you could see it in the way she rested a keen eye across her visor flickering with eagerness as she spoke.

To Shai Serra invoked a sense of a lost kindred mother, hidden beneath the wires. She found it hard to fathom the kind of knowledge she would have accessed this past 150 years. Shai leant over to Tau perching respectfully behind her ear and in an instant whispered softly “I like this one”. Tau met her comment with a smile, Shai immediately spotted her dimples and met with a cute contained giggle.

“I am sure you and Shai will get along just fine”, Doc drew his attention from Serra to Shai, gesturing at Shai with his human like hand. “Shai is our Deep Space Medic Technician, if something goes wrong medically work with her in any extractions that may occur”. Serra’s template emoted what looked akin to a smile. “You must update me on the progress of the genetic tree printing bio-gel after this briefing Shai, I would be interested in your abstract around Neural flexibility in this new field”. Tex raised his eyebrows, with a slightly impressed tone but shying on impatience. “I am sure you will have plenty of time to get acquitted after the mission brief”. John gently redirected the attention of the room while nodding respectfully at the Doctor.

From behind the Doctor

"Serra designed the facility herself: She ... was a board member on the Europa exploration team. head architect." The Doctor gave praise in his statement. "We worked together to test the viability of the worker bots in the high radiation of Europa's surface." Serra stepped forward she could tell Tex was the most uncomfortable about her sudden emergence into the room, although she put it down to sexual tension internally, he was just shy and she saw straight through it. "As well as pressure testing for the depth. My role was crucial in designing the hyperbaric chambers in a way that could convert the hydrogen to cells for the worker bot program” The Doctor announced “Nova was extraordinary in her field!” with a tone of excitement, that filled Tau with joy, Tau really liked her, and you could see it in the way she rested a keen eye across her visor flickering with eagerness as she spoke.

To Shai Serra invoked a sense of a lost kindred mother, hidden beneath the wires. She found it hard to fathom the kind of knowledge she would have accessed this past 150 years. Shai leant over to Tau perching respectfully behind her ear and in an instant whispered softly “I like this one”. Tau met her comment with a smile, Shai immediately spotted her dimples and met with a cute contained giggle.

“I am sure you and Shai will get along just fine”, Doc drew his attention from Serra to Shai, gesturing at Shai with his human like hand. “Shai is our Deep Space Medic Technician, if something goes wrong medically work with her in any extractions that may occur”. Serra’s template emoted what looked akin to a smile. “You must update me on the progress of the genetic tree printing bio-gel after this briefing Shai, I would be interested in your abstract around Neural flexibility in this new field”. Tex raised his eyebrows, with a slightly impressed tone but shying on impatience. “I am sure you will have plenty of time to get acquitted after the mission brief”. John gently redirected the attention of the room while nodding respectfully at the Doctor.
From behind the Doctor

scene-0028.editorText:
The door to the mess slid open with a soft hiss, retracting into the hull. The tension in the room thickened. Then, as if on cue, confusion followed awe when a tall, unfamiliar figure stepped through the threshold. The figure’s strange, organic appearance defied everything they had expected. It stood still, its shoulders angled toward John as though it recognised him intimately. But it was unlike anything created by man—a being that seemed to have evolved from something beyond human science.

With a grace that belied its alien form, it bowed its head toward John, the gesture carrying an eerie sense of recognition—like an echo from a distant past.

John rose from his chair to address the figure, but the sudden shift in the ship’s thrust gravity—caused by the uncoupling of the Doctor’s transport pod—sent his balance faltering. His attempt to stand with respect felt disjointed, as scattered as his thoughts had been at the figure’s arrival.

"Looks like he’s planning to stay for a while," Kitten murmured softly to John, her voice almost lost in the subtle hum of the ship.

Through the port window, the Doctor’s pod could be seen drifting back toward the planet’s surface. The atmosphere seemed to wrap around it, pulling it deeper into a blue silhouette until it was swallowed entirely by the distant horizon. The room was awkwardly quiet, as John waited for their new acquaintance to address the room. Yet the voice that spoke up was not that of a male but of a female.

  Nova, It’s me, Doc,”  Said the alien as it looked over in John’s direction once more. “My Son..” The words eased out gently but heavy with history from the being vocal glands. It didn’t have a mouth as such but emitted sound-like vibrations, just as though spoken from a tongue.

Tex’s eyes darted around the room. First to Shai, then Tau then back to John resting once more on the strange alien standing before them. “Well, I’m sorry” Tex proclaimed sarcastically, “ Am I the only one failing to see the fucking resemblance here. Am I missing something?”

“I apologise for the Doctor’s impromptu arrival in his..derived form”. The sentient’s voice eased the lying tension commanding the room as she stood gently beside the Doctor. Tex shied away from the sound of this new sentient’s voice but found it strangely comforting. It was something in the machine’s voice. She or it’s voice, Tex corrected himself to maintain some order with his internal conflict of the rapidly evolving world before him, had reminded him of his long passed sister, who had been lost in the 3rd war.

The strange figure before them looked nothing like the Sentient’s anatomy on the surface, its shape a distant echo perhaps. But this was something more, sophisticated, organic. Shockingly unfamiliar, and so, grotesque, it threw the entire room into shock. “Don’t let my appearance startle you, My primitive sentient body is undergoing some.. Alterations for our next mission, as surprisingly versatile and resilient it is to extreme conditions as our Engineers intended them, I expect we may encounter some, Extraordinary circumstances on Oasis, and so preparations were in order.” John’s face was riddled still with confusion, trying to find sense in what was happening averting his gaze from the constant directed eyes upon him.

“What have you got us into” they said, he could hear their thoughts, but he persisted, fixing his eyes on the mess table, his chin resting as he perched his arm in his elbows cradle “You’re.. A figure of your imagination” John knew what he said made no sense, “You, re-invented your biology to capitalise on the atmospheric make-up of Oasis”. He had never seen the alien standing before them, yet he recognised the speech patterns, it was his father. But he couldn’t piece the alien before him with his father’s youthful face as he remembered it. Is this what his father had become?

"I am simply an evolved version of my prior model," it continued, voice steady. "We had to make adjustments to better adapt to Oasis's ever-changing environment."

As the Doctor spoke, faint blue and green hues danced along its temples, pulsing with emotion—an attempt, it seemed, to mimic sentience, though it was clearly more advanced. Its movements were fluid, more organic than the previous sentient designs.

The creature's outer shell gleamed faintly under the lights, resembling a crustacean that had evolved into a humanoid form. Ports replaced where lungs might have been, housing what appeared to be fuel cells. Its skin had a matte sheen, hard and protective, guarding what lay beneath. Its chest didn’t rise or fall like a human’s but instead emitted a soft hum as it moved through the room.
